papers.title: Habitual Diet, Gut Microbiome Dysbiosis, and α-Synucleinopathy Conversion in Isolated Rapid Eye Movement (REM) Sleep Behavior Disorder.
papers.abstract: Accumulating evidence indicates that habitual diet, including plant-based dietary patterns, is associated with neurodegenerative α-synucleinopathy risk. However, the role of diet and its correlation with the gut microbiome in prodromal α-synucleinopathy, specifically among patients with isolated rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder (iRBD), remains unclear. To evaluate dietary patterns, their interplay with gut microbial dysbiosis, and longitudinal effects on neurodegenerative progression in iRBD patients. We recruited 287 iRBD patients and 208 age- and sex-matched controls. Plant-based diet indices (PDIs) were derived from food frequency questionnaires. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed in 456 subjects for diet-microbiome analyses. After a median follow-up of 4.2 years, 45 (15.7%) iRBD patients converted to α-synucleinopathies. Cox proportional hazards models assessed the associations between diet and neurodegenerative outcomes. We found that iRBD patients exhibited lower healthful PDIs (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 95% confidence interval [95% CI]: 0.48 [0.29-0.80], P = 0.005) but higher consumption of unhealthful plant-based foods (refined grains, sweets, and sweeteners). Diet-microbiome interaction analysis identified dietary associations for 84.3% of iRBD-related gut microbes, including co-occurrence between healthful PDI and Clostridium sp. AF20-17LB. Longitudinally, four dietary factors and five iRBD-related microbes were associated with neurodegenerative outcomes; specifically, higher coffee consumption was linked to a lower risk of progression to α-synucleinopathy (aHR [95% CI]: 0.30 [0.11-0.78], P = 0.01). Furthermore, mediation analyses indicated that the iRBD-enriched species Ruthenibacterium lactatiformans mediated the association between unhealthful PDI and dementia-first conversion. Habitual diet in iRBD is associated with gut microbiome dysbiosis and predicts neurodegenerative progression. These findings highlight diet-microbiome interactions as modifiable targets for intervention in prodromal α-synucleinopathy. © 2026 The Author(s). papers.title: Molecular clockwork hypothesis for the KaiABC circadian oscillations.
papers.abstract: When three cyanobacterial proteins-KaiA, KaiB, and KaiC-are incubated with ATP in vitro, the phosphorylation level of KaiC exhibits stable circadian oscillations. Biochemical and structural analyses have shown that KaiC's ATPase activity is crucial for these oscillations, leading to the hypothesis that ATP-consuming dynamics function as a molecular clock, determining the oscillation period of individual molecules. Moreover, these molecular clocks synchronize collectively, resulting in oscillations at the ensemble level. In this study, we develop a theoretical model to test this molecular clockwork hypothesis. Our model clarifies the relationship between the oscillation period and ATPase activity, explaining the significant changes in the period induced by amino acid substitutions near the CI-CII domain boundary of the KaiC hexamer. Furthermore, the model addresses the physical basis for temperature compensation concerning both the oscillation period and ATPase activity. Thus, the molecular clockwork perspective provides a framework for understanding the atomic design behind collective oscillations.

papers.title: Frequency extraction from invariant flows.
papers.abstract: In nondegenerate integrable Hamiltonian systems, invariant tori can be parametrized by action variables or fundamental frequencies. We introduce an invariant-flow formulation, consistent with the Liouville-Arnold geometry, for extracting these frequencies. Treating invariants as generators of commuting Hamiltonian flows yields the frequencies from time-of-flight parameters, providing a direct alternative to action-angle constructions and long-time spectral analysis. The resulting numerical procedure extends naturally to multiple degrees of freedom and achieves high accuracy for the McMillan map. More broadly, the framework provides an invariant-centered view of near-integrable dynamics, recovering frequencies and other dynamical information from high-quality approximate invariants.

papers.title: Multivariate stochastic coupling in unknown complex systems: Informative randomness in deterministic brain-body communication.
papers.abstract: Physiological systems exhibit deterministic behavior influenced by dynamic stochasticity, where informative random components play a crucial role in complex system interactions. Fully characterizing multivariate random components is challenging when the underlying deterministic dynamics are unknown. We propose a framework for estimating stochastic coupling in unknown deterministic systems influenced by dynamic noise. Building on a multivariate extension of approximate entropy (MApEn), the proposed framework exploits the divergence of this metric in the presence of dynamical noise. After establishing the theoretical basis and validity of the method, which can accommodate arbitrary multivariate noise probability distributions, we show that, in the case of bivariate white Gaussian noise, the framework enables closed-form estimation of the noise covariance matrix without requiring prior knowledge of the underlying deterministic functions. To this end, we introduce an iterative algorithm to estimate the covariance matrix coefficients. The algorithm identifies the parameter values that rescale the differential behavior of multivariate MApEn along a target curve. We validate the framework using both synthetic datasets and real physiological recordings. The analysis reveals important insights into brain-heart interactions, particularly the modulation of stochastic coupling across sleep-stage transitions through low-frequency oscillatory activity. Our results indicate that conscious wakefulness is characterized by stronger stochastic coupling, which progressively decreases during the transition to sleep. This framework opens new avenues for investigating stochastic physiological dynamics and their associated networks, with potential applications across a wide range of scientific disciplines.

papers.title: GPU-accelerated sequential Monte Carlo for Bayesian spectral analysis.
papers.abstract: Bayesian spectral deconvolution provides a data-driven framework for mathematical model selection and parameter estimation from spectral data. Although highly versatile, its computational cost grows with the number of model parameters, data points, and candidate models, often rendering practical applications infeasible. We propose a GPU-accelerated approach in which a sequential Monte Carlo sampler (SMCS) is executed in parallel on a GPU to perform Bayesian model selection for the number of spectral peaks and Bayesian estimation of peak-function parameters. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the GPU-parallelized SMCS reaches the free-energy accuracy of an optimized CPU-parallelized replica exchange Monte Carlo (REMC) baseline up to approximately 37× faster-with smaller gains, down to near parity, in the least favorable settings-and is faster than GPU-parallelized REMC in many of the tested cases. The method is validated on artificial data designed to emulate x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and x-ray diffraction measurements, as well as on real experimental spectra. As measurement techniques such as microscopic spectroscopy and in situ methods continue to drive rapid growth in the volume of spectral data, the proposed approach offers a practical computational foundation for advanced analysis of each individual dataset.

papers.title: The characteristics of depression and sleep among Chinese high school students: A cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Mental health and sleep problems are among the most significant burdens of illnesses for adolescents in China. This study aimed to investigate the characteristics of depression and sleep quality among high school students and compare sleep quality across students with varying levels of depression. A cross-sectional study was performed to collect data on depression and sleep quality using a paper questionnaire including a self-rating depression scale (SDS) and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Among all the 537 high school students, 57.0% (306 participants) experienced depression and 47.5% (255 participants) suffered from poor sleep quality. Males showed significantly greater SDS scores than females (55.2 ± 7.2 vs 53.8 ± 6.8, P = .027). Significantly greater PSQI score in high school students with moderate-to-severe depression than those with mild depression and nondepression (5.2 ± 2.7 vs 5.3 ± 2.4 vs 6.2 ± 2.3, F = 3.5, P = .032). In contrast, an adjusted logistic regression model indicated that depression severity was not an independent significant predictor of poor sleep quality after adjusting for age, sex, and BMI (all P > .05). Overall, high school students exhibited a high prevalence of depression and poor sleep quality, with those experiencing moderate-to-severe depression showing the poorest sleep quality in unadjusted comparisons. However, depression severity did not remain an independent significant predictor of poor sleep quality after adjustment. Depression and sleep problems among high school students should receive greater attention, particularly for high school students with moderate-to-severe depression.

papers.title: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation for the treatment of restless legs syndrome: A meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: The benefit of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in patients with Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS) is uncertain. This study was performed to explore the therapeutic effect of rTMS in treating RLS. Databases including PubMed, EMbase, the Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang database were searched from their inception to May 1, 2026. Eligible studies comparing rTMS with sham stimulation were included. Data were analyzed using Review Manager Version 5.3. Four studies were included in the meta-analysis. The overall pooled analysis confirmed that rTMS could effectively reduce International RLS-Rating Scale (IRLS-RS) scores (mean difference [MD] = 6.46, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 4.44 -8.48, P < .00001) and Pittsburgh sleep quality index (PSQI) scores (MD = 4.80, 95% CI: 3.51-6.08, P < .00001) at different follow-up periods. Meanwhile, the overall pooled analysis confirmed that rTMS could effectively reduce IRLS-RS scores (MD = 7.79, 95% CI: 3.90-11.68, P < .0001) and PSQI scores (MD = 5.58, 95% CI: 3.81-7.35, P < .00001) in the subgroup analysis by RLS subtype. However, rTMS showed no significant effect on PSQI scores in primary RLS (MD = 1.86, 95% CI: -2.65-6.37, P = .42). In addition, the overall pooled analysis confirmed that both low-frequency and high-frequency rTMS could effectively reduce IRLS-RS scores (MD = 7.79, 95% CI: 3.90-11.68, P < .0001) and PSQI scores (MD = 5.58, 95% CI: 3.81-7.35, P < .00001). Finally, the overall pooled analysis confirmed that rTMS could not significantly reduce Hamilton anxiety scale and Hamilton depression scale scores in subgroup analyses of follow-up period, RLS subtype, or rTMS frequency (P > .05). rTMS might alleviate core limb discomfort symptoms measured by IRLS-RS and improve sleep quality assessed by PSQI in patients with RLS. However, rTMS might not be effective in improving symptoms of anxiety and depression. To further confirm the conclusion, more large randomized controlled trials are necessary.

papers.title: Numerical investigation of the impact of neural stem cells on brain tumors.
papers.abstract: Malignant brain tumors, including glioblastoma and medulloblastoma, remain highly treatment-resistant. Neural stem cells (NSCs) are being investigated as tumor-tropic therapeutic vectors, but the temporal interaction between tumor and NSC populations requires quantitative characterization before model-based treatment hypotheses can be interpreted reliably. This study aimed to develop and numerically evaluate a reproducible 2-population model of tumor-NSC dynamics and to quantify the influence of NSC persistence and NSC-mediated tumor killing on simulated tumor burden. A normalized system of 2 coupled nonlinear ordinary differential equations was used: dT/dt = rT(1 - T) - βTN and dN/dt = αN(1 - N) - γTN. The baseline simulation used r = 0.20000 day-1, α = 0.05000 day-1, β = 0.35000 day-1, γ = 0.30000 day-1, T0 = 0.50000, and N0 = 0.40000. Explicit Euler integration was performed with Δt = 0.01 day over 20 days. A descriptive nonlinear regression fit, Fourier spectral analysis, 1-parameter sensitivity analyses, and joint α-β sensitivity analysis were applied to the simulated trajectory. In the baseline simulation, tumor density decreased from 0.5000 to a minimum of 0.4772 at day 2.59 (4.57% below the initial value) and subsequently increased to T20 = 0.8273, while NSC density declined from 0.4000 to N20 = 0.0247. The descriptive regression reproduced the simulated tumor trajectory with R2 = 0.9973 and root mean square error = 0.00590. Increasing α from 0.05 to 0.10 day-1 reduced T20 by 12.6% relative to baseline, and increasing β from 0.35 to 0.50 day-1 reduced T20 by 19.9%. Jointly setting α = 0.10 and β = 0.50 day-1 yielded T20 = 0.4427, 46.5% below the baseline terminal tumor density. The Fourier spectrum was dominated by the zero and low-frequency components, with no distinct oscillatory peak over the 20-day window. The model indicates that NSC persistence and NSC-mediated tumor killing materially influence terminal tumor burden, but the baseline parameterization produces only transient early suppression followed by tumor regrowth as the NSC population declines. The results are population-level, model-based estimates rather than tumor-type-specific clinical efficacy measures. Tumour-specific calibration, spatial migration, immune interactions, and experimental validation are required before translational conclusions can be drawn.

papers.title: Gut microbiota, sleep and coronary artery disease: A Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: Inadequate and poor-quality sleep is increasingly recognized as a risk factor for coronary artery disease (CAD). Gut microbiota may play a role in sleep regulation. However, the associations between gut microbiota, sleep, and CAD risk, and the causal nature of these associations, remain unclear. We performed a 2-step Mendelian randomization analysis using summary-level data to assess the association between gut microbiota and CAD and the potential mediating roles of sleep-related traits (i.e., chronotype, insomnia, sleep duration, short sleep, and long sleep) herein. The inverse-variance weighted method served as the primary analysis, with several other complementary methods as sensitivity analyses. Our findings revealed that 2 gut microbial taxa were negatively associated with genetically predicted CAD risk, while 4 taxa, including species Veillonella unclassified (odds ratio: 1.054, 95% confidence interval: 1.010-1.101), showed positive associations. Regarding sleep-related traits, we found that insomnia (odds ratio: 1.553, 95% confidence interval: 1.081-2.230) and short sleep duration causally increased CAD risk, whereas longer sleep duration causally reduced CAD risk. The mediation Mendelian randomization analysis demonstrated that insomnia partially mediated the causal, predisposing effect of species Veillonella unclassified on increased CAD risk, with a proportion mediated of 5.7%. This study provides evidence for a causal relationship between specific gut microbial taxa and CAD risk, as well as the mediating role of insomnia in this relationship. These findings offer novel insights into potential strategies for CAD prevention through modulation of the gut microbiome and improvement of sleep quality.

papers.title: The effects of multiregional fascial mobilization on heart rate and physiological parameters in patients with obstructive sleep apnea: A randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with increased sympathetic activity and an elevated cardiovascular risk. Noninvasive interventions targeting autonomic regulation may offer complementary therapeutic strategies. This randomized controlled trial aimed to investigate the acute effects of multiregional fascial mobilization on the physiological parameters of patients with OSA. Patients with polysomnography-confirmed moderate-to-severe OSA (apnea-hypopnea index ≥ 15 events/hour) were randomly assigned to an intervention group that received a standardized 16-minute multiregional fascial mobilization protocol or a control group that rested quietly in the supine position for the corresponding period without receiving manual or tactile intervention. The intervention targeted the cervical, thoracic, and abdominal regions, under controlled conditions. The primary outcomes included heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, and peripheral oxygen saturation. Measurements were obtained at baseline, immediately post-intervention, and 5 and 15 minutes post-intervention. A total of 95 male patients (mean age: 48.12 ± 10.21 years) completed the study. Baseline characteristics were comparable between the groups, except for heart rate. After adjustment for baseline heart rate using mixed analysis of covariance, no significant group × time interaction was observed for heart rate (P = .476, partial ηp2 = .008). Similarly, no significant group × time interactions were observed for systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, or peripheral oxygen saturation (all P > .05). Although significant time effects were observed for some physiological parameters, the magnitude of these effects varied across outcomes, and none was accompanied by a significant group × time interaction. Therefore, these temporal changes were not interpreted as intervention-specific effects. No adverse events were reported. Heart rate changed significantly over time following the interventions; however, after adjustment for baseline heart rate, the pattern of change did not differ significantly between the fascial mobilization and control groups. Similarly, no significant between-group differences in changes over time were observed for blood pressure or oxygen saturation. These findings do not demonstrate a specific acute effect of multiregional fascial mobilization on the physiological parameters assessed. Further studies using advanced measures of autonomic function and longer follow-up periods are warranted.

papers.title: A cross-sectional study on the relationship between hepatitis C virus infection and the risk of sleep disorders among adults based on NHANES data from 2017 to 2020: A cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Patients with hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection often report sleep‑related complaints, but the relationship between HCV and clinically significant sleep disturbances remains poorly defined. This cross‑sectional study aimed to explore whether HCV infection is associated with an increased risk of sleep disorder among adults. Data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2017 to 2020 were analyzed. HCV infection status and sleep disorder were assessed using standardized questionnaires. Covariates including gender, age, race, marital status, alcohol use, body mass index, diabetes status, cancer history, and smoking status were adjusted in the analysis. A total of 7924 participants aged 20 to 80 years were enrolled, of whom 2310 had sleep disorder. The prevalence of HCV infection was significantly higher in participants with sleep disorder. After adjustment for potential confounders by multivariable logistic regression, HCV infection was independently associated with an increased risk of sleep disorder (odds ratio = 2.08; 95% confidence interval = 1.37-3.15; P < .05). HCV infection is significantly associated with an elevated risk of sleep disorder in adults. HCV screening among patients with sleep complaints may facilitate comprehensive clinical management.

papers.title: Individualized multimodal pain management for chronic perineal pain: A case report.
papers.abstract: Persistent perineal pain is a challenging clinical condition that may substantially impair sleep, urination, daily activities, and psychological well-being. Accurate assessment and individualized multimodal management are essential for improving symptom control and patient participation in care. A 68-year-old woman presented with chronic perineal pain and tenderness that had persisted for 3 years. The pain significantly interfered with her sleep, urination, and daily activities. Clinical assessment suggested chronic perineal pain with neuropathic involvement of the pudendal nerve and lumbosacral or sacral nerve roots. The diagnosis was established based on the patient's clinical manifestations, physical examination findings, and comprehensive evaluation. The patient received a multimodal pain management approach, including oral pregabalin, computed tomography-guided sacral canal catheterization with targeted nerve-root adhesiolysis and ozone injection, continuous pain assessment, psychological support, pelvic floor muscle training, and individualized rehabilitation guidance. At the two-week follow-up, the visual analog scale score decreased from 8/10 to 3/10, and the pain no longer interfered with sleep. Approximately 3 weeks after discharge, the pain temporarily increased to 5/10 and subsequently stabilized at 4/10 at the one-month follow-up while the patient continued oral pregabalin. Individualized multimodal pain management may effectively reduce pain intensity and improve sleep and daily functioning in patients with persistent perineal pain. Continuous assessment, patient participation, psychological support, and rehabilitation strategies are important components of comprehensive pain management.

papers.title: The bidirectional causal relationships of insomnia with eleven cancers: A Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is closely associated with tumors and is recognized as a risk factor for cancer development. This two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study investigated the potential causal link between genetically determined insomnia and various cancers, including brain, colorectal, esophageal, gastric, hepatic bile duct, liver, lung, malignant lymphoma, pancreatic, skin, and thyroid cancers. Summary statistics from genome-wide association studies for insomnia and eleven cancer types were examined. instrumental variables (IVs) were selected from single nucleotide polymorphisms that passed strict quality control for minimal linkage disequilibrium and genome-wide significance. All IVs demonstrated strong predictive power for insomnia, with F-statistics exceeding the conventional threshold of 10. The primary analysis was conducted using the inverse variance weighted method. Sensitivity analyses were performed using MR-Egger regression, weighted median, and weighted mode methods to test robustness, pleiotropy, and heterogeneity. MR analysis suggested potential causal associations between insomnia and increased risk of hepatic bile duct cancer (odds ratio [OR] = 4.458, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.074-18.493, P = .040), reduced risk of hepatic cancer (OR = 0.312, 95% CI: 0.100-0.973, P = .045), and reduced risk of skin cancers (OR = 0.599, 95% CI: 0.439-0.818, P = .001). However, after Bonferroni correction (adjusted threshold P < .0045), these associations did not retain statistical significance. No notable causal influence of these cancers on insomnia was observed. Sensitivity analyses showed no evidence of reverse causality or significant bias. These findings, though not retaining statistical significance after stringent multiple testing correction, provide suggestive evidence that genetically predicted insomnia may influence the risk of certain cancers, potentially through mechanisms involving genetic predisposition and biological pathways that modulate inflammation, immune function, and circadian rhythms. The study highlights the translational value of understanding insomnia's role in cancer risk, suggesting that clinicians should consider this association when managing patients with insomnia. Further research with larger sample sizes is warranted to validate these findings.

papers.title: Is cardiovascular autonomic control during the day-to-night transition dependent on dim light melatonin onset? An exploratory analysis in healthy adults.
papers.abstract: We tested whether dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO) is time-aligned with the transition between biological day into night in cardiovascular autonomic control (CV onset time). We studied 10 healthy adults (4 females, age 25 ± SD 2 years) under an ultra-short semi-constant routine protocol (<8lux). Participants remained seated for 7 h until 1 h after their habitual bedtime. We collected saliva samples every 30 min and recorded R-R intervals and beat-to-beat blood pressure every hour. DLMO was defined as the interpolated time for melatonin increase over 3 pg/mL. Phase angle was defined as the time difference between DLMO and the midpoint of self-reported sleep as a measure of the alignment between sleep-wake patterns and biological circadian rhythms. CV onset time was defined using a segmental (piecewise) analysis to identify the inflection point (X0 slope) throughout the study. CV autonomic modulation was assessed using indices of heart rate and blood pressure variability. CV onset times for all indices did not differ significantly from DLMO (p > 0.05). Mean differences between DLMO and CV onset time were significantly correlated with the phase angle of entrainment (all significant, r > +0.75). Our results suggest that CV autonomic transition into biological night was not associated with DLMO, which seems to depend on the phase angle of entrainment.

papers.title: Abdominal Tics in Children and Adolescents: A Phenomenology-First Diagnostic Framework and Differential Diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Abdominal tics are a less commonly described axial or tonic tic phenotype in children and adolescents with Tourette syndrome and chronic tic disorders. Their abdominal location and symptom language may create diagnostic uncertainty with gastrointestinal, epileptic, myoclonic, respiratory or functional presentations. This clinically focused narrative synthesis identified relevant literature through targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science from database inception through March 2026, supplemented by a targeted PubMed/MEDLINE and citation-chasing update during revision through August 2026 focused on focal abdominal motor seizures, CASPR2-associated movement phenomena, peripheral nerve hyperexcitability and related mimics. Abdominal tics are supported by the same core tic features that apply across body regions: premonitory urge, partial suppressibility, stereotyped recurrence, waxing-and-waning course, sleep attenuation and prior or concurrent tics when present. Key neurological mimics include belly dancer's dyskinesia, propriospinal myoclonus, focal abdominal motor seizures, CASPR2-associated abdominal movement disorders and functional tic-like behaviours. Preserved awareness does not exclude a focal motor seizure. Gastrointestinal mimics include disorders of gut-brain interaction and inflammatory bowel disease. A pattern-directed clinical triage algorithm is proposed alongside management principles derived from established paediatric tic-disorder evidence, including behavioural intervention as first-line treatment and comorbidity-guided pharmacotherapy. A phenomenology-first, red-flag-guided approach can improve diagnostic clarity and help clinicians avoid both reflexive investigation and premature attribution of organic disease to tics. This review provides a practical clinical triage framework for determining when an abdominal movement behaves like a tic, when targeted neurological or gastrointestinal investigation is indicated and when management can follow established tic-disorder principles.
papers.journal: Journal of paediatrics and child health

papers.title: Seizures Secondary to Aconitum Plant Poisoning: a case report.
papers.abstract: Aconitum plant poisoning typically manifests as isolated early cardiotoxicity or late neurotoxicity. However, the dynamic temporal evolution from arrhythmia-driven cardiogenic syncope to true epileptic seizures mediated by direct central nervous system injury remains rarely documented and poorly characterized. We report a 53-year-old Han Chinese male who presented with ventricular tachycardia rapidly degenerating into ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest following ingestion of homemade Aconitum kusnezoffii (caowu)-infused liquor. Initial convulsions were tightly coupled with malignant arrhythmias, consistent with cardiogenic syncope. After successful resuscitation, hemoperfusion, and restoration of stable sinus rhythm, the patient developed breakthrough generalized tonic-clonic seizures on hospital days 4-6. Electroencephalography performed during sedation withdrawal revealed bilateral occipital spike-and-slow and sharp-and-slow waves with focal epileptiform discharges, confirming direct central nervous system neurotoxicity rather than recurrent cardiac ischemia. A mechanism-based, staged treatment strategy was employed: early advanced cardiac life support and hemoperfusion targeted cardiotoxicity, while sodium valproate and acetylglutamine were administered for antiepileptic prophylaxis and neuroprotection. The patient was discharged on day 13; antiepileptic therapy was successfully tapered and discontinued at 3 months without seizure recurrence, with normalization of electroencephalography and electrocardiography. This case provides the first systematic documentation, validated by electroencephalography, of the transition from cardiogenic convulsions to true epileptic seizures in Aconitum alkaloid poisoning. The findings highlight the critical role of pharmacokinetic-driven central nervous system retention in delayed seizure onset and underscore the necessity of prolonged neurological monitoring, early electroencephalography evaluation for late-onset convulsions, and sustained antiepileptic prophylaxis to reduce mortality and long-term neurological sequelae. Aconitum plant poisoning may manifest as early cardiogenic syncope and convulsions secondary to malignant arrhythmias, progressing in the late stage to genuine seizures caused by central nervous system (CNS) injury. Effective management requires a staged treatment strategy targeting both cardiotoxicity and neurotoxicity, with a focus on stabilizing cardiac rhythm and providing neuroprotection as needed.

papers.title: Qualitative Exit Interviews to Characterize the Positive Treatment Experiences of Patients in the Phase III Trial of Orforglipron Versus Oral Semaglutide for the Treatment of Type 2 Diabetes.
papers.abstract: There is an unmet need for effective and well-tolerated oral formulations of glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists for the management of type 2 diabetes. Orforglipron and oral semaglutide are two oral glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists evaluated in the ACHIEVE-3 clinical trial (NCT06045221). These novel treatments have the means to achieve clinically meaningful glycemic control and weight reduction, which may result in substantial positive changes in patients' daily lives. The objective of this study was to conduct exit interviews following the ACHIEVE-3 trial to characterize positive treatment experiences and outcomes, beyond glycated hemoglobin and weight reduction, reported by patients living with type 2 diabetes who received oral glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist-based treatments. Qualitative interviews were conducted across ten clinical sites within the USA with patients who had enrolled in ACHIEVE-3 and completed at least 3 months of treatment. Interviews were conducted in English or Spanish, audio-recorded, and transcribed. Transcripts were analyzed to identify and categorize positive treatment benefits reported during the interviews. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize the sample. Sixty patients completed the qualitative exit interviews. Patients had a mean age of 59.1 years (standard deviation [SD] = 10.3), and almost half were female (n = 28, 46.7%). Patients had been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for a mean of 8.5 years (SD = 5.7). By the end of the study, patients reduced their glycated hemoglobin by 1.6% (SD = 1.3) from a baseline of 8.3% and lost a mean of 4.7 kg (SD = 6.8) from a baseline of 96.0 kg. All patients reported being satisfied with the trial medication (n = 59/59), were likely to recommend the treatment to other patients, and all but one were willing to continue taking the medication. As expected, the two most important and most frequently reported positive changes were controlled glycated hemoglobin (n = 53, 88.3%) and weight reduction (n = 50, 83.3%). Other common spontaneously reported positive concepts included increased perceived energy (n = 28, 46.7%), reduced appetite and cravings (n = 23, 38.3%), improved exercise/movement (n = 18, 30.0%), and psychological improvements (n = 18, 30.0%). Additional positive changes included increased confidence/self-esteem, improved diet and eating habits, improved sleep, and improved or a lack of deterioration in vision. All reported positive changes were considered meaningful by patients. The current study explored the positive experiences of patients taking an oral glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist in the ACHIEVE-3 trial beyond traditional clinical benefits, such as glycemic control and weight reduction. The positive changes identified may be suitable targets for future clinical trial clinical outcome assessment endpoint strategies to help differentiate treatments and in clinical practices to classify patients' experiences.

papers.title: The Importance of Translational Research for Neurodevelopmental Disorders and Autism Spectrum Disorders.
papers.abstract: Translational research is the process of transforming fundamental biological discoveries into safe and efficacious interventions for patients. This specialized field is of particular importance for neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), a broad class of behaviorally defined conditions including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDDs), and related disorders. NDDs present unique translational challenges including (i) a lack of biological diagnostic markers; (ii) the fact that they are diagnosed exclusively by behavioral criteria; (iii) their involvement of dysfunction in complex brain circuitry; and (iv) that there is no single unifying biological mechanism. This chapter reviews the current landscape of translational neuroscience for NDDs, examining the strengths and limitations of preclinical model systems, including rodent models humanized mice, human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) 3D spheroids and brain organoids. This work emphasizes that research emanating from the varying preclinical experimental systems above should be leveraged and their complementary strengths integrated, coordinated, and considered collaboratively, to strengthen current knowledge, identify the remaining research gaps, and prioritize future research. We also emphasize the importance of rigorous, reproducible methodology and conservative interpretation of behavioral and functional outcomes. Discussion is presented on key translational bridges or connections that are urgently required to advance the field: bridging non-human model systems to humanized models, identifying and validating translational biomarkers, bridging in vitro and in vivo findings, and developing corroborative alternatives to animal models. It is our stance that integrating multiple complementary model systems, limiting erroneous behavioral inferences, relying on evolutionarily conserved circuits, and prioritizing robust and reproducible outcome measures will reduce failures in the translational pipeline and accelerate the development of meaningful therapies for individuals with NDDs.

papers.title: Recovery after cystectomy and urinary diversion: patient experiences and challenges.
papers.abstract: Radical cystectomy with urinary diversion is the standard treatment for muscle-invasive bladder cancer, yet patients often face substantial recovery challenges post-surgery. Previous research has identified common issues; however, the prevalence and predictors of these challenges remain underexplored. This study was aimed at assessing the frequency and nature of post-operative challenges experienced by bladder cancer patients and at identifying clinical and demographic factors associated with higher unmet needs. Participants from three Kaiser Permanente regions who underwent cystectomy with either ileal conduit or neobladder diversion between 2013 and 2015 completed surveys at 6 and 18 months post-surgery. Items were derived from prior qualitative research and clinician input. Multivariable linear and negative binomial regressions were used to examine associations between surgery type and patient characteristics and challenges. Among 269 respondents at 6 months and 201 at 18 months, 80% and 68% reported at least one challenge, respectively. Common issues included accidents/leaks, sleep disturbances, and managing necessary urinary diversion supplies. Patients with ileal conduits reported more body habitus-related challenges, which increased over time. At 18 months, younger age, male sex, and advanced AJCC stage were associated with a higher number of challenges. Surgery type and complications were not significantly associated with challenge burden. Recovery from cystectomy and urinary diversion is marked by persistent challenges which vary by diversion type and patient characteristics. These findings highlight the extent to which challenges continue over time, and may help inform the development and future evaluation of tailored supportive interventions for bladder cancer survivors.

papers.title: Morning blood pressure surge and morning hypertension in kidney transplant recipients.
papers.abstract: Kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) frequently exhibit abnormal ambulatory blood pressure (BP) patterns, particularly nocturnal hypertension and impaired dipping. However, morning hypertension and morning BP surge (MBPS) remain less well-characterized in this population. This analysis aims to evaluate the prevalence and phenotypes of morning hypertension and ambulatory BP monitoring (ABPM)-derived morning surge indices according to nocturnal BP status and dipping pattern in KTRs. A total of 135 KTRs who underwent 24 h ABPM (ABPMpro device) were included. Morning BP was defined as mean BP during the first two hours after awakening. MBPS was assessed using pre-awakening, sleep-through and rising surge definitions. Morning hypertension was present in 53.3% of KTRs; among those with morning hypertension, 93.1% had sustained nocturnal and morning hypertension. Elevated SBP was equally frequent during morning and nighttime periods (43.7% each), but only half of them had elevated BP during daytime. Office BP underestimated morning BP burden, with masked morning hypertension identified in 18.5%. Participants with nocturnal hypertension had lower pre-awakening systolic MBPS than those without nocturnal hypertension (8.0 ± 12.1 vs. 15.2 ± 12.8 mmHg, p = 0.014), as well as lower sleep-through systolic MBPS (15.6 ± 13.0 vs. 22.2 ± 13.9 mmHg, p = 0.037), while rising MBPS did not differ significantly. Across dipping categories, MBPS indices were consistently higher in dippers and lower in reverse dippers (pre-awakening SBP surge: dippers 24.7 ± 13.1, non-dippers 10.7 ± 9.1, and reverse-dippers 1.1 ± 11.2 mmHg; p < 0.001). Morning hypertension is common in KTRs and is driven predominantly by sustained nocturnal and morning hypertension. Blunted MBPS likely reflects persistent nocturnal BP elevation and impaired dipping status.

papers.title: Cellular consequences of non-ablative radiotherapy, a novel approach to ventricular tachycardias.
papers.abstract: Radiotherapy (RT) with a single application of ionizing radiation (STAR) has been suggested as a non-invasive alternative to radiofrequency in ablating ventricular tachycardia (VT). Emerging data reveal that STAR may suppress VT without substrate destruction, by enhancing impulse conduction instead, through increased expression of NaV1.5 channels and connexin 43. The study aims to investigate electrophysiology and intracellular Ca2+ dynamics in cardiomyocytes (CMs) from mice subjected to in-vivo RT. The emerging data led us to evaluate biochemical changes potentially linking electrophysiological response to ionizing irradiation. CMs isolated 2 weeks after RT with low-dose (15 Gy) or high-dose (25 Gy) were compared to those of sham-treated mice (CTRL). We evaluated: i) the properties of the transient (INaT) and sustained (INasus) components of INa; ii) AP parameters, including the prevalence of Early After-Depolarizations (EADs); iii) intracellular Ca2+ dynamics; iv) CaMKII phosphorylation and v) ROS content. 25 Gy RT i) increased INaT and, to a larger extent, INasus (increased INasus/INaT ratio); ii) increased AP amplitude, +dV/dtMAX and duration (APD) and facilitated EADs; iii) depressed intracellular Ca2+ dynamics. 15 Gy RT had similar but smaller effects (dose-dependency). 25 Gy RT reduced CaMKII phosphorylation but increased cell ROS content, thus providing a mechanism for the late component of INa (INaL) enhancement. The results support the view that STAR may supress VT by increasing conduction velocity, with APD prolongation providing an additional mechanism. On the other hand, INasus enhancement and Ca2+ handling depression may impair electrical stability and contractility in the irradiated region.
papers.journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology

papers.title: Bispectral index-suppression ratio discordance during general anaesthesia.
Systemic outcomes following maxillomandibular advancement for obstructive sleep apnea: systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common sleep disorder associated with an elevated risk of systemic comorbidities. Maxillomandibular advancement (MMA) surgery can reduce upper airway obstruction and improve sleep parameters, but its systemic health benefits remain less well characterized. This systematic review and meta-analysis was performed to synthesize evidence on the systemic health outcomes associated with MMA in patients with OSA. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception through May 20, 2026. Inclusion criteria encompassed original research studies (case series, cohort studies, trials) reporting systemic health outcomes after MMA for OSA. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed using an NIH quality assessment tool. Seven studies (271 patients), with mean follow-up ranging from 5.2 months to 6.6 years, met the inclusion criteria . All studies reported significant reductions in apnea-hypopnea index postoperatively. Four studies included in a meta-analysis demonstrated statistically significant reductions in blood pressure: systolic, mean difference -8.6 mmHg (95% confidence interval -14.2 to -3.0); diastolic, mean difference -5.3 mmHg (95% confidence interval -8.5 to -2.0). MMA for OSA not only improves airway patency and sleep metrics, but is also associated with enduring systemic health benefits, including a blood pressure reduction. Limited evidence also suggests potential improvements in neurocognitive outcomes. Although the evidence suggests a positive impact, further high-quality randomized controlled trials employing rigorous outcome measures (e.g., ambulatory blood pressure monitoring) are needed to fully delineate the persistent systemic effects of maxillomandibular advancement.
papers.journal: International journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery

papers.title: Mediterranean diet adherence and sleep quality in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: association or independent predictor? Author's reply.
Wearable-assessed sleep in Arctic industrial shift workers: effects of shift type, chronotype and season.
Deep learning-based excitation-emission matrix fluorescence spectroscopic analysis of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in coal tar.
papers.abstract: Rapid and accurate analysis of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in coal tar (CT) is essential yet challenging due to spectral overlap and matrix effects. Excitation-emission matrix (EEM) fluorescence spectral analysis using deep learning algorithms can address this challenge. Coal tar samples were extracted and diluted with cyclohexane. A dataset of 1173 EEM spectra covering 3- to 6-ring PAHs and various concentration gradients was constructed. Seven machine learning algorithms were used for qualitative classification of PAHs, and the deep learning algorithm, ResNet18, achieved the highest accuracy, close to 90%. Quantitative analysis was performed using a convolutional neural network-based variational autoencoder (CNN-VAE) model, yielding Root mean square error (RMSE) and (Mean absolute error) MAE values as low as 0.0036 mg/L and 0.0028 mg/L, respectively. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for accurate PAH quantification in complex coal-tar matrices. This new approach provides a cost-effective, rapid, and reliable alternative to conventional methods, mitigating issues such as Rayleigh scattering and spectral overlap. It offers a new strategy for detecting PAH molecules in complex matrices.

papers.title: SpectralTAG: Functional group identification from infrared spectra via unified LLM and GNN textual graphs.
papers.abstract: Spectral analysis underpins much of modern chemical characterization, yet extracting chemically meaningful interpretations from spectral signals remains constrained by the disconnect between data-driven pattern recognition and structured domain knowledge. Here we present SpectralTAG, a unified graph-based reasoning framework that bridges this gap by representing infrared spectra, hierarchical chemical knowledge graphs, and scientific text within a common textual attribute graph (TAG). In this representation, continuous spectra are discretized into semantically annotated range nodes, aligned with functional-group and vibration-type entities from a chemical ontology, and augmented with task-specific prompt and response nodes, enabling a single graph backbone to support node-level functional group classification, edge-level peak-pair relationship judgment, and graph-level molecular classification tasks through large language model encoding and graph neural network inference, without task-specific architectural redesign. Evaluated on 306 organic molecules with infrared spectra, SpectralTAG achieves AUC > 0.98 on edge- and graph-level tasks across 24 encoder-GNN combinations, with LLaMa2-7b paired with R-GCN delivering the most consistent cross-task performance. The framework further supports multitask training with negligible performance trade-off and exhibits emerging zero-shot and few-shot generalization under disjoint label conditions. These results establish textual attribute graphs as a viable paradigm for unifying heterogeneous scientific data within a single reasoning architecture, with implications beyond spectroscopy for broader knowledge-enhanced scientific analysis.

papers.title: Intelligent Wearable Respiratory Monitoring System Based on All-Electrospun Silver Nanowires/Graphene/Thermoplastic Polyurethane Strain Sensors.
papers.abstract: Respiration serves as a critical physiological indicator, with abnormalities in its patterns and rates closely associated with respiratory and cardiovascular diseases, particularly sleep apnea syndrome (SAS). Wearable abdomen-mounted respiratory sensors offer a promising solution for long-term, comfortable, and noninvasive monitoring; however, the subtle mechanical deformations induced by respiration impose stringent requirements on sensor sensitivity and stability. Here, we report a versatile flexible strain sensor designed for comprehensive respiratory monitoring across diverse scenarios. This sensor adopts an all-fibrous and fully electrospun architecture composed of silver nanowires (AgNWs), graphene (GR), and thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU), which is fabricated through a dual-channel hybrid electrospinning strategy. The sensor exhibits dual-regime sensitivity. It delivers a stable and linear gauge factor (GF) of 133.3 in the low-strain range (0-40%), which is highly suitable for high-fidelity daily respiration monitoring. Meanwhile, a high GF is achieved in the high-strain region (>40%), enabling the accurate capture of vigorous physiological behaviors such as severe coughing and strenuous exercise. This multi-range sensitivity endows the sensor with high precision for subtle biological signals and reliable responsiveness to intense physiological events, along with outstanding flexibility, mechanical durability, and wearable comfort. Benefiting from the highly interpenetrated three-dimensional conductive network, the sensor enables precise detection of minute respiratory-induced deformations. Furthermore, an integrated respiratory monitoring system is developed, allowing accurate identification of different respiratory states through feature signal extraction and analysis. This work provides an efficient and scalable strategy for constructing high-performance dual-regime flexible strain sensors and demonstrates their strong potential for wearable respiratory health monitoring applications.

papers.title: Central Neuroendocrine Governance as a Unifying Framework for Host-Tumor Interaction: From Afferent Sensing to Therapeutic Modulation.
papers.abstract: Cancer is not biologically confined to the tumor bed. Cachexia, fatigue, metabolic dysfunction, circadian disruption, and immune dysfunction reflect disturbances that local models alone cannot fully explain. The brain is well positioned to participate in these processes because it continuously samples circulating signals and coordinates endocrine and autonomic responses. Yet the afferent side of this communication has received less attention than its downstream consequences. Here, we synthesize evidence showing that cytokines, hormones, metabolites, and cargo carried by extracellular vesicles can engage central sensory interfaces and integrative regions, particularly circumventricular organs and hypothalamic and brainstem circuits. We use the term Endocriception to describe afferent humoral sensing and early central decoding of circulating biochemical signals, and focus here on how tumor- and host-associated changes engage this process in cancer. Central neuroendocrine governance refers to the subsequent integration of this information and the generation of autonomic and endocrine outputs. Persistent inflammation, stress, circadian disruption, and impaired feedback may gradually reconfigure this regulatory system. The resulting changes can affect systemic immunity, metabolism, behavior, and host tolerance of cancer. Evidence is strongest for a limited number of pathways, whereas many proposed links remain incomplete or dependent on tumor type and experimental context. We therefore present central neuroendocrine governance as a working framework for organizing current evidence and guiding mechanistic studies, biomarker development, and interventions aimed at restoring host physiology.

papers.title: Early Nocturnal Care Disruption and the Hazard of Incident ICU Delirium in Critically Ill Adults: A Target-Trial Emulation in MIMIC-IV.
papers.abstract: Nighttime care contacts fragment sleep and are often invoked as a contributor to intensive care delirium. Whether a higher intensity of those contacts early in the stay is associated with later incident delirium is unclear. Sicker, more sedated patients are monitored more often overnight and are also more likely to become delirious. We emulated a target trial in MIMIC-IV version 3.1. Adults were eligible if the first intensive care stay lasted at least 48 hours and the delirium screen was negative at that landmark. High exposure was a nocturnal contact rate above the cohort median, built from vital-sign charting, laboratory draws, and bedside medication administrations between 22:00 and 05:59 and divided by 16 nocturnal hours. Follow-up for incident delirium began at the landmark. We estimated the hazard ratio with stabilized inverse-probability weights and a pooled-logistic survival model. Of 12,922 eligible stays, 2,862 developed incident delirium. High nocturnal care-contact intensity was associated with a higher hazard (adjusted hazard ratio 1.43, 95% confidence interval 1.27 to 1.60). The hazard rose across tertiles of the contact rate and was higher for vital-sign charting and phlebotomy than for medication administration. A higher intensity of early nocturnal care contacts was associated with a moderately higher hazard of incident delirium. Residual confounding remains possible, including reverse causation if prodromal delirium itself increases overnight contacts before the first positive screen.

papers.title: Neurovascular coupling in simultaneous EEG-fNIRS studies: A scoping review of analytical frameworks and clinical applications.
papers.abstract: Simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) have been used across cognitive and physiological states and in diverse clinical populations. However, the interpretation of cross-modal coupling remains difficult because findings from different analytical frameworks, populations, and experimental conditions have not been systematically mapped. This scoping review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, EBSCO, and IEEE Xplore were searched through February 10, 2026, for studies that quantitatively related simultaneously recorded EEG and fNIRS signals. Two reviewers independently screened the records. Findings were synthesized narratively, and analytical pipelines were mapped across the signal domain, feature extraction, coupling metric, and temporal lag handling. Fifty-seven studies were included. Amplitude-based studies related event-related potentials and oscillatory EEG features to focal hemodynamic responses, with associations varying across electrophysiological features, cortical regions, and task conditions. Frequency- and scale-specific analyses identified band-dependent relationships, while coupling at ultra-slow scales showed sensitivity to vascular and systemic physiological influences. Studies that explicitly modeled timing identified several-second offsets in some paradigms, while directional estimates varied across tasks and recording states. Network analyses showed partial and context-dependent correspondence between EEG- and fNIRS-derived measures, while model-based approaches characterized multivariate and predictive cross-modal relationships. Across frameworks, observed coupling differed with recording state, frequency band, cortical region, and temporal lag handling rather than representing a single quantity. Clinical findings were heterogeneous, and most condition-specific patterns were supported by small and methodologically diverse evidence bases. These findings support framework-matched analysis and pipeline-explicit reporting when interpreting EEG-fNIRS coupling.

papers.title: Longitudinal wearable monitoring and polygenic score for major depressive disorder in the All of Us Research Program.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) susceptibility reflects both stable inherited liability and dynamic behavioral patterns, yet these dimensions are rarely examined together using long-term data in real-world settings. Here, we integrated genomic, electronic health record (EHR), and longitudinal Fitbit wearable data from 3030 adults of genetically inferred European ancestry in the All of Us Research Program, 284 of whom had an EHR-recorded MDD diagnosis during follow-up after a 180-day baseline period. Time-varying Cox models examined associations of the MDD polygenic score (PGS), monthly wearable-derived physical activity and sleep features, and wearable feature × MDD PGS interactions with EHR-recorded MDD. Higher MDD PGS, lower daily steps, lower light and vigorous physical activity, lower sleep efficiency, and greater sleep duration variability were associated with a higher hazard of EHR-recorded MDD. The associations of sedentary time and sleep duration variability with MDD differed across MDD PGS levels, with stronger associations among participants with higher MDD PGS. Model-estimated hazard ratio curves across MDD PGS levels further showed that the behavioral levels corresponding to the same relative hazard differed across levels of genetic liability, with more favorable behavioral levels observed at higher MDD PGS levels. Sequentially integrating MDD PGS, baseline wearable features, monthly wearable features, and selected wearable feature × MDD PGS interactions increased model discrimination, with the C-index increasing from 0.637 to 0.705. These findings support the complementary value of genetic liability and longitudinal behavioral monitoring for characterization of MDD susceptibility and may inform work on genetically informed digital phenotyping for personalized monitoring and prevention.

papers.title: Structural and Functional Characterization of a Novel Broad-Spectrum Oligosaccharide Uptake Channel OmpV25 in Vibrio campbellii.
papers.abstract: Vibrio campbellii (formerly Vibrio harveyi) is a marine pathogen that causes vibriosis, a major disease affecting global aquaculture. This bacterium inhabits chitin-rich environments and uses chito-oligosaccharides as a main nutrient source. Here, we identify the novel outer membrane protein OmpV25 as a porin mediating broad-spectrum oligosaccharide uptake in V. campbellii. OmpV25 was heterologously expressed in Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3) Omp8, purified by nickel affinity and size exclusion chromatography, and crystallized. The resulting 2.70 Å crystal structure revealed the 25-kDa OmpV25 to be a monomeric β-barrel composed of 12 β-strands connected by six extracellular loops and five periplasmic turns. Single-channel electrophysiology demonstrated that OmpV25 forms stable monomeric pores in artificial lipid bilayers characterized by a conductance of 0.19 ± 0.003 nS in 1 M KCl. The channel facilitated binding of mono-, di-, tri- and tetragalacturonic acids, as well as chitotetraose and maltotetraose. Fluorescence spectroscopy revealed moderate-affinity binding to tetragalacturonic acid (Kd = 3.04 ± 0.42 μM), chitotetraose (Kd = 6.79 ± 0.27 μM), and maltotetraose (Kd = 5.21 ± 0.78 μM). A liposome swelling assay confirmed that OmpV25 enables translocation of a broad range of oligosaccharides beyond oligogalacturonic acids. These findings define the physiological role of OmpV25 as a broad-specificity sugar channel that may support environmental resilience of Vibrio species in nutrient-variable marine habitats.

papers.title: Circadian system and human health: From molecular mechanisms to clinical integration.
papers.abstract: The circadian system, an evolutionarily conserved endogenous oscillator coordinating physiological adaptation to geophysical cycles, coordinates hierarchical gene regulatory networks, metabolic pathways, and physiological functions to maintain organismal homeostasis. Circadian disturbances caused by modern lifestyle are recognized as key etiological factors in complex multisystem disorders, including neurodegenerative, cardiovascular, metabolic, and oncogenic pathologies. The review synthesizes current evidence to delineate that organ-specific physiological programs across the human body are under circadian clock, and chronic desynchronization of system drives a broad spectrum of clinical disorders. Moreover, the review critically assesses state-of-the-art therapeutic modalities, and identifies promising technological innovations. It advances precision chronomedicine by proposing public health interventions, such as environmental modification combined with behavioral education, offering a roadmap for clinical implementation of circadian restoration therapies.

papers.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of antihistamines, increased antihistamine dosing, and antihistamine adjuncts for chronic urticaria: a systematic review, dose-response, and network meta-analysis of randomized trials.
papers.abstract: Chronic urticaria is a common immune-mediated condition characterized by wheals (itch and hives), angioedema, or both, lasting for greater than six weeks. It is managed with H1 antihistamines as the first-line therapy. Fundamental unresolved questions remain regarding the comparative benefits and harms of antihistamines and their adjuncts, and of H1 antihistamine dose-escalation. To analyze the comparative benefits and harms of antihistamines and their adjuncts (H2 blockers or montelukast), and of H1 antihistamine dose-escalation. As part of updating the American Academy of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology and American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology Joint Task Force on Practice Parameters Chronic Urticaria guidelines, we searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, CENTRAL, and regulatory databases from inception to March 17, 2025, for randomized trials addressing antihistamines or their adjuncts for chronic urticaria. Paired reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. Random effects network and dose-response meta-analyses addressed urticaria activity (composed of itch and wheal scores), angioedema activity, urticaria-related quality of life, and harms including sedation. The GRADE approach informed certainty of evidence ratings. CRD42022367280. 211 trials (22,187 participants) evaluated 55 unique treatments. Bilastine, desloratadine, fexofenadine, and levocetirizine are among the most effective in improving overall urticaria activity, urticaria-related quality of life, and sleep disturbance. Cetirizine and loratadine are among the most effective in reducing overall urticaria activity and its subcomponents, with cetirizine also among the most effective in improving urticaria-related quality of life. Escalating from a single to quadruple daily dose may yield diminishing additional benefit. Second-generation agents as a class may be more effective than first-generation agents in improving urticaria activity and sleep disturbance. Sedation risk likely increases with higher doses, with first-generation agents (e.g., diphenhydramine, hydroxyzine) and doxepin among the most sedating; cetirizine, ketotifen, levocetirizine, and rupatadine among the intermediate sedating; and bepotastine, bilastine, desloratadine, ebastine, fexofenadine, and loratadine among the least sedating. Adding montelukast (moderate certainty) or an H2 blocker (very low certainty) to a second-generation agent may further reduce urticaria activity. For chronic urticaria, second-generation agents differ in their efficacy and safety. First-generation agents are less beneficial and more harmful. Escalating to higher daily doses may provide additional benefits but likely increases sedation.
papers.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology

papers.title: Sleep and fatigue/energy bolt-ons for the EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: This study systematically reviewed the development, use, psychometrics, and valuation of sleep and fatigue/energy bolt-ons for the EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L. A systematic review was conducted based on key elements of the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Searches on PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science, supplemented by citation tracking and manual Google Scholar and EuroQol conference searches, were used. Key study characteristics, bolt-on specifications, psychometric properties, and valuation evidence were summarized narratively. Twenty-one publications from 19 unique studies conducted in 19 countries were published between 1991 and 2025. Sleep and fatigue/energy bolt-ons were used together in 13 studies. Twelve distinct sleep and 14 fatigue/energy bolt-on versions have been developed, mostly in five-level formats (sleep=67%; fatigue/energy=71%). The development of 3 sleep and 5 fatigue/energy bolt-ons was supported by qualitative evidence. Quantitative evidence from 13 sleep and 13 fatigue/energy bolt-on studies revealed bolt-ons commonly reduced ceiling effects although not across all conditions (absolute reduction: sleep=0.3-30.0%, fatigue/energy=1.9-30.9%), showed good convergent validity with conceptually related external measures or their items/domains, and improved EQ VAS explanatory power (sleep=0.7-10.0%, fatigue/energy=0.1%-3.7%). Findings on known-group validity were heterogeneous across clinically relevant known-groups. Evidence on test-retest reliability (n=1) and responsiveness (n=3) was limited. Valuation evidence (n=5) regarding the impact of bolt-ons on preferences was scarce and inconclusive. The development of sleep and fatigue/energy bolt-ons to date has lacked sufficient qualitative input, while some psychometric findings supported their added value to the EQ-5D. Future mixed-methods bolt-on development and refinement studies are needed for both constructs.
papers.journal: Value in health : the journal of the International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research

papers.title: The glymphatic system as a mechanistic bridge between migraine and sleep: Evidence from clinical studies and animal models.
papers.abstract: Migraine is a highly prevalent, disabling neurological disorder often accompanied by sleep disturbances; however, the mechanisms linking sleep disturbance to migraine susceptibility remain unclear. The glymphatic system, a sleep-modulated perivascular clearance network facilitated by astrocytic aquaporin-4 (AQP4) and functionally connected to meningeal lymphatic drainage, is a potential mechanistic link between migraine and sleep disturbances. This review synthesizes evidence from clinical neuroimaging, cerebrospinal fluid and blood biomarker studies, and preclinical animal models to evaluate glymphatic involvement in migraine. Astrocytic AQP4 polarization, perivascular patency, and meningeal lymphatic drainage directly intersect with core migraine mechanisms, including cortical spreading depression-induced perivascular closure and calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)-mediated meningeal lymphatic dysfunction. Although clinical findings are heterogeneous, glymphatic-related imaging and biomarker abnormalities appear to be more evident in association with higher attack frequency, longer disease duration, and poorer sleep quality. Animal models have linked sleep disruption, cortical spreading depression, and CGRP signaling to altered glymphatic and meningeal lymphatic functions. Four complementary hypotheses-waste accumulation, bidirectional disruption loop, the meningeal lymphatic-CGRP axis, and chronification-provide an integrative framework for this relationship across multiple timescales. These findings support the integration of sleep assessment with a glymphatic-informed framework in migraine evaluation and generate testable hypotheses that sleep-directed interventions may influence glymphatic function and that anti-CGRP therapies may partly act through meningeal lymphatic mechanisms, although these clearance-related therapeutic mechanisms remain unconfirmed in patients.

papers.title: An Efficient Convolutional Neural Network Model for Classifying Positive Affective States from EEG Data Considering Sleep Condition.
papers.abstract: The recognition of affective states from EEG recordings considering the sleep condition can be an important supporting tool in therapy and in the treatment of psychological or psychiatric disorders. Since sleep deprivation changes EEG characteristics, a two-stage framework is developed for affective state classification. First, a classification between "Normal Sleep" (NS) and "Sleep-Deprived" (SD) is conducted using resting-state EEG data. The data are then fed into one of two newly proposed, lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to recognize four affective states. In the first stage, CNN-BiLSTM achieves 95.96% accuracy under window-level splitting and 70.46% under subject-independent 5-fold cross-validation, while in the second stage the proposed models achieve 93.40% (NS) and 90.95% (SD) under window-level splitting, and 38.98% (NS) and 38.97% (SD) under cross-validation. The lower subject-independent accuracies reflect the class imbalance and the clustering of scores near the class boundaries, which make cross-subject four-class generalization challenging. As existing studies mostly classify momentary emotions without addressing sleep conditions, direct comparison with prior work is difficult; we therefore benchmarked our framework against several established baseline models, including SqueezeNet, EEGNet, ShallowConvNet, Support Vector Machine, and Random Forest. This study suggests that considering physiological states can improve multi-class classification of affective states from time-varying neurophysiological signals such as EEG. The framework performs strongly under window-level evaluation, whereas its performance under the stricter subject-independent setting is more limited and should be interpreted accordingly. It can nonetheless contribute to more comprehensive research in affective neuroscience.

papers.title: Myocardial Fibrosis as an Arrhythmogenic Substrate: Integrating Genetics, Imaging and Invasive Electrophysiology for Sudden Death Risk Stratification.
CSTO-Net: Cross-View Spectral-Transport and Topology-Operator Network for EEG Emotion Recognition.
papers.abstract: Multi-view electroencephalography (EEG) emotion recognition must decide how the spectral graph sets of different connectivity views correspond and how their graph propagation operators interact. We present CSTO-Net, a cross-view spectral-transport and topology-operator network for EEG-based emotion recognition.Approach: CSTO-Net integrates three window-wise views: dynamic differential entropy (DDE) as node attributes, amplitude-envelope Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) graphs, and phase-locking value (PLV) graphs. Cross-View Spectral Transport Routing (CSTR) formulates PCC-PLV spectral correspondence as an entropy-regularized optimal-transport problem with explicit marginal constraints, deliberately separating correspondence estimation from band-importance estimation. Directional Cross-Topology Modulation (DCTM) performs ordered composition of the two routed propagation operators on shared node features and encodes order-dependent propagation discrepancy via a provably skew-symmetric graph-operator commutator with signed decomposition.Main results: On the Database for Emotion Analysis using Physiological Signals (DEAP) dataset, CSTO-Net achieves 93.95 ± 2.50% valence and 94.97 ± 2.72% arousal accuracy under the subject-dependent setting, and 93.73% and 94.54% under participant-wise five-fold subject-independent cross-validation across 32 participants. On the SJTU Emotion EEG Dataset (SEED), it achieves 93.12% under the standard subject-dependent split, 91.36% under 15-fold leave-one-subject-out evaluation across 15 participants, and 98.05 ± 2.32% under subject-dependent five-fold cross-validation. Ablation studies confirm that both CSTR and DCTM contribute substantially to recognition accuracy.Significance: These results demonstrate that explicit cross-view spectral correspondence and topology-operator-level interaction provide complementary benefits for EEG emotion recognition, offering an interpretable route for modeling order-sensitive interactions between functional connectivity views.

papers.title: [Diagnostics of polyneuropathies].
papers.abstract: Polyneuropathies are a heterogeneous group of peripheral nerve disorders with diverse causes and phenotypes. Structured, phenotype-oriented diagnostics are important for reliably identifying common and treatable triggers such as diabetes, alcohol, vitamin deficiency, or medication, and for distinguishing them from immune-mediated, paraneoplastic, or genetic neuropathies. Medical history, clinical examination, and electrophysiology usually provide the decisive clues. In addition, basic laboratory diagnostics, targeted immunological tests, and modern genetics are used for selected indications-such as for the question of sorbitol dehydrogenase (SORD) mutations and repeat expansion of replication factor C 1 (RFC1). Nerve ultrasound and biopsy have selected indications. Entities such as immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated neuropathies and nitrous oxide induced myeloneuropathy are gaining in importance. Age-related physiological changes must always be taken into account.

papers.title: Performance evaluation of MAGIX-UPu software for determination of uranium and plutonium isotopic composition with medium resolution gamma-ray detectors.
papers.abstract: This study evaluates the performance of the MAGIX-UPu software for determining the isotopic composition of uranium (U) and plutonium (Pu) using medium-resolution gamma-ray detectors in nuclear industry applications. The analysis involves two Lanthanum Bromide (LaBr3) detectors of different sizes and an H3D gamma camera (Cadmium Zinc Telluride, CZT). Developed by CEA List, this code performs a comprehensive and automatic spectrum analysis, including calibration, peak deconvolution, and simultaneous determination of relative efficiency and isotopic composition. The analysis revealed that the H3D gamma camera provided significantly better results due to its superior energy resolution. The mass fractions of 239Pu can notably be obtained with an average total uncertainty of 1.3%. The results obtained for uranium spectra are also satisfying, with an average total uncertainty of 8.9% for 235U. With the LaBr3 detectors, MAGIX-UPu can determine the isotopic composition of U and Pu, but the poor resolution complicates the analysis and makes consistency checks difficult. Nevertheless, the results provided by MAGIX-UPu for plutonium are good compared to other software.
papers.journal: Applied radiation and isotopes : including data, instrumentation and methods for use in agriculture, industry and medicine

papers.title: Early caregiver mirroring predicts the emergence of action-unit-based facial representations in the infant brain.
papers.abstract: Early caregiver-infant interactions play a crucial role in the development of facial expression understanding, but little is known about how early experience shapes the neural representation of facial expression information. In the adult brain, facial expressions are represented componentially, with neural activity encoding constituent facial muscle configurations, or action units (AUs), independently of global emotion categories. This may provide important functional advantages, but the developmental emergence of such a representational format is unclear. We examined whether neural representations of facial expressions become increasingly organised around AU structure across early development, and whether caregiver mirroring predicts this process. Electroencephalography (EEG) data were analysed from samples of nine-month-olds and 30-month-olds, who viewed short video clips of dynamic facial expressions. Nine-month-olds had also been observed during mother-infant interactions at two months of age. Time-resolved representational similarity analysis was used to characterise the dynamic geometry of neural representations. At 30 months, neural activity reliably encoded AU structure, whereas group-level AU encoding was not observed at nine months. However, individual differences in AU encoding at nine months were predicted by maternal mirroring of infant facial expressions at two months. This relationship was specific to direct mirroring responses, and was not explained by more general maternal responding. These findings suggest that neural representations of facial expressions become increasingly organised around constituent facial movements across early development, and that caregiver mirroring is associated with the emergence of componential facial representations. More generally, they provide initial evidence linking early embodied social interaction to the development of facial representational organisation.

papers.title: Prevalence of meeting sleep duration recommendations among over 1.4 million children and adolescents across 58 countries: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to estimate the prevalence of children and adolescents meeting sleep duration recommendations across international studies and to examine variation by age group, day type, sex, and region. Three databases were searched. Eligible studies reported adherence to age-specific recommendations (9-11 h/day for children and 8-10 h/day for adolescents). Subjective or proxy-reported estimates were pooled using maximum-likelihood random-effects models of logit-transformed proportions with Knapp-Hartung confidence intervals. Fifty-three studies including 1,402,868 participants (49.7% female) were included. Pooled prevalence was 76.5% (95% CI 71.6-80.9) in children and 54.8% (95% CI 50.0-59.6) in adolescents. Adolescents had lower odds of meeting recommendations before multiplicity adjustment (OR = 0.37, 95% CI 0.15-0.94; p = 0.040), but not after Holm adjustment (p = 0.120). Prevalence was lower on school than non-school days in children (56.7% vs 82.2%; based on three publications) and adolescents (50.6% vs 86.4%; both Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). No robust sex differences were observed. Regional estimates varied substantially and require cautious interpretation because of extreme heterogeneity and uneven geographic representation. In conclusion, insufficient sleep appears especially common during adolescence and on school days, supporting strategies to improve sleep during the school week. PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420261289109.

papers.title: Functional neurological disorder and sleep disturbances: from comorbidity to mechanistic insight.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are common in functional neurological disorder (FND), with meta-analytic evidence confirming their high frequency. Their relevance may extend beyond comorbidity, raising questions about their relationship to FND mechanisms and potential as therapeutic targets. To synthesize evidence on prevalence, clinical profile, objective findings, and potential mechanisms of sleep disturbances in FND, focusing on subjective-objective discrepancies in sleep perception and vigilance-state assessment. Structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE from inception to April 2026. Evidence was appraised with Joanna Briggs Institute checklists and AMSTAR-2.
