Data collection and analysis for phase 1 were conducted between 2023 and 2025, including literature reviews and exploratory interviews. A deprived neighborhood in the municipality of Rotterdam, the Netherlands, was selected as the target neighborhood. The target population was defined as (pre)pregnant couples and families with a child aged <4 years. Phase 2 is ongoing (2024-2026), focusing on iterative design through locally established field labs and community building. Phase 3 is planned for 2026 to 2028. This protocol describes a socially embedded, multiphase approach to developing and implementing a digital coaching intervention for families in vulnerable circumstances. Through a transdisciplinary approach within a real-world, local community setting, the OSFB program aims to develop a context-sensitive intervention to support sustainable behavior change in early life.

papers.title: Sweet Dreams: Incretin therapy for prevention of obstructive sleep apnea in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity.
papers.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine

papers.title: Influence of Trained Companion Dog Ownership Among Military Veterans Diagnosed With a Mental Health Condition.
papers.abstract: To explore the perceptions of U.S. Veterans on the influence of owning trained companion dogs (TCDs) from animal shelters on their mental health and influence of the historical distress of the dog on dog-owner bonding. A descriptive, exploratory design was used to collect data via telephone interviews with 90 veterans who adopted dogs and had a mental health diagnosis at the time of adoption. Ownership influenced perceptions of loneliness (97%), sense of purpose (87%), exercise (86%), safety (86%), anxiety (84%), depression (84%), and sleep (74%). Veterans who perceived that their dog experienced distress or trauma pre-adoption acknowledged it influenced feelings of connectedness (66%), relating to the dog (81%), helping the dog (81%), and the dog helping them (88%). TCD ownership positively influenced veteran mental health. Help is a two-way street between veterans and dogs with a history of distress or trauma. Health care professionals caring for veterans with mental health conditions should explore dog ownership through specific companion programs.
papers.journal: Journal of psychosocial nursing and mental health services

papers.title: Osteopathic manual therapy in fibromyalgia: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: The aim of this pilot study was to evaluate the preliminary efficacy and feasibility of integrating Osteopathic Manual Therapy Techniques combined with Clinical Pilates on pain, symptom severity, and sleep quality in patients with fibromyalgia. Twenty women with fibromyalgia were randomized into Osteopathic Manual Therapy Techniques+Clinical Pilates (n=11) and Clinical Pilates (n=9) groups. The protocol lasted 6 weeks (3 sessions/week). Osteopathic Manual Therapy Techniques included rib raising, suboccipital myofascial release, Sternocleidomastoid (SCM) mobilization, diaphragm/mediastinum techniques, and visceral mobilizations. Primary outcomes were the Widespread Pain Index, Symptom Severity Scale, and Pressure Pain Threshold. Sleep was assessed via the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Both groups showed significant intra-group improvements (p<0.05). Within-group analyses revealed that the Osteopathic Manual Therapy Techniques+Clinical Pilates group achieved significant improvements in Widespread Pain Index (p=0.003), Symptom Severity Scale (p=0.005), and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (p=0.007). However, in the between-group analysis of change scores, the Osteopathic Manual Therapy Techniques+Clinical Pilates group demonstrated significantly superior improvements exclusively in sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, p=0.034) and maximal Pressure Pain Threshold at the trapezius (p=0.035) compared to the Clinical Pilates-only group, while between-group differences for Widespread Pain Index and Symptom Severity Scale did not reach statistical significance (p>0.05). Integrating Osteopathic Manual Therapy Techniques into exercise-based rehabilitation presents promising preliminary evidence for enhancing central sensitization symptoms and sleep quality in fibromyalgia patients, though larger trials are needed.

papers.title: Effectiveness of a fully digital mandibular advancement appliance compared with CPAP in the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.abstract: Clinicians often face the decision of recommending Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) or a Mandibular Advancement Appliance (MAA) for Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA). The objective of this study was to evaluate the effectiveness of a fully digital workflow MAA and compare its outcomes with CPAP therapy. Twenty adults with OSA confirmed by Type I polysomnography (AHI < 50 events/hour), non-adherent to CPAP, were enrolled in a crossover clinical study. After MAA titration (50% and 75% of maximum protrusion), participants underwent home sleep testing under three conditions: no treatment, CPAP, and MAA. Outcomes included oxygen desaturation index (ODI), snoring score, oxyhemoglobin saturation (SpO₂), hypoxic burden, and mean heart rate. Treatment-induced changes (Δ = treatment - no treatment) were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (α = 5%). Both therapies significantly reduced ODI and snoring, compared to baseline. Median ODI decreased from 13.55 events/hour (untreated) to 6.05 with MAA and 5.30 with CPAP. No statistically significant differences were found between MAA and CPAP for ΔODI (p = 0.401), snoring (p = 0.103), hypoxic burden (p = 0.165), or heart rate (p = 0.824). A significant difference in SpO₂ was observed (p = 0.003), favoring CPAP; however, the difference was small. The fully digital MAA was effective in reducing oxygen desaturation, snoring, and hypoxic burden, showing no clinically meaningful difference compared with CPAP, supporting its use as a viable therapeutic alternative for OSA.

papers.title: Lifestyle factors and clustered patterns of body shape change in Korean adults: A longitudinal observational study.
papers.abstract: Obesity is a major health problem driven by lifestyle habits and changes in body composition, particularly increased body fat mass and reduced skeletal muscle mass. Body mass index alone cannot fully characterize adiposity distribution or changes in muscle mass. Body-shape indicators such as waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, and waist-to-height ratio predict metabolic and cardiovascular disease risk; however, few studies have assessed longitudinal changes in these measures together with lifestyle factors. In this study, we aimed to identify clusters of body-shape change using 2-year follow-up data from Korean adults and to elucidate the body-composition and lifestyle factors underlying these changes. K-means cluster analysis was applied to 1,404 participants in the Korean Medicine Daejeon Citizen Cohort using 2-year changes in body mass index, waist circumference, hip circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, waist-to-height ratio, and body weight. Baseline body shape, body composition, and lifestyle indicators were compared across clusters, and multinomial logistic regression was used to identify variables associated with cluster membership. Three clusters were identified: Stable (48.0%), Adiposity-Increasing (31.0%), and Adiposity-Decreasing (21.0%). At baseline, cluster membership was significantly associated with body fat mass. Over follow-up, changes in body fat mass and skeletal muscle mass showed strong associations with cluster assignment. In addition, clinically meaningful worsening in sleep quality (increase of ≥2.5 points in the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index) and reduced physical activity (decrease in activity as measured by the Global Physical Activity Questionnaire) were significantly associated with the Adiposity-Increasing cluster. Changes in body composition, especially body fat mass and skeletal muscle mass, were closely associated with body-shape trajectories, while worsening sleep quality and declining physical activity were associated with the Adiposity-Increasing trajectory. These findings support an integrative approach that considers body shape, body composition, and modifiable lifestyle factors when characterizing adiposity-related trajectories and designing tailored lifestyle interventions.

papers.title: Post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) are associated with distinct clinical phenotypes two years after SARS-CoV-2 infection: A data-driven approach.
papers.abstract: It is important to determine whether the persistent cognitive and fatigue complaints, as part of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), are associated with underlying patterns and specific symptoms clusters. Therefore, the aim of the present study was to investigate symptom clusters and clinical phenotypes in PASC. We included n = 153 individuals (53 years old, 66% female, 2 years post SARS-CoV-2 infection) categorized into groups with (n = 88) and without (n = 65) PASC, defined by severe fatigue and concentration problems using validated cut-offs. Symptom clusters (i.e., component loadings and component scores) were identified using principal component analyses (PCA, eigenvalue[EV]>1.0), using clinical, somatic, coping and sleep factors, symptom severity, neuropsychological and physical tests (totalling 19 tests and questionnaires). We then used logistic regression techniques on (participant-level) component scores (standardized) to investigate associations with PASC. Finally, K-means clustering methods to identify clinical phenotypes. Analyses were adjusted for age, sex, education, nationality and time since infection. PCA identified 5 components, explaining 70% of the variance. We labelled these components as follows: (1) PEM, ME/CFS and sleep symptoms, coping factors (EV = 7.0, 36.9% variance), (2) information-processing speed (EV = 2.5, 13.3%), (3) executive functioning (EV = 1.5, 8.0%, (4) physical performance (EV = 1.2, 6.5%), (5) somatic comorbidities and hospital admission (EV = 1.0, 5.5%). Logistic regression showed that only the first component scores (Odds ratio [95% confidence interval] = 97.1 [16.5-570.3], p < 0.001,), and none of the others (all p > 0.05), associated with PASC. Cluster analysis revealed two distinct clinical phenotypes among individuals with severe chronic fatigue: one marked by physical impairment and the other by diminished cognitive performance. Consistent with existing literature, we confirmed that PASC is a heterogeneous syndrome marked by extensive, interrelated symptoms. Notably, we identified specific cognitive and physical clinical phenotypes. These findings are important for future targeted diagnosis and treatment.

papers.title: The world's oldest living culture leads the way with interpretable generative AI: Aboriginal women shaping the future of perinatal mental health services.
papers.abstract: Despite their strengths, Aboriginal mothers experience significant health disparities, including perinatal mental health challenges influenced by social, historical, and cultural determinants. Routine risk screening informs follow-up care, yet conventional approaches often fail to address cultural considerations. The Baby Coming You Ready (BCYR) program provides a strengths-based, culturally adapted digital assessment designed to enhance perinatal mental health care. However, some clinicians continue to rely primarily on conventional risk scores, which can neglect broader contextual circumstances influencing Aboriginal mothers, including cultural strengths and protective factors, thereby limiting the program's full impact. This exploratory model-development study examined whether generative AI data augmentation combined with an intrinsically interpretable machine-learning model could support culturally contextualised prediction of perinatal psychological distress among Aboriginal mothers. We analysed deidentified BCYR pilot data from 293 Aboriginal mothers across six Western Australian sites. After excluding five records with incomplete outcome data, the analytic dataset included 288 participants. Models were evaluated using repeated internal train-test splits, with synthetic data used only for training augmentation and performance assessed on held-out real test data. The highest internal performance was observed for the TVAE-augmented Explainable Boosting Machine at an augmentation ratio of 1.0, with an accuracy of 0.867, an F1 score of 0.817, and an AUC of 0.934. Model explanations identified self-blame, loneliness, family pride, day-to-day management, sleep, and related contextual factors as influential contributors to model-estimated risk. These explanations are intended as prompts for culturally safe discussion and clinical reflection. Findings suggest that interpretable generative AI may have potential to support culturally responsive perinatal mental health assessment. However, broader community-governed external validation and prospective clinical workflow evaluation are required before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Healthy lifestyle as a protective factor against the risk of gastroesophageal reflux disease: Prospective population cohort analysis.
papers.abstract: Lifestyle modifications are recommended by American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) for managing gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), a significant health issue; but evidence is scarce. This study aims to investigate the longitudinal association between healthy lifestyle behaviors and the risk of GERD. We analyzed data from 306,543 participants aged between 38 and 73 years without GERD at baseline from the UK Biobank. A summarized healthy lifestyle score (range, 0-7) was calculated using seven items: never smoking, healthy sleep, moderate body mass index (BMI), regular physical exercise, moderate alcohol intake, healthy diet, and moderate tea/coffee intake. Multivariable Cox regression was performed to examine the associations. During a mean follow-up of 12.7 years, 27,943 (9.1%) GERD cases were identified. Each healthy lifestyle, except for moderate alcohol intake (hazard ratios [HR], 1.00; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.98-1.03) was associated with a lower risk of GERD. Relative to participants with less than 2 of summarized healthy lifestyle score, those with 2, 3, 4, and 5-7 of this score showed a significantly lower risk of GERD, with the HR of 0.94 (95% CI: 0.90-0.98), 0.83 (0.80-0.86), 0.74 (0.71-0.77), 0.63 (0.60-0.66), respectively (P for trend <0.001). Stratified analysis shows that the above associations were more pronounced among participants who were younger (< 60 years), female and employed (all P for interaction <0.05). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated similar results. This study highlights the importance of adherence to healthy lifestyle behaviors in reducing the prevalence of GERD in the general population.

papers.title: Sleep EEG oscillations and synaptic plasticity in memory consolidation across NREM and REM sleep.
papers.abstract: Based on a synthesis of recent advances, this review elucidates the distinct yet synergistic roles of non-rapid eye movement (NREM) and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep in memory consolidation. During NREM sleep, cortical slow oscillations (SOs) establish a temporal framework by alternating between UP and DOWN states, facilitating cross-regional communication. SOs phase-couple with thalamic spindles to coordinate hippocampal sharp-wave ripples (SWRs), thereby driving the reactivation and transfer of labile hippocampal memories to neocortical networks for long-term storage. Concurrent synaptic homeostasis optimises network efficiency through global downscaling while selectively strengthening memory-relevant connections. In REM sleep, theta oscillations synchronise limbic-prefrontal-hippocampal circuits, and ponto-geniculo-occipital (PGO) waves further integrate emotional and procedural memories. The cholinergically dominant, monoamine-depleted neurochemical milieu of REM sleep promotes dendritic spine remodelling and sparse neuronal reactivation, enabling affective decoupling and synaptic refinement. Despite progress, key challenges remain in understanding cross-frequency oscillatory coupling among slow oscillations, spindles, ripples and REM-specific rhythms, glial contributions and clinical translation. Future integration of high-density electrophysiology with computational approaches may yield mechanistic models and clinically relevant biomarkers for sleep-based cognitive monitoring and intervention.

papers.title: Deciphering genomic adaptations and climate resilience in the intertidal seagrass Zostera japonica.
papers.abstract: Seagrasses are coastal foundation species that support ecosystem stability but face increasing global change. Here, we assemble a chromosome-level reference genome for the intertidal seagrass Zostera japonica to investigate adaptive evolution and climate resilience. Comparative genomic analyses reveal features underlying intertidal adaptation, including ion transport, circadian regulation, and stress responses. We identify positively selected genes associated with the transition to marine environments. Population genomic analyses identify strong divergence between northern and southern populations, reflecting deep historical separation, largely independent evolutionary trajectories, and local adaptation. Selection signals are enriched in stress response and ion transport genes, among which TIP3-1 confers tolerance to both salinity and heat. Genomic offset projections indicate greater climate vulnerability in northern populations, whereas southern populations show higher adaptive potential and may serve as genetic sources for assisted gene flow. Together, our study provides a genomic framework for understanding adaptation and guiding conservation under climate change.

papers.title: TSMCA-Net: A Multi-Granular Cross-Attention Framework for Cross-Session EEG-fNIRS Decoding.
papers.abstract: We propose TSMCA-Net, a lightweight cross-session EEG-fNIRS decoder that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with <1M parameters-70.6% fewer than the strongest baseline-while maintaining sub-8ms inference latency. TSMCA-Net decomposes multimodal interactions into three complementary views-temporal-spatial (TS), temporal-modal (TM), and spatial-modal (SM)-through structured multi-view factorization that separates heterogeneous dependency axes while preserving cross-branch information sharing. A Dynamic Multi-Scale Context module adaptively aggregates spatial dependencies on a unified scalp topology, while a causal lag modeling strategy captures delayed hemodynamic responses under strict temporal causality. An asymmetric cross-attention mechanism then integrates the multi-granular representations for role-aware fusion. Under a leave-one-session-out protocol on two public datasets, TSMCA-Net achieves the highest mean accuracy across three cognitive paradigms (71.41% MI, 86.36% MA, 80.30% WG), outperforming all 12 baselines in absolute accuracy and achieving statistical significance in 31 of 36 pairwise comparisons (p<0.05). Perturbation experiments demonstrate 38%-62% smaller accuracy degradation under simulated spatial perturbations.

papers.title: Veterinary Student Experience and Learning Using a 4D Electrocardiogram Simulator.
papers.abstract: Cardiac electrophysiology and electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation present challenges for veterinary and medical education. Various resources and simulators exist to address this challenge. This study investigates the impact on learning and student experience of Epicardio Simulation™-VET in a UK undergraduate veterinary curriculum. This multi-method study invited students at the University of Liverpool School of Veterinary Science to complete a survey, comprising Likert-type and free-text questions, exploring their Epicardio experience. A case-control study used a pre- and post-learning quiz to compare learning gain in a self-directed clinical rotation ECG tutorial between a group learning with Epicardio and one learning with traditional resources. Survey responses were generally positive, with median scores of 4/5, except in response to the statement "Epicardio is easy to navigate" (Mdn 3/5), and "Epicardio workshops should replace traditional lectures" (Mdn 2/5; considerable variability in responses). Students also varied on whether "the tutorials were easy to follow." Thematic analysis identified positive themes around application, clarification, visualization, interactivity, formative assessment, and user-friendliness. Negative themes highlighted technical difficulties including navigation and structure of the software, as well as curricular integration. The case-control study showed learning gains in both groups and no difference between groups before or after the self-directed tutorial. Students valued Epicardio as an additional learning tool and learned equally well with Epicardio and traditional resources in a self-directed format.

papers.title: Integrated systems integrating self-care: Supporting the prevention and mitigation of team member burnout and compassion fatigue.
papers.abstract: Health care providers are among the highest risk professionals in Western culture(s) for burnout and compassion fatigue (BO/CF). Although they report being wholly committed to what they do, they are often overwhelmed by the intensity and volume of their clinical responsibilities and patient panels, workplace and interdisciplinary politics, administrative demands, and a tendency to underreport personal struggles or seek help. Trends show, too, that these sequelae are becoming even more prevalent-not less-over recent years. After reviewing literature for this conceptual article across both behavioral/mental health and biomedical/physical health fields, we determined that conventional wisdom regarding the prevention and mitigation of BO/CF-that is, calling for providers to engage in generic self-care practices like sleep hygiene, physical activity, strategic time management, and appropriate boundary-setting-is not enough. Preventing and mitigating burnout and compassion fatigue through multisystemic approaches is superior to monomodal approaches that focus solely on individual self-care practices. This article expands the scope to integrate baseline individual self-care with empirically supported strategies across other system levels (e.g., workplace teams, operational/administrative care structures) designed to synchronously-and holistically-promote provider health and well-being. Purposeful efforts to attend to BO/CF prevention and mitigation across multiple system levels in integrated care contexts are both indicated and essential. Doing so will promote the health and well-being of our providers and facilitate the delivery of high(est) quality care to the patients and families we serve. papers.journal: Families, systems & health : the journal of collaborative family healthcare

papers.title: Analyzing uncertain decision processes in problematic pornography use: ERP insights into decision evaluation and feedback processing.
papers.abstract: Individuals with Problematic Pornography Use (PPU) continue engaging in excessive pornography use despite awareness of its adverse consequences, suggesting a knowledge-behavior dissociation potentially driven by decision-making deficits. The present study aimed to disentangle decision evaluation and feedback processing as potential contributors to maladaptive decision-making in individuals at risk for PPU using event-related potentials (ERP) during a modified Iowa Gambling Task (IGT). Eighty male participants (40 PPU risk, 40 controls) completed a pass-play variant of the IGT in which all four decks were presented on each trial, with one deck preselected, requiring participants to decide whether to play or pass that option, while EEG was recorded. Behavioral performance was analyzed using linear mixed models to capture learning trajectories, focusing on changes in approach toward advantageous decks and avoidance of disadvantageous decks across blocks. ERP components indexing distinct decision stages were examined, including decision P3, decision preceding negativity (DPN), feedback-related negativity (FRN), and feedback P3. Behaviorally, individuals at risk for PPU showed a reduced decline in disadvantageous choices across blocks, suggesting slower adaptation to disadvantageous options, while learning for advantageous choices remained intact. At the neural level, the PPU risk group exhibited attenuated P3 amplitudes during both decision evaluation and feedback processing stages, without significant modulation by choice type or feedback valence. These findings suggest that maladaptive behavior in individuals at risk for PPU may arise from inefficient integration of value-related information across decision and feedback stages, providing a neurocognitive account of the dissociation between knowledge and behavior.

papers.title: Psychoeducational interventions for children and adolescents with potentially traumatic experiences: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Background: Children and adolescents with potentially traumatic experiences (PTEs; e.g. violence, severe injuries, displacement) are at considerable risk for psychological distress. Psychoeducation is frequently used to reduce stress and enhance coping; however, evidence of its effectiveness for PTEs, particularly as a stand-alone intervention, remains inconclusive.Objective: This systematic review aimed to summarise existing evidence on stand-alone psychoeducational interventions for children and adolescents with PTEs, focusing on three child outcomes: trauma-related knowledge, psychopathological symptoms and disorders, and psychosocial functioning.Method: A systematic search was conducted in six databases, following PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024532660). We included peer-reviewed experimental and observational studies investigating psychoeducation delivered as a stand-alone intervention to children and adolescents exposed to PTEs, either directly or through caregivers, with a focus on child outcomes.Results: Out of 9,214 records screened for title and abstract, 114 were eligible, and seven met inclusion criteria (k = 7). Interventions were delivered in print, digital, or in-person formats across hospital and school settings. Two studies reported improvements in knowledge of posttraumatic stress disorder and posttraumatic growth, while one showed no effect. Among five studies on psychopathological symptoms, two suggested reduced anxiety and one suggested reduced posttraumatic stress symptoms in highly distressed children, while the remaining findings, including on sleep disturbances, depression, anger, and dissociation, were not significant. One study indicated improved psychosocial functioning. No studies addressed interpersonal or complex trauma, highlighting evidence gaps.Conclusions: These sparse and mixed findings call for further research on the short- and long-term effects of stand-alone psychoeducation. Based on the current evidence, psychoeducation appears to be a low-threshold and accessible approach with potential preventive value for children and adolescents with PTEs.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence across the continuum of care for the aging musculoskeletal patient: From longitudinal phenotyping to personalized surgery and recovery monitoring.
papers.abstract: Musculoskeletal care is being reshaped by population aging, multimorbidity, frailty, osteoporosis, sarcopenia, polypharmacy and increasing vulnerability to postoperative loss of independence. Artificial intelligence (AI) has entered orthopaedic research, but its clinical translation remains constrained. Many models address isolated diagnostic, imaging or short-term prediction tasks rather than the longitudinal care trajectories that determine outcomes in older musculoskeletal patients. The central limitation is therefore not simply whether older adults are represented in datasets, but whether AI systems are valid across the continuum of geriatric orthopaedic care. This review argues for a transition from task-specific orthopaedic AI toward continuum-of-care AI for the aging musculoskeletal patient. Upstream, radiomics, longitudinal osteoarthritis phenotyping, opportunistic computed tomography (CT)-based skeletal assessment and AI-augmented dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) modelling may improve prediction of disease progression, fracture risk, treatment failure and surgical timing. At the point of intervention, AI-assisted arthroplasty planning may help move total knee arthroplasty from generic alignment targets toward phenotype-specific reconstruction strategies that account for constitutional alignment, bone morphology, ligament envelope, neuromuscular control, frailty and functional reserve. Perioperatively, automated frailty and sarcopenia phenotyping, wearable gait analysis and multimodal temporal models integrating imaging, electronic health records, laboratory data, medications, patient-reported outcomes and wearable signals may support dynamic risk prediction. After discharge, continuous monitoring of mobility, sleep, pain trajectories, wound-related symptoms and rehabilitation adherence may help close the high-risk surveillance gap during the 90-day postoperative episode. However, clinical adoption requires more than high discrimination. Explainable AI should be understood as one component of a broader trust framework that also includes calibration, uncertainty quantification, decision-curve analysis, external and prospective validation, workflow integration, post-deployment monitoring and accountability. The future of orthopaedic AI is not simply better diagnosis or more precise surgery, but longitudinal, multimodal support across the full care continuum: predicting progression, selecting treatment, personalizing surgery, optimizing perioperative care, monitoring recovery and preserving mobility and independence. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV.
papers.journal: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA

papers.title: Pharmacological Interventions for Acute Stress Disorder and for the Prevention and Treatment of Post-traumatic Stress Disorder in Children and Adolescents: A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Traumatic events are common during childhood and adolescence and may lead to acute stress disorder (ASD) or post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), both associated with developmental, cognitive and functional impairment. Although trauma-focused psychotherapies are recommended as first-line treatments, pharmacological interventions are frequently used in clinical practice despite limited evidence in paediatric populations. To review the evidence on pharmacological interventions for the prevention and treatment of paediatric ASD and PTSD, we reviewed the literature published up to December 2025. Eligible studies included participants aged younger than 18 years and evaluated pharmacological interventions targeting ASD, PTSD prevention or PTSD treatment. After screening and a full-text review, 75 publications were included. Given the methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesised narratively. Evidence for pharmacological interventions in paediatric trauma-related disorders remains limited and heterogeneous. For PTSD prevention, only limited data support sertraline and, in the context of ASD, imipramine. Limited data also suggest that opioids used for pain management after trauma may reduce subsequent PTSD risk. Early opioid (morphine) exposure for pain management was also associated with lower subsequent severity symptoms in observational paediatric burn studies. Evidence for PTSD treatment is weaker. Anticonvulsants (sodium valproate, carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, lamotrigine), antipsychotics (clozapine, quetiapine, aripiprazole), glutamatergics (D-cycloserine, ketamine, ifenprodil), propranolol and cannabidiol do not appear to provide sufficient benefit for routine use. Alpha-adrenergic agents (prazosin, clonidine, guanfacine) have shown preliminary signals of benefit, particularly for hyperarousal and trauma-related sleep disturbances. However, these findings are based on non-randomised and uncontrolled studies. Antidepressants (sertraline, citalopram) show mixed results; among them, citalopram was associated with symptomatic improvement in one small open-label study and one case series. These findings should be considered preliminary and hypothesis generating. No pharmacological treatment has sufficient evidence to warrant routine recommendation for paediatric PTSD and ASD. Pharmacotherapy should therefore be considered only as an adjunct to trauma-focused psychotherapy in selected clinical situations. Further randomised controlled trials are needed.

papers.title: Measures of Overall Illness Severity and Burden for ME/CFS: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Consensus has not been established on measures of illness severity and burden for Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS), which is characterized by a wide range of symptoms including post-exertional malaise, unrefreshing sleep, and cognitive impairment. A scoping review was conducted to systematically evaluate the measurement of illness severity and burden in individuals with ME/CFS. A literature search was conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines across five academic databases and one patient-organization-led website (with no restrictions on publication date; restricted to English language studies, and excluding review articles). Records were imported into Covidence, a systematic and scoping review data management tool, with studies retained if they evaluated an ME/CFS population and explicitly measured illness severity or illness burden. Information from each source was extracted and relevant measures were evaluated. From the reviewed literature, 190 full-text articles met the final inclusion criteria and were retained for analysis. The most frequently utilized tools for evaluating illness severity and burden in individuals with ME/CFS were the Medical Outcomes Study 36-Item Short-Form Health Survey (SF-36) and the Sickness Impact Profile (SIP). Additional prominent instruments identified across the literature include disease-specific measures such as the DePaul Symptom Questionnaire (DSQ) and generic health-related quality of life indices like the EuroQoL 5-Dimension (EQ-5D-5L). Significant discrepancies persist in how illness severity and illness burden are operationalized in ME/CFS research. The reliance on generic instruments often obscures core symptom domains like post-exertional malaise (PEM), while inconsistent standards limit cross-comparability. Establishing standardized, disease-specifici illness metrics is critical to accurately capturing the true burden of illness and advancing rigorous clinical research.

papers.title: BHLHE40 as a transcriptional rheostat: decoding microenvironmental signals in context-dependent tumor plasticity.
papers.abstract: The basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor BHLHE40 (also known as BHLHB2, DEC1, STRA13) functions as a critical molecular rheostat in cancer biology, exhibiting context-dependent roles that contribute to tumor plasticity. This review synthesizes current knowledge of BHLHE40, with emphasis on its structural features, including DNA binding, dimerization, and regulatory domains, as well as its integration of key physiological signals, such as circadian rhythm regulation, hypoxic adaptation, cellular senescence, and immune modulation. Pancancer analyses indicate that BHLHE40 expression is dysregulated across multiple tumor types. Elevated expression is associated with poor prognosis in cancers such as glioblastoma, acute myeloid leukemia, and ovarian cancer, whereas it correlates with favorable outcomes in breast and kidney cancers. Notably, the functional role of BHLHE40 is highly tissue-dependent. It promotes tumor progression in hepatocellular carcinoma, gastric cancer, colorectal cancer, and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma by enhancing proliferation, invasion, migration, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and therapeutic resistance. In contrast, BHLHE40 exhibits tumor-suppressive effects in prostate cancer by inducing cellular senescence, and in endometrial cancer by inhibiting EMT. The tumor microenvironment plays a pivotal role in modulating BHLHE40 activity, with factors such as hypoxia, cytokine signaling, and immune cell interactions shaping its oncogenic or tumor-suppressive functions. Importantly, its role in maintaining CD8+ T-cell effector function during immune checkpoint blockade highlights its therapeutic potential. However, the context-dependent duality of BHLHE40 presents significant challenges for clinical targeting. Emerging therapeutic strategies, including targeted protein degradation approaches and advanced tumor models such as patient-derived organoids, offer promising avenues for intervention. Future studies integrating multi-omics data and spatial transcriptomics will be essential to fully elucidate the role of BHLHE40 and to harness its potential as a biomarker and therapeutic target for overcoming tumor progression, therapeutic resistance, and immune evasion.

papers.title: Social jetlag in a longitudinal Chinese wearable cohort: weekly variation, solar-time mismatch, and sleep-activity associations.
papers.abstract: To examine how sleep-corrected social jetlag (SJLsc) varied with work-rest schedules and solar time zone and how it was associated with sleep, physical activity, and nocturnal heart rate variability (HRV). Wearable-device and questionnaire data from 63,752 adults contributing 2,037,507 person-weeks were analyzed. SJLsc was the difference in sleep midpoint between workdays and free days, corrected for sleep debt. High SJL was SJLsc > 1 h. Weeks were classified as normal, extended-rest (statutory holidays added), or extended-work (weekend days reassigned as workdays). Provinces were grouped as east, central, or west by solar time offset, the gap between local solar time and China Standard Time. Generalized linear mixed models tested week type and solar offset. Within-person centering was used to separate between- from within-person associations. Median SJLsc was 0.70 h. High SJL was more common by week than by person (25.02% of person-weeks vs 20.25% of participants). High SJL was less likely during extended-rest (OR = 0.844, 95% CI 0.830-0.859) and extended-work weeks (OR = 0.776, 95% CI 0.758-0.794), while short-sleep odds were higher in both. Locations farther west were associated with later sleep and greater SJLsc. Adverse associations of SJL with sleep and physical activity were stronger between people than within people, whereas HRV showed no robust association. Associations of social jetlag with sleep and physical activity were driven mainly by between-person differences. Lower social jetlag during extended-rest and extended-work weeks coexisted with higher odds of short sleep, suggesting that social jetlag should be interpreted alongside sleep duration and schedule context. Social jetlag has been linked to adverse sleep and health outcomes, but prior studies have relied largely on cross-sectional or questionnaire-based measures. Large longitudinal wearable data can test how social jetlag varies across real-world schedules and examine associations between social jetlag and sleep, physical activity, and HRV, with stable person-level differences or week-to-week change clearly defined. In 63,752 Chinese adults, high social jetlag was more common at the week level than at the person level, and lower social jetlag during altered schedules did not necessarily indicate longer or more continuous sleep. Adverse associations with sleep and physical activity were driven mainly by between-person differences, supporting trait-state decomposition in clinical sleep research.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine

papers.title: Fatigue in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: The Role of Drug Therapy Within a Holistic Management Framework.
papers.abstract: Fatigue is one of the most common and disabling symptoms experienced by individuals with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Significant fatigue is experienced by approximately 40-80% of adults with IBD, with higher prevalence during active disease states but persisting in up to one-third of individuals who are in clinical remission. Fatigue is not solely a consequence of disease activity, but rather a unique and multifactorial manifestation of IBD. In this narrative review we synthesize evidence on the various mechanisms of fatigue in IBD, as well as pharmacological agents to address fatigue both directly or through secondary contributors including anaemia, psychiatric comorbidities, sleep disturbance, and pain. The review further situates pharmacological therapy within a holistic framework that integrates non-pharmacological approaches as part of a multidisciplinary approach to fatigue in IBD. Drug therapy has a meaningful role in this context, both when targeting disease-related inflammation and secondary contributors to fatigue. However, the evidence base for most of these approaches remains weak. It is clear that no single pharmacological agent will resolve IBD-related fatigue in isolation, but effective management should identify a patient's dominant contributors and address them systematically with both drug and nondrug intervention strategies. This framework should be delivered by a multidisciplinary team through an integrated care approach and optimally be guided by the patient's priorities and goals.

papers.title: Circadian disruption exacerbates alcohol-induced cardiac injury through impaired cellular quality control and increased cardiomyocyte death.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythms orchestrate 24-h oscillations in physiology and gene expression in many tissues, including the heart. Disruptions to these rhythms have been linked to increased cardiovascular risk and impaired cellular homeostasis. However, the extent to which circadian disruption influences cardiac responses to environmental stressors such as alcohol, remains poorly understood. Herein, we performed RNA-sequencing and transcriptomic analysis on hearts from C57BL/6 J mice exposed to alcohol for ten weeks and collected at two distinct circadian time points (Zeitgeber Time (ZT)8 and ZT20). Principal component analysis and differential expression profiling revealed robust time-of-day-dependent transcriptional programs induced by alcohol, with significant enrichment of pathways governing mitochondrial quality control, autophagy/mitophagy, ferroptosis, and key signaling nodes (FOXO, MAPK, AMPK, mTOR, HIF, Hippo). To investigate the impact of circadian disruption, we compared alcohol-challenged hearts from circadian disrupted and control mice. Circadian disruption markedly altered transcriptional profiles and pathways associated with cardiomyopathy and insulin resistance, while further amplifying dysregulation of quality control and stress signaling networks. At the cellular level, alcohol exposure reduced autophagosome formation in isolated adult cardiomyocytes and this decrease was exacerbated by circadian disruption. Further, circadian disruption impaired mitochondrial quality control by reducing ATP production, altering mitophagy, and mitochondrial dynamics, resulting in mitochondrial dysfunction. These alterations were accompanied by increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and elevated apoptotic cell death compared with either condition alone. Altogether, these findings demonstrate that circadian disruption exacerbates alcohol-induced molecular and cellular cardiac injury by compromising cellular quality control processes, mitochondrial integrity, and cell survival pathways. These findings identify mechanisms that may contribute to increased susceptibility to alcohol-induced cardiac dysfunction and may offer novel approaches to mitigate alcohol-related cardiac injury in shift-workers or individuals with disrupted circadian rhythms.

papers.title: Are the EQ-5D-5L and EQ-HWB-9 valid instruments for measuring informal carer outcomes for use in economic evaluations?
papers.abstract: Despite growing interest in incorporating informal carer outcomes into economic evaluations, evidence on the performance of utility measures for informal carers remains limited. This study assesses the psychometric performance of the EQ‑5D‑5L and EQ‑HWB‑9 in capturing informal carer outcomes for economic evaluations. This study utilized cross-sectional EQ-DAPHNIE survey data from English‑speaking countries (Australia, Canada, New Zealand, UK, and US) to evaluate the EQ‑HWB‑9 (UK pilot value set) and EQ‑5D‑5L (country‑specific value sets), assessing distributional (i.e., acceptability, distribution, floor and ceiling effects) and construct validity (i.e., convergent and known-group) properties, with subgroup analyses by age and financial situation. There were 6,743 informal carers across Australia (n = 1447), Canada (n = 1265), New Zealand (n = 1435), UK (n = 1337), and US (n = 1259). The EQ-5D-5L showed a ceiling effect (19%), but not the EQ-HWB-9 (5%). Most respondents reported problems (level 2-5) on the EQ-5D-5L pain/discomfort (67%) and anxiety/depression (60%), with anxiety/depression showing the highest proportion with worst (level 5) responses (5%). For the EQ-HWB-9, ≥ 50% reported problems (level 2-5) across all domains except mobility, with ≥ 5% reporting the worst (level 5) responses in exhaustion, loneliness, cognition, sad/depressed, anxious, and control. Both instruments moderately correlated with the WHO-5, PROMIS-10 (physical and mental t-scores), ASCOT-SCT4, OPQOL-brief, PHQ-2, and GAD-2, and demonstrated known-group validity across groups relating to self-reported physical and mental disability, chronic conditions, sleep, social support, impact of caring, psychological wellbeing, and self-reported quality-of-life. Results were consistent in subgroup analyses. This study provides evidence supporting the acceptability and construct validity of the EQ-5D-5L and EQ-HWB-9 in measuring informal carer outcomes for use in economic evaluations. Responsiveness evidence remains limited and warrants further research.
papers.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation

papers.title: A Beginner's Guide to Cardiac Optical Mapping.
papers.abstract: Optical mapping is a high spatiotemporal resolution imaging technique used to study cardiac electrophysiology by recording fluorescent signals that correspond to changes in transmembrane potential, intracellular calcium, and metabolic activity. This review provides a comprehensive guide for beginners, covering the fundamentals of optical mapping system components, including dye selection, optical filters and mirrors, camera specifications, and system configurations. A range of tissue preparations, from single cells to whole hearts, is described, with attention to how preparation type affects experimental design, perfusion methods, and system setup. Pharmacological and computational strategies to reduce motion artifacts are discussed. Electrical stimulation protocols, such as pacing and restitution mapping, are described in the context of arrhythmia induction and rate dependent electrophysiological properties. Technical considerations including system maintenance and troubleshooting are also addressed. Finally, the review outlines current limitations, including dye cytotoxicity, tissue viability, and photobleaching, and explores future directions such as genetically encoded indicators and oxygen-enriched perfusates. This guide aims to equip new users with the foundational knowledge needed to design, perform, and interpret optical mapping experiments.

papers.title: Digital Eye Behaviour Phenotypes and Their Association with Axial Length and High Myopia in Chinese Adolescents.
papers.abstract: Screen exposure is often summarised as total duration, although this aggregate measure obscures important differences in how devices are used. This study sought to identify digital eye behaviour phenotypes and evaluate their associations with axial length (AL) and high myopia. A school-based cross-sectional study of 898 high school students in Shanghai was conducted. The four-class latent class analysis (LCA) used eight questionnaire-derived indicators of device use. Regression models evaluated exploratory cross-sectional associations with AL and high myopia, adjusting for demographic, familial, sleep and school covariates. LCA identified four phenotypes differing by screen purpose, weekday-weekend patterns, viewing distance and visual-break behaviour. The entertainment-dominant, weekend-heavy phenotype (11.5%) had the highest entertainment ratio and weekend concentration. The lower-screen, study-oriented phenotype (15.4%) had the lowest total screen time and the highest study ratio. Adjusted AL point estimates relative to the reference phenotype ranged from -0.25 to -0.02 mm. The lower-screen, study-oriented phenotype had nominally higher odds of high myopia (adjusted odds ratio = 1.90; 95% CI, 1.06 to 3.39; p = 0.03). This association was attenuated in the attention-check-correct subset. Mean AL was 24.83 ± 1.20 mm; mean worse-eye spherical equivalent was -3.35 ± 2.36 D and 115 students (12.8%) had high myopia. Four digital eye-behaviour phenotypes captured multidimensional exposure heterogeneity beyond total duration. These profiles provide a framework for prospective studies of whether behaviour combinations relate to refractive development beyond total duration.
papers.journal: Ophthalmic & physiological optics : the journal of the British College of Ophthalmic Opticians (Optometrists)

papers.title: Letter to the Editor Regarding: "Upper airway dimensions in pediatric obstructive sleep-disordered breathing: a systematic review and meta-analysis".
FAM43B mediates BMAL1-driven regulation of ERK signaling to promote cervical cancer progression.
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer is a common malignant tumor of the female reproductive system, and patients with advanced and metastatic diseases have poor prognosis. It is urgent to explore novel molecular targets and regulatory mechanisms. As a core circadian rhythm factor, BMAL1 exerts tumor-suppressive or oncogenic effects in various malignancies, while its biological functions, downstream pathways and molecular mechanisms in cervical cancer remain largely unclear. In this study, human cervical cancer cell lines SiHa and HeLa, as well as nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft models were used as research systems. A series of experiments including transcriptome sequencing, protein interaction assay, ubiquitination detection, cellular functional experiments and in vivo animal assays were performed. The results demonstrated that BMAL1 knockdown markedly inhibited the proliferation, colony formation, invasion and migration of cervical cancer cells, and induced G1-phase cell cycle arrest. Transcriptome sequencing and KEGG pathway enrichment analysis identified the ERK signaling pathway as the major downstream pathway of BMAL1, and BMAL1 positively regulated the phosphorylation of key molecules in the ERK pathway. Mechanistically, BMAL1 specifically bound to FAM43B via its transactivation domain (TAD), promoted K63-linked ubiquitination of FAM43B, enhanced the protein stability of FAM43B. As a downstream effector, FAM43B unidirectionally activated the ERK signaling pathway, and no reverse regulatory loop existed between the two proteins. Silencing FAM43B significantly reversed the malignant phenotypes of cervical cancer cells. In vivo xenograft experiments further verified that BMAL1 knockdown suppressed tumor growth, reduced tumor proliferative activity. In summary, BMAL1 regulates the ERK signaling pathway by modulating the ubiquitination of FAM43B, thereby promoting the progression of cervical cancer. This study reveals a novel BMAL1/FAM43B/ERK regulatory axis and its underlying mechanism, providing potential molecular targets and experimental evidence for prognostic evaluation and targeted therapy of cervical cancer.

papers.title: Cannabinoids and sleep bruxism: mechanistic rationale, polysomnographic evidence, and future research directions.
papers.abstract: Sleep bruxism (SB) is masticatory muscle activity during sleep, most often studied through its polysomnographic marker, rhythmic masticatory muscle activity (RMMA). Cannabinoids have attracted interest for their analgesic, anxiolytic and sleep-modulating properties, but whether they influence SB, and whether such modulation would benefit patients, remains unclear. This review examines cannabidiol (CBD), tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabinol (CBN) in relation to sleep, arousal and masticatory muscle activity, and separates what has been demonstrated from what is inferred. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and Web of Science for records published between 1 January 2004 and 14 June 2026, with searches last run on 14 June 2026. Cannabinoid terms were crossed with sleep terms and with bruxism terms, and searched independently for mechanistic literature. Seminal earlier work was retrieved by hand-searching reference lists. Each source was classified by level and directness of evidence. Meta-analytic evidence indicates that cannabis administration at therapeutic doses does not consistently alter total sleep time, sleep onset latency, sleep efficiency or sleep staging. A randomised polysomnographic trial of CBN missed its primary endpoint (wake after sleep onset); in uncorrected secondary and tertiary analyses, 300 mg reduced the electroencephalographic arousal index and sleep onset latency and increased N2 sleep. Preclinical polysomnography supports a hypnotic action of CBN and of its brain-penetrant metabolite, with partial tolerance within two weeks. One randomised trial reported that topical CBD reduced a portable device bruxism index and masseter activity in patients with SB and painful temporomandibular disorders, through a proposed local mechanism involving myorelaxation and analgesia. The entire direct clinical evidence base comes from a single research group, and no study has measured RMMA by polysomnography under any cannabinoid. Two distinct pathways could link cannabinoids to SB, one peripheral and one central, and neither has been demonstrated in patients with SB. The clinically relevant question is not whether a cannabinoid lowers a motor activity index, but whether it improves outcomes that matter in patients whose SB carries consequences. Trials combining polysomnography, masseter electromyography and patient-centred outcomes are required before any clinical recommendation. Not applicable (narrative review).

papers.title: Ambulatory blood pressure characteristics and left ventricular hypertrophy in untreated children with primary hypertension.
papers.abstract: To identify clinical and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM)-derived factors associated with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) in untreated children and adolescents with primary hypertension. This retrospective study included 306 untreated patients aged 9-17 years with newly diagnosed primary hypertension. LVH was defined as a left ventricular mass index ≥ 45 g/m^2.16. Propensity score-based overlap weighting was used to balance demographic and obesity-related characteristics between patients with and without LVH. Weighted logistic regression was performed to evaluate clinical, laboratory, and ABPM-derived factors associated with LVH. LVH was present in 89 patients (29.1%). Grade 2 office hypertension was the strongest factor associated with LVH (OR 4.22, 95% CI 2.29-7.77; P < 0.001). Selected metabolic and inflammatory markers showed exploratory associations with LVH. Among continuous ABPM parameters, nighttime mean diastolic blood pressure was associated with LVH (OR 1.54 per 10-mmHg increase, 95% CI 1.02-2.31), although this association was lost after adjustment for hypertension grade. In contrast, a systolic non-dipper pattern remained associated with LVH after adjustment for hypertension grade (OR 2.83, 95% CI 1.18-6.80; P = 0.020). LVH was common among untreated children with primary hypertension, with office HTN severity being the predominant associated factor. Abnormal circadian BP patterns may provide complementary information for identifying children with LVH. • Left ventricular hypertrophy is a common form of cardiac target-organ damage in children with primary hypertension. • Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring provides information on nocturnal blood pressure and circadian patterns beyond office blood pressure. • In untreated children, grade 2 office hypertension was the factor most strongly associated with left ventricular hypertrophy. • A systolic non-dipping pattern remained associated with left ventricular hypertrophy after adjustment for hypertension severity, suggesting additional value of circadian blood pressure assessment.

papers.title: Evaluation of sleep-related breathing disorders and polysomnography findings in pediatric patients with achondroplasia.
papers.abstract: To describe sleep-disordered breathing in children with achondroplasia at their first polysomnography (PSG) assessment and examine associations with clinical characteristics. This retrospective study included 49 children evaluated between March 2016 and February 2025. Obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS) was classified using the obstructive apnea-hypopnea index (oAHI). Total AHI was compared according to sex, upper airway surgery history, foramen magnum stenosis, and vosoritide treatment. Infant findings were also presented separately because severity thresholds require cautious interpretation at this age. Median age was 4.48 years (range, 0.22-16.15). OSAS was identified in 39 children (79.6%); 25 (51.0%) met the study criteria for moderate-to-severe disease. Of 15 children without reported sleep-related symptoms, 12 (80.0%) had OSAS, including seven (46.7%) with moderate-to-severe disease. Three children had a central apnea index ≥ 5 events/hour, and two (4.1%) had nocturnal hypoventilation. Total AHI did not differ significantly by sex, surgery history, or foramen magnum stenosis. Median total AHI was 3.2 events/hour in children receiving vosoritide and 6.9 in those not receiving treatment (p = 0.105). OSAS was common at the first PSG assessment and was also found in children without reported symptoms. These findings support objective sleep assessment in achondroplasia. The retrospective design and age-dependent interpretation of infant PSG limit conclusions about prevalence and severity; the study cannot establish a respiratory effect of vosoritide. • Achondroplasia increases the risk of obstructive and central sleep apnea. • Reported symptoms may not reliably identify sleep-disordered breathing. • At first PSG, 12/15 children without reported symptoms had OSAS; 7 had moderate-to-severe disease. • Total AHI did not differ significantly by vosoritide treatment status.

papers.title: [The role of physical activity in obesity prevention].
papers.abstract: Obesity is a chronic, multifactorial disease whose development is influenced by genetic, neuroendocrine, psychosocial and environmental factors as well as physical inactivity. Therefore, physical activity is a central pillar in the prevention and treatment of obesity. As well as increasing energy expenditure, it affects muscle mass, insulin sensitivity, fat metabolism, inflammatory processes, mental health, sleep and functional capacity. This narrative review summarises current guidelines, meta-analyses and representative monitoring data on the role of physical activity across the lifespan with regard to both prevention and treatment.In terms of prevention, general and age-specific physical activity recommendations for moderate and vigorous activity and the reduction of prolonged periods of sitting apply. In terms of treatment, weight loss achievable through exercise alone is usually moderate in adults. However, physical activity is independently associated with significant improvements in body composition, fitness, metabolic health, mobility and quality of life.From a public health perspective, promoting physical activity also requires environmental approaches, such as safe walking and biking paths, attractive and accessible spaces for physical activity, activity-friendly educational and work environments, and healthcare services that avoid stigmatization. Physical literacy-as a competency-based construct comprising motivation, self-confidence, physical competence, knowledge and understanding-can help to establish physical activity as a long-term resource for health and well-being, rather than merely as a means of preventing weight gain or losing weight.

papers.title: Optimized Cardiorespiratory State at Tone Onset Enhances Sensory Responses but Not Associative Learning in Healthy Adults.
papers.abstract: Previous studies suggest that when a tone-conditioned stimulus (CS) predicting an airpuff towards the eye is presented at diastole during expiration, both sensory responses to the CS and trace eyeblink conditioning (TEBC) are enhanced. However, not all participants learn and individual variation in the body-brain relationship remains overlooked. We studied whether timing the CS based on an individually optimized bodily state enhances sensory responses and TEBC. We assumed so, as sensory response magnitude reflects attention and stimulus salience: A salient CS should facilitate TEBC. Forty-one young adults and 19 older adults completed a passive auditory task while electrocardiogram, respiration and electroencephalogram were recorded. The cardiorespiratory state associated with the largest N1-P2 response was identified individually. Optimal states varied across participants and did not differ between age groups. Participants underwent TEBC at their optimal state (Personalized) or at diastole during expiration (Control). As expected, the CS evoked a larger N1-P2 response in the Personalized than the Control group. However, conditioned responding, peak performance, and learning rate, or the proportion of good learners did not differ between groups. Older adults learned more slowly, made fewer conditioned responses, and were less aware of the tone-airpuff association than young adults. These findings tentatively suggest that enhancing early sensory processing of the CS may not improve TEBC, although the low reliability of the individually determined optimal state limits this conclusion. Future studies should examine whether timing external stimuli to specific bodily states effectively influences behaviour in tasks that rely on rapid sensory processing.

papers.title: GBA1 Canada initiative (G-can), a pre-competitive, open science platform for GBA1 research.
papers.abstract: GBA1 Canada (G-Can) is a pre-competitive, open-science platform serving as a central hub for basic, translational, and clinical research on GBA1, which encodes the lysosomal enzyme acid beta-glucocerebrosidase (GCase), a key component of the glycosphingolipid metabolism pathway. G-Can unites basic scientists, clinicians, and industry partners in Canada and internationally to minimize duplication of effort and maximize research impact. G-Can has established a comprehensive and growing suite of biological, clinical, and analytical resources for the GBA1 research community. Through the C-BIG Repository and partner infrastructures, these resources are made broadly accessible to academic and industry investigators under non-exclusive agreements, in accordance with G-Can's open-science mandate. G-Can's primary objectives are to deepen understanding of GCase biology and its genetic modifiers, validate disease-relevant biomarkers, and establish trial-ready cohorts exceeding 5000 genotyped participants. Therapeutic programs under development include gene therapy, RNA-based approaches, and combination strategies, with a Phase 0/1 clinical trial targeted within five years. By integrating open-science infrastructure with coordinated therapeutic development, G-Can aims to accelerate the translation of discovery into clinical application for patients with GBA1-associated neurodegeneration.

papers.title: The Clinical Impact of Periodic Limb Movements During Sleep (PLMS): Under-Recognition in Sleep Disordered Breathing and Associations with Key Clinical Outcomes in 481,857 Patients.
papers.abstract: To evaluate periodic limb movements during sleep (PLMS) in a large sleep disorders cohort and explore associations with sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), demographics and key clinical comorbidities. A retrospective analysis including 481,857 adults who completed overnight polysomnography (PSG) and a sleep/medical history questionnaire. Data collection spanned 240 sleep centers across 30 U.S. states. Periodic limb movement index (PLMI) was calculated from technician-scored PSGs, and all PSG measures were scored in accordance with American Academy of Sleep Medicine guidelines. Associations with PLMI were assessed using multivariable linear regression, with self-reported and objective measures analyzed separately, first in predictor-specific and then in simultaneous models. The sample included 54.1% males, with a mean age of 54.4 ± 14.4 years (range: 18-107), average PLMI of 10.3 ± 22.1 events/hour and average Apnea Hypopnea Index (AHI) of 14.7 ± 19.1 events/hour. PLMI was highest among White individuals; lower among Hispanic, Asian, and Black individuals. PLMI was strongly negatively associated with SDB measures, persisting even when stratified by CPAP usage.In both predictor-specific and simultaneous multivariable models, PLMI was associated with diagnosed depression, insomnia score, elevated blood sugar and anemia. Objectively, PLMI was associated with arousal index and lower sleep efficiency. Our findings highlight the potential clinical relevance of PLMS across neuropsychiatric, cardiometabolic, and sleep domains. Racial disparities may reflect genetic and sociocultural factors. Most strikingly, in the setting of increased SDB, PLMS may be undercounted, potentially warranting further evaluation of scoring criteria. These results support further genetic and mechanistic investigations.

papers.title: Impact of Music as Environmental Enrichment on Chronic Stress and Anxiety-Related Responses in Broiler Chickens.
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the effects of classical music as auditory environmental enrichment on chronic stress and anxiety-related responses in broiler chickens. Two hundred Cobb 500 chicks were assigned to a control group (no enrichment) or an enriched group exposed to classical music for 6 h daily from 1 to 40 days of age. At 40 days, affective states were assessed using the attention bias test (ABT), while chronic stress was evaluated through feather corticosterone (CORT) concentrations. Music-exposed birds had significantly lower feather CORT concentrations than controls (p < 0.0001), indicating reduced chronic stress. No significant treatment effects were detected for ABT behavioral measures. However, music-exposed birds showed a numerically longer latency to take the first step (p = 0.055), although this difference did not reach statistical significance. Overall, these findings demonstrate that classical music enrichment can reduce physiological indicators of chronic stress in broilers, while evidence for effects on anxiety-related behavior remains inconclusive. The results suggest that auditory enrichment may help reduce chronic stress in broilers under the conditions evaluated and highlight the need for further replicated studies to clarify its effects on affective states and behavioral responses.
papers.journal: Animal science journal = Nihon chikusan Gakkaiho

papers.title: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline: Management of Menopause-Related Vasomotor, Sleep, and Mood Symptoms.
papers.abstract: To provide evidence-based recommendations for the management of vasomotor, sleep, and mood symptoms related to spontaneous menopause and induced menopause (at or beyond age 40 years). Perimenopausal and postmenopausal individuals assigned female sex at birth (ie, women, transgender men, and gender-diverse individuals) with vasomotor, sleep, and mood symptoms related to spontaneous or induced menopause. This guideline was developed using an a priori protocol in conjunction with a writing team consisting of a subspecialist in reproductive endocrinology and infertility, a Menopause Society Certified Practitioner and subspecialist in reproductive endocrinology and infertility, and a specialist in obstetrics and gynecology. Studies that moved forward to the full-text screening stage were assessed by two authors from the writing team based on standardized inclusion and exclusion criteria. Included studies underwent quality assessment, and a modified GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) evidence-to-decision framework was applied to interpret and translate the evidence into recommendation statements. This Clinical Practice Guideline includes recommendations on pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic interventions for the management of menopause-related vasomotor, sleep, and mood symptoms. Recommendations are classified by strength and evidence quality. Ungraded Good Practice Points are included to provide clinical guidance when a formal recommendation could not be made because of inadequate or nonexistent evidence.
authors: American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists' Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines–Gynecology

papers.title: Tetraethylammonium-Sensitive ventricular repolarization in diabetic rat myocardium: effects of rosiglitazone.
papers.abstract: To examine ventricular action-potential responses to tetraethylammonium (TEA), a non-selective potassium-channel blocker, in streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats and determine whether rosiglitazone modifies these responses. Male Wistar rats were assigned to Control (C), Control plus Rosiglitazone (C+RSG), Diabetic (D), or Diabetic plus Rosiglitazone (D+RSG) groups. Diabetes was induced with streptozotocin (45 mg/kg, intravenous). Resting membrane potential (RMP), action potential amplitude (APA), and half-repolarization time (½RT) were recorded from isolated left ventricular papillary muscles before and after TEA administration (2 mmol/L). At week 8, blood glucose was 563 ± 29 mg/dL in diabetic rats and 98 ± 6 mg/dL in controls (p < 0.001). Rosiglitazone reduced the diabetic value to 336 ± 25 mg/dL (p < 0.05 vs. D). TEA increased ½RT from 18 ± 1 to 38 ± 2 ms in controls (+20 ms) and from 60 ± 3 to 65 ± 3 ms in diabetic myocardium (+5 ms). Diabetic preparations had higher post-TEA ½RT because repolarization was prolonged at baseline; however, the absolute TEA-associated increment was smaller than in controls. TEA also increased APA in untreated control and diabetic preparations. Diabetes was associated with marked baseline prolongation of ventricular repolarization. The smaller absolute ½RT increment in diabetic myocardium does not support enhanced TEA responsiveness. Because TEA is non-selective, the findings reflect an integrated response to TEA-sensitive potassium conductances rather than dysfunction of a specific current subtype. Rosiglitazone modified selected electrophysiological responses without normalizing diabetic repolarization.

papers.title: Participant experience with the SpaceLabs 90227 ambulatory blood pressure monitor and SOMNOmedics ABPMpro device.
papers.abstract: Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) is recommended for confirming hypertension and assessing out-of-office blood pressure (BP). However, patient burden and device tolerability may limit broader implementation. We compared participant experience with a traditional oscillometric ABPM device and a compact cuff-integrated ABPM. The PRO-BP Study was a pilot randomized crossover study of 20 adults in New York City. Participants completed two 24-h ABPM periods over 7 days using the SpaceLabs 90227 and SOMNOmedics ABPMpro devices. After each period, participants rated comfort, pain, sleep interference, embarrassment, noise, skin irritation, and interference with daytime activities. Both devices achieved guideline-based recording-quality thresholds. Compared with SpaceLabs, ABPMpro was associated with greater comfort [median: 7.0 (interquartile range - IQR: 5.0-8.5) vs. 3.5 (IQR: 2.0-6.5); P = 0.026] and less pain [1.5 (0-3.5) vs. 5.0 (0.5-7.0); P = 0.022]. Other experience ratings did not differ significantly. Participant experience should be considered alongside recording quality when evaluating validated ambulatory BP monitoring technologies.

papers.title: The influence of health conditions, lifestyle factors, and stress on seafarers' self-rated health - a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Self-rated health (SRH) is a validated holistic indicator of health, yet evidence among seafarers is limited. We examined how health conditions and lifestyle factors relate to poor SRH and whether perceived stress modifies these associations in active-duty seafarers. A total of 22,432 international seafarers who were on board were included in the analysis of an electronic survey distributed via 52 shipping and manning companies in February-March 2024. An 82-item questionnaire assessed SRH, self-reported health conditions, lifestyle factors (physical activity, sleep/feeling rested, smoking, alcohol risk, loneliness, screen time), and perceived stress. Cross-sectional analyses used descriptive statistics and logistic regression. Models were adjusted for age, sex, rank, and time on board; stress was added as an independent predictor. Additive interactions between stress and lifestyle factors were evaluated using relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI). Poor SRH was strongly associated with multimorbidity and selected conditions, particularly depression/anxiety, gastrointestinal issues, and musculoskeletal issues. In fully adjusted lifestyle models, sedentary behavior, not feeling rested, smoking, loneliness, and excess screen time remained associated with poor SRH, while alcohol risk was not. Stress was independently associated with poor SRH and amplified the effects of not feeling rested, loneliness, and excess screen time. Self-rated health captured a combined burden of physical and mental symptoms as well as recovery--related and psychosocial factors relevant to life at sea. The stress-sensitive clustering of poor sleep/rest, loneliness, and high screen time suggests that interventions may be most effective when stress management is integrated with fatigue and social-connection measures. Health conditions and modifiable lifestyle/psychosocial factors were associated with seafarers' SRH, and perceived stress acted as both an independent predictor and an effect modifier. Targeting sleep, stress, social well-being, and sedentary recovery patterns may improve perceived health and potentially safety on board.

papers.title: HDL-related inflammatory biomarkers are associated with sleep disorders: Evidence from a cross-sectional NHANES study.
papers.abstract: Sleep disorders are common and heterogeneous conditions associated with systemic inflammation. They can impair quality of life and increase disease burden. Currently, studies investigating the association between sleep disorders and high-density lipoprotein (HDL)-related inflammatory biomarkers are lacking. This study aimed to explore the associations between HDL-related inflammatory biomarkers and sleep disorders. This study utilized data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES; 2005-2014). Multivariable logistic regression models were applied to explore the associations between HDL-related inflammatory biomarkers, including platelet-to-HDL ratio (PHR), lymphocyte-to-HDL ratio (LHR), neutrophil-to-HDL ratio (NHR), and monocyte-to-HDL ratio (MHR), and the prevalence of sleep disorders and sleep duration. Subgroup analyses were conducted to investigate potential interactions. In addition, the nonlinear relationship between these inflammatory biomarkers and the likelihood of sleep disorders was assessed using restricted cubic spline (RCS) models. Finally, the robustness of the observed associations was examined through sensitivity analyses. A total of 23,045 individuals were included. In the fully adjusted models, higher MHR (odds ratio (OR) = 1.33; 95% confidence interval (95% CI): 1.11-1.60), NHR (OR = 1.25; 95% CI: 1.04-1.49), LHR (OR = 1.24; 95% CI: 1.05-1.48), and PHR (OR = 1.18; 95% CI: 1.00-1.39) were positively associated with an increased prevalence of sleep disorders. The RCS analysis revealed linear relationships between these inflammatory biomarkers and the likelihood of sleep disorders (all p for nonlinearity >0.05). Subgroup analyses indicated that sex and marital status significantly interacted with all 4 indices (all p for interaction <0.05). Compared with individuals with the recommended sleep duration (7-9 h/day), those with short (<7 h/day) and long (>9 h/day) sleep durations had elevated NHR levels. This study revealed a linear association between HDL-related inflammatory biomarkers and sleep disorders. Moreover, sex and marital status modified the associations of all 4 indices with sleep disorders. In addition, these inflammatory biomarkers were associated with sleep duration.
papers.journal: Advances in clinical and experimental medicine : official organ Wroclaw Medical University
keywords: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)

papers.title: Mediating role of sleep in the association between HIV infection and depression: a cross-sectional analysis with NHANES data.
papers.abstract: Depression is a major public health concern and frequently coexists with sleep disturbances, particularly among individuals with Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection. However, it remains unclear to what extent sleep disturbance may account for the observed association between HIV infection and depressive symptoms. This study examined the associations among HIV infection, sleep status, and depressive symptoms and assessed the potential contribution of sleep status. Using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2005-2014 cycles, weighted logistic regression, Firth's penalized regression, Bayesian mediation analysis, and LightGBM with SHAP interpretation were applied. Among 14444 adults, HIV-positive status was associated with higher odds of depressive symptoms, but the association was attenuated and became non-significant after adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, and behavioral factors. Sleep quality showed a graded association with depression, with ORs of 2.17, 5.83, and 13.60 for fair, poor, and very poor sleep. Bayesian mediation analysis suggested that sleep disturbance may explain the association between HIV infection and depressive symptoms. SHAP analysis identified sleep status as the most important predictor of depression. These findings highlight the importance of sleep assessment and management for improving mental health among individuals with HIV infection.

papers.title: Mantra Meditation for Pain Conditions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Pain is biopsychosocial in nature, and international guidelines now emphasise interdisciplinary treatment.
