Psychotherapeutic interventions such as mantra meditation (MM) are being increasingly studied for their potential benefits in pain management. To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis of the evidence for MM in improving biopsychosocial outcomes in acute and chronic pain conditions. A systematic search of MEDLINE, PsycINFO, CINAHL, CENTRAL, EMBASE and Scopus identified controlled clinical trials of MM for acute and chronic pain, with no date limits. Data were synthesised using an inverse-variance random-effects meta-analysis of continuous outcomes with precalculated effect sizes (Hedges' g). Seven studies (n = 374) met inclusion criteria, with low-to-moderate methodological quality. Meta-analyses showed significant effects of MM versus controls for improving mental quality of life (QoL) and reducing negative mood states. No significant effects were found for pain, physical QoL, depression symptoms, anxiety, stress, psychological well-being or sleep. However, subgroup analysis indicated significant improvement in depression symptoms for participants with chronic pain compared with acute pain. Further high-quality randomised controlled trials are required to determine the efficacy of MM in pain management. Current evidence suggests MM may improve selected psychological outcomes, including mental QoL, negative mood states and depression in chronic pain. These findings indicate that MM has potential as an adjuvant intervention within holistic, interdisciplinary approaches to pain management.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence EEG biomarkers for schizophrenia diagnosis: Systematic review with PROBAST+AI assessment.
papers.abstract: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) to resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) data represents a burgeoning frontier in schizophrenia diagnostics. However, the inferential validity of findings is frequently compromised by methodological heterogeneity. This systematic review rigorously evaluates the diagnostic efficacy and methodological robustness of AI-generated EEG biomarkers by implementing the Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool for Artificial Intelligence (PROBAST+AI). Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science identified 43 primary studies encompassing 3,420 patients with schizophrenia or first-episode psychosis and 3,164 healthy controls (total N = 6,584). Methodological quality and validation strategies were assessed using the 34 signaling questions of the PROBAST+AI framework. The aggregate mean diagnostic accuracy across the literature was 93.38%, with deep learning architectures demonstrating superior metrics relative to classical machine learning (96.83% vs. 87.68%). Critically, external validation was restricted to 4.7% of the included studies. A pronounced performance discrepancy was observed between subject-wise (88.22%) and segment-wise (98.14%) validation protocols, indicating pervasive data leakage. Overall, 76.7% of the analyzed studies were characterized by a high risk of bias, predominantly stemming from suboptimal data partitioning and inadequate independent verification. Contemporary diagnostic accuracies appear to be artifactually elevated due to structural methodological deficiencies and data leakage. Consequently, current evidence does not support the immediate clinical implementation of AI-EEG biomarkers in schizophrenia. To facilitate translational progress, we propose a standardized methodological framework optimizing validation strategies.
papers.journal: European psychiatry : the journal of the Association of European Psychiatrists

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation Selectively Alters Cellular Stress Responses During Exercise in the Heat in Young and Older Males.
papers.abstract: Older adults are at heightened risk of heat-related morbidity, particularly in occupational settings where insufficient sleep and heat exposure commonly coincide. Autophagy and other proteostatic pathways are essential for maintaining cellular homeostasis during acute physiological stress; however, whether acute sleep deprivation modifies these responses during exercise-heat stress remains unknown. Ten young (23±3 years) and 10 older (61±4 years) males completed an exercise-heat stress test following normal sleep and after 24 h of total sleep deprivation in which participants performed three 30-min cycling bouts at fixed rates of metabolic heat production (150, 200, and 250 W·m -2), each separated by 15 min rest in the heat (40°C, ~13% relative humidity). Autophagy and related cellular stress pathways were assessed before and after exercise. Sleep deprivation did not alter macroautophagy-related proteins, including LC3-II, the LC3-II/I ratio, ULK1 phosphorylation, or beclin-2 in either age group. However, p62 was reduced at end-exercise in young males following sleep deprivation (p=0.010), whereas the corresponding reduction in older males did not reach statistical significance. Sleep deprivation differentially altered proteins involved in chaperone-mediated autophagy, with LAMP-2A decreasing in young males but increasing in older males (both, p≤0.004). In older males, sleep deprivation reduced HSP90 and increased cleaved-caspase-3 and TNF-α (both, p≤0.048), indicating greater apoptotic and inflammatory signaling. Our findings indicate that 24 h of sleep deprivation does not broadly alter markers of macroautophagy during exercise-heat stress but selectively modifies cellular stress pathways in older males, with distinct responses observed in young and older males.
papers.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise

papers.title: Recombinant bovine αs1-casein ameliorates PCPA-induced insomnia-like behavioral and physiological abnormalities in mice.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is a multifactorial sleep-wake disorder associated with altered neurotransmitter homeostasis, systemic inflammatory changes, and gut microbial dysbiosis. Recombinant bovine αs1-casein (RC) is a scalable milk-protein ingredient, but its effects on insomnia-like physiological and behavioral abnormalities have not been systematically evaluated. We investigated RC in a p-chlorophenylalanine (PCPA)-induced mouse model. Male ICR mice received RC (100, 300, or 500 mg kg-1 day-1), melatonin, Naoxinshu oral liquid, natural casein, or vehicle for 7 days after PCPA modeling. Body weight, open-field behavior, serum cytokines, brain neurotransmitters, hippocampal histology, organ indices, and cecal microbiota were assessed. RC improved body-weight recovery and open-field performance without altering major-organ indices. It increased brain 5-HT, 5-HIAA, dopamine, GABA, and glutamate concentrations and reduced the elevated norepinephrine concentration. High-dose RC reduced serum IL-6 and was associated with better-preserved hippocampal morphology. 16S rRNA gene sequencing showed RC-associated changes in bacterial richness and community structure. The parallel physiological, neurochemical, inflammatory, and microbial changes support an association between RC administration and improvement of PCPA-induced insomnia-like abnormalities. These results identify recombinant bovine αs1-casein as a promising food-derived ingredient for further investigation in sleep-health applications, while the microbiota-gut-brain axis is presented as a testable mechanistic framework rather than a demonstrated causal pathway.

papers.title: Perceptions of Intra-Operative EEG Brain Monitoring During Pediatric Anesthesia Among Children and Parents: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Survey.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) monitoring during pediatric anesthesia may improve perioperative safety by optimizing anesthetic titration and reducing adverse outcomes. However, little is known about patient and caregiver perceptions regarding this technology and its implementation into routine anesthesia care. This study evaluates perceived importance, utility, and extent of reassurance provided by intra-operative EEG monitoring among pediatric patients and their parents. Secondary aims include identifying concerns surrounding general anesthesia (GA), concerns surrounding EEG monitoring, cost and willingness to pay, and sociodemographic and medical factors shaping these attitudes. We conducted an exploratory cross-sectional survey at a tertiary pediatric hospital in Singapore between July 2022 and September 2025. Respondents were parents of children aged 1-18 years and children aged 12-18 scheduled for elective procedures under general anesthesia. A 16-item anonymized questionnaire assessed perceptions of intra-operative EEG monitoring, concerns about anesthesia, and attitudes regarding the cost of EEG monitoring. Of 400 respondents (100 children, 300 parents), 83.5% rated intra-operative brain monitoring as "very" or "quite" important and 93% reported feeling more reassured by its use. Children were most concerned about intraoperative awareness and failure to awaken, whereas parents were most concerned about anesthetic side effects and dosage. Parents with higher education and whose children had prior anesthetic exposure reported greater reassurance from EEG monitoring. Cost was the leading concern regarding EEG monitoring, particularly among parents from families residing in public housing. Despite this, most parents (75%) and children (59%) expressed willingness to pay for EEG monitoring. Pediatric patients and parents viewed intra-operative EEG monitoring as important and reassuring, and expressed willingness to support its implementation despite cost concerns. These findings suggest that families are unlikely to be a major barrier to EEG adoption and highlight the need for clinician- and system-level strategies to integrate EEG monitoring into family-centered pediatric anesthesia care.

papers.title: A cortical pathway to sleep: Role of long-range inhibition.
Prolonged Transcortical Mixed Aphasia Following Awake Glioma Resection: Functional Language Network Disruption Associated with Persistent Epileptiform Activity.
papers.abstract: Aphasia occurring after tumor resection in the language-dominant hemisphere is commonly interpreted as a consequence of irreversible structural injury. In awake craniotomy, intraoperative language mapping enables real-time functional monitoring and is expected to reduce the risk of postoperative aphasia. However, postoperative language impairment is not always attributable to structural damage alone, and functional network disturbances may also contribute. We report a case of prolonged aphasia following awake glioma resection in the dominant hemisphere, in which epileptiform activity was suspected to underlie a prolonged functional disruption of the language network. Intraoperative language mapping confirmed preserved language function throughout tumor resection. However, during the late intraoperative phase, stimulation-induced after-discharges were observed on electroencephalography, followed by the emergence of unstable language output. Postoperatively, severe aphasia persisted despite the absence of new ischemic or hemorrhagic lesions on neuroimaging. Serial electroencephalography demonstrated sustained epileptiform activity within the interictal-ictal continuum, raising concern for possible aphasic status epilepticus. Detailed language assessment revealed severe impairment of spontaneous speech and auditory comprehension, with relative preservation of repetition, reading aloud, and writing. This pattern was consistent with transcortical mixed aphasia, classically described as isolation of the speech area, suggesting functional disconnection of the language network despite anatomical preservation of core language cortices. Although electroencephalographic abnormalities gradually attenuated with antiseizure treatment, language impairment remained prolonged. Prolonged aphasia after awake glioma resection may reflect potentially reversible language network disconnection associated with persistent epileptiform activity rather than structural injury alone, supported by SLTA-confirmed recovery at 6 months.

papers.title: Retinochoroidal structural alterations in obstructive sleep apnea: A spectral domain optical coherence tomography study.
papers.abstract: The purpose of this study was to analyze retinochoroidal parameters in patients with obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS) using spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) and evaluate their relationship with disease severity. This cross-sectional observational study included 60 OSAS patients diagnosed by overnight polysomnography and 60 age-matched healthy controls. The OSAS group was subdivided based on apnea-hypopnea index into mild (n = 18), moderate (n = 28), and severe (n = 14) categories. SD-OCT measurements included retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness, ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GC-IPL) thickness, subfoveal choroidal thickness, and central macular thickness. OSAS patients showed significant thinning in average RNFL (94.7 ± 7.84 μm vs. 98.93 ± 7.67 μm, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.43-7.03, P = 0.003) and GC-IPL thicknesses (80.03 ± 3.11 μm vs. 82.1 ± 2.05 μm, 95% CI: 1.12-3.02, P < 0.001) compared to controls. Severity-based analysis revealed progressive thinning across all parameters, with the strongest correlations observed between disease severity and GC-IPL (r = -0.979) and RNFL parameters (r = -0.922). The most significant differences were consistently found between mild and severe OSAS groups (P < 0.001). Significant retinochoroidal alterations occur in OSAS patients, with changes correlating to disease severity. The distinctive pattern of retinal layer thinning, particularly in superotemporal RNFL and superior GC-IPL, demonstrates an association with OSAS severity.

papers.title: Global Advances in Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation.
papers.abstract: Ventricular tachycardia (VT) is a potentially life-threatening arrhythmia associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, particularly in patients with structural heart disease. Over the past several decades, the management of VT has evolved significantly with the development of catheter-based and noninvasive ablation strategies aimed at eliminating arrhythmogenic myocardial substrates. This review provides a comprehensive overview of global advances in VT ablation, highlighting historical foundations, current therapeutic modalities, and emerging technologies shaping the future of ventricular arrhythmia (VA) management. Radiofrequency ablation remains the cornerstone of VT ablation and has undergone substantial technological refinement through innovations such as irrigated-tip catheters, high-density electroanatomic mapping, contact force sensing, and strategies for achieving deeper myocardial lesions. Alternative catheter-based energy modalities, including cryoablation and the emerging nonthermal technique of pulsed field ablation, provide additional therapeutic options with distinct mechanisms of action and safety profiles. In parallel, procedural advancements such as remote magnetic navigation have improved catheter stability and access to complex ventricular substrates. Beyond traditional catheter ablation, the therapeutic landscape has expanded to include neuromodulatory approaches targeting the cardiac autonomic nervous system, including thoracic epidural anesthesia, stellate ganglion blockade, cardiac sympathetic denervation, and renal denervation. These strategies play an important role in the management of refractory VAs and electrical storm. Furthermore, stereotactic body radiation therapy has emerged as a promising noninvasive treatment for patients with VT who are not candidates for or have failed catheter-based interventions. Additional investigational technologies including laser ablation, microwave ablation, and high-intensity focused ultrasound have been explored in preclinical and limited clinical settings but remain experimental in the context of VT management. Collectively, these evolving technologies underscore the increasingly multimodal approach required to treat complex VAs. In conclusion, VT ablation has progressed from early surgical and direct-current approaches to a sophisticated field incorporating advanced catheter techniques, neuromodulation, robotic navigation, and noninvasive therapies. Continued technological innovation, improved substrate characterization, and integration of emerging tools such as artificial intelligence are expected to further enhance procedural efficacy and patient outcomes. Individualized treatment strategies tailored to patient-specific arrhythmogenic substrates and clinical characteristics remain central to optimizing the management of VT.
papers.journal: The Journal of innovations in cardiac rhythm management

papers.title: Hirayama Disease in A Patient with Loeys-Dietz Syndrome: The First Reported Association.
papers.abstract: Hirayama disease (HD) is a rare, self-limiting cervical flexion myelopathy causing progressive, painless distal upper-limb weakness, typically in young Asian males. Loeys-Dietz syndrome (LDS) is a heritable connective tissue disorder due to TGF-β pathway variants, associated with dural ectasia. Their co-occurrence has not previously been reported. We describe a 23-year-old woman with genetically confirmed LDS type 2 who developed progressive, painless distal upper-limb weakness, initially unilateral and later bilateral. Examination and electrophysiology showed a C7-T1 polyradicular pattern. Dynamic flexion cervical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated anterior displacement of the posterior dural sac at C5-C7, fully reversible on extension, confirming HD. This presentation was atypical for HD (female sex, third-decade onset, bilateral course), yet electrophysiological and dynamic-MRI findings were unequivocal. HD should be considered in patients with heritable connective tissue disease presenting with progressive distal upper-limb weakness, irrespective of sex or age, and dynamic flexion MRI is essential for diagnosis. Hirayama disease should be considered in progressive, painless distal upper-limb weakness even outside its classic demographic (young Asian males), including in women and in patients with an underlying connective tissue disorder.Dynamic (flexion) cervical magnetic resonance imaging is required to demonstrate the anterior dural sac displacement that confirms the diagnosis and avoids unnecessary immunomodulatory treatment.Heritable connective tissue disorders such as Loeys-Dietz syndrome may modify cervical dural biomechanics, and internists should be aware of neuromuscular complications beyond the classical cardiovascular, skeletal and dural manifestations.
papers.journal: European journal of case reports in internal medicine

papers.title: Prevalence and Correlates of Nomophobia and Insomnia Among Health Sciences Students: Evidence From a Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Nomophobia is a behavioral condition characterized by fear or anxiety resulting from inability to access mobile phones. Excessive smartphone use has been associated with psychological and sleep-related disturbances. University students, particularly health sciences students, may be especially vulnerable due to academic stress and high digital exposure. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of nomophobia and insomnia symptoms among health sciences students and to assess the association between nomophobia severity and insomnia symptom severity. A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted among undergraduate health sciences students at Batterjee Medical College (BMC), Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Data were collected using a structured electronic questionnaire including sociodemographic variables, the Nomophobia Questionnaire (NMP-Q), and the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI). A total of 702 participants were included. Descriptive statistics, chi-square test, Spearman's rank correlation, and binary logistic regression analysis were performed. The mean nomophobia score was 77.21 ± 31.7. Overall, 96.6% of participants demonstrated nomophobia, with moderate nomophobia being the most prevalent category (45.3%), followed by severe nomophobia (26.1%). The mean insomnia score was 10.86 ± 5.7, and 71.4% of participants exhibited elevated insomnia symptoms, predominantly at the subthreshold level (46.3%). A statistically significant association was observed between nomophobia and insomnia symptoms (p < 0.001). Using continuous total scores, a weak positive correlation was identified between nomophobia severity and insomnia symptom severity (Spearman's ρ = 0.290, p < 0.001). Female gender was significantly associated with higher nomophobia prevalence (p = 0.014). In multivariable logistic regression analysis treating nomophobia as a continuous predictor, each 10-point increase in NMP-Q score was associated with significantly higher adjusted odds of insomnia symptoms (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 1.20, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.13-1.27, p < 0.001) after adjustment for sociodemographic factors. Nomophobia and insomnia symptoms are highly prevalent among health sciences students. A weak but statistically significant association was observed; however, the cross-sectional design and convenience sampling warrant cautious interpretation. These findings highlight the need for interventions promoting healthy smartphone use and sleep hygiene.

papers.title: Beyond Sleep Perception: Does the Largest WASO Bias Reflect Impaired Memory Rather Than Blunted Perception? [Response to Letter].
Association Between Vitamins Related to Brain Development and Sleep in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
papers.abstract: Sleep problems and nutritional abnormalities are common in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), yet the relationships between specific vitamin status, sleep characteristics, and ASD symptoms remain unclear. This study investigated the associations between neurodevelopment-related vitamin levels, sleep problems, and clinical features in children with ASD. This cross-sectional study included 605 children with ASD aged 2-7 years. Blood vitamin levels were measured using high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Sleep problems were assessed using the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire (CSHQ) and ASD symptoms were evaluated using the Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS), Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS), and Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule-Second Edition (ADOS-2). Vitamin A (VA) deficiency was the most prominent nutritional abnormality, followed by vitamin D (VD) deficiency. VA levels differed significantly by sex, whereas VD levels varied across age groups. Several dimensions of sleep problems showed significant differences according to both sex and age. Lower VA levels were associated with greater sleep problems, including higher bedtime resistance, daytime sleepiness, and higher total CSHQ scores (all P < 0.05). Lower VD levels were associated with greater severity of core ASD symptoms (all P < 0.05), but not with sleep problems. Greater sleep problems were consistently associated with more severe ASD symptoms. VA and VD deficiencies are prevalent among children with ASD. VA levels were associated with sleep problems, whereas VD status was associated with ASD symptom severity. These findings suggest that nutritional status may be associated with specific clinical features of ASD and warrant further investigation in longitudinal studies.

papers.title: Lifestyle, APOE ε4, amyloid burden, and race/ethnicity differences in cognition, mood, and anxiety among cognitively unimpaired older adults.
papers.abstract: We assessed whether lifestyle, race/ethnicity, and apolipoprotein E gene (APOE) ε4 were associated with cognition or mood/anxiety. This secondary cohort analysis used data from the Anti-Amyloid Treatment in Asymptomatic Alzheimer's Disease (A4) Study and the Longitudinal Evaluation of Amyloid Risk and Neurodegeneration (LEARN) cohort. Cognitively unimpaired adults aged 65 to 85 years (n = 1705) reported baseline lifestyle behaviors (summed as healthy lifestyle index [HLI]). APOE ε4 carrier status and amyloid positron emission tomography were assessed at baseline, while cognitive, anxiety, and depressive outcomes were assessed longitudinally. Associations were tested using mixed-effects models. Among Non-Hispanic White participants, higher HLI was associated with fewer depressive symptoms, sufficient sleep was associated with smaller ε4-related increases in anxiety, and excessive alcohol use amplified ε4-related cognitive decline. Among participants from other racial/ethnic groups, walking and higher HLI were associated with more favorable anxiety/depression trajectories. Adequate sleep, limited alcohol, walking, and no smoking may support emotional and cognitive health.
keywords: Anti‐Amyloid Treatment in Asymptomatic Alzheimer's Disease Study

papers.title: Chronotype and Peripheral Clock Genes: Association With Frailty and Insomnia in Mexican Older Adults.
papers.abstract: Frailty is a geriatric syndrome associated with increased vulnerability to adverse health outcomes in older adults. Circadian rhythms regulate multiple physiological processes relevant to aging, including sleep, metabolism, and immune function; however, the relationship between circadian biology and frailty remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to examine associations between chronotype, insomnia, metabolic parameters, and peripheral clock gene expression in Mexican older adults. A total of 751 community-dwelling older adults were included. Chronotype was assessed using the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (MEQ), and associations with insomnia and metabolic parameters were evaluated using multivariate regression models. Peripheral circadian clock gene expression was analyzed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from a subsample of 82 participants using principal component analysis (PCA) and gene-specific linear regression models. Most participants exhibited a morning chronotype. Individuals with an extreme morning chronotype had lower odds of insomnia than those with an intermediate chronotype (adjusted OR = 0.393, 95% CI 0.169-0.827, p = 0.020). No significant associations between chronotype and metabolic parameters remained after adjustment for covariates and correction for multiple comparisons. PCA identified a coordinated pattern of clock gene expression, with pre-frail and frail participants exhibiting lower PC1 scores than robust individuals. Gene-specific analyses showed lower expression of several clock genes in pre-frail and frail participants, while lower CLOCK expression remained significantly associated with pre-frailty after adjustment for chronotype, insomnia, age, sex, and body mass index. In this cohort of older adults, morning chronotype was associated with lower odds of insomnia, whereas frailty was associated with differences in peripheral clock gene expression measured at a morning time point. These findings support a relationship between circadian-related characteristics and frailty in older adults and warrant further investigation using longitudinal and multi-time-point circadian assessments.

papers.title: Frontal theta power prospectively associated with response inhibition.
papers.abstract: A proactive mechanism has been postulated to promote successful inhibition. Specifically, this mechanism is thought to operate before any action-demanding or countermanding event has occurred. In the current study, we investigated whether theta-range oscillatory power measured using electroencephalography (EEG) could reflect this mechanism in a sample of healthy individuals performing a stop-signal task. We tested whether frontal-midline (FM) theta power preceding failed versus successful stop trials predicts inhibition success. Results from two experiments demonstrate that FM theta is indeed higher preceding successful stopping events than failed ones. However, theta power turned out to be equally stronger preceding slow than fast, go trials, suggesting that proactive slowing could explain the association between theta and stop success. There was no correlation between the strength of the within-subject theta-stop-success association and the within-subject theta-RT association. In sum, group-average-level analysis suggests strong overlap between FM theta associated with proactive inhibition and proactive slowing, respectively, while at the same time there are dissociations in terms of individual differences. A further, unexpected, finding was that FM alpha power was specifically associated with proactive inhibition but not with slowing, and, relative to theta, peaked closer in time to the action-demanding event.

papers.title: The late positive component in recognition memory is linked to mnemonic evidence accumulation.
papers.abstract: Recognising objects from memory requires an integration of sensory and mnemonic information. This process has been theorised to occur via a stochastic evidence accumulation process implemented within the parietal cortex. Recent electroencephalographic (EEG) evidence indicates that the widely studied parietal Late Positive Component (LPC) shows characteristics of such a mnemonic accumulation signal. Here, we formally investigated this hypothesis using generative computational modelling that links a trial-level memory strength variable in the Diffusion Decision Model (DDM) with LPC amplitudes prior to the time of the decision. We recorded EEG from 24 participants making recognition judgements based on either studied or novel words. Each participant completed up to three testing sessions. We replicated recent findings that the LPC ramps up and peaks around the time of the decision and corresponding motor response. LPC amplitudes also covaried with accuracy and response time, as expected of a neural correlate of memory strength. By fitting DDMs to LPC amplitudes and behavioural data using specialised neural network tools, we demonstrate that LPC amplitudes are selectively associated with the rate of evidence accumulation, signifying memory strength. This association was stronger for previously studied words compared to novel words, and strongest at the time window immediately prior to the recognition decision. Our findings, therefore, recast the LPC as a neural signature of mnemonic strength linked to the rate of evidence accumulation during recognition memory decisions.

papers.title: Speech-sound memory consolidation over a daytime nap in adults with and without developmental language disorder.
papers.abstract: Sleep plays a critical role in memory consolidation, yet its contribution to the formation of perceptual-linguistic representations remains only partially understood. In the current study, we examined sleep spindles and slow oscillations (SOs) in relation to offline changes in speech-sound memory in adults across a wide range of language ability. Twenty-nine monolingual English-speaking participants completed a perceptual training task contrasting retroflex /ɖ/ and dental /d̪/ consonants, followed by a polysomnography-monitored nap. Slow spindle density was positively associated with perceptual discrimination performance following a nap, whereas slow oscillation (SO) density was negatively associated. SO-slow spindle coupling strength was significantly correlated with language difficulty amongst those with developmental language disorder, such that those with a lower synchronization index were observed with greater difficulties in language ability. Together, these findings point to the potential relationship between sleep and perceptual-linguistic representation, and developmental language disorder.

papers.title: Case Report: Reappearance of spermatozoa following multicomponent lifestyle modification in men with previously diagnosed azoospermia: a case series.
papers.abstract: Azoospermia, defined as the absence of spermatozoa in the ejaculate, is a severe form of male infertility, and the potential effects of intensive lifestyle modification on sperm production remain uncertain. We describe three adult men whose available pre-intervention records reported azoospermia and who undertook a multicomponent lifestyle programme centred on a predominantly raw, whole-food, plant-based diet, prescribed hydration, progressive physical activity, sleep and stress-management guidance, reduced alcohol consumption, and avoidance of ultra-processed and animal-derived foods. Clinical records, serial semen analyses, and available hormonal assessments were retrospectively reviewed. Approximately 10 weeks after programme initiation, spermatozoa were detected in all three participants, with concentrations of 1.6, 2.0, and 2.2 × 106/mL, respectively, at the first sperm-positive assessments; these values remained within a severe oligozoospermic range, and motility and subsequent trajectories varied. Two participants had previously received fertility-directed hormonal therapies, and one had undergone unsuccessful testicular sperm extraction. Participants also reported improvements in body weight, sleep, physical-activity tolerance, libido, perceived energy, and general well-being, with no major adverse events documented. Complete etiologic assessment, genetic testing, objective adherence measures, and uniform documentation of semen-analysis methods were not available for all participants. This uncontrolled case series documents a clinically notable temporal association between initiation of an intensive lifestyle programme and subsequent detection of spermatozoa in men with previously reported azoospermia. Causality cannot be established, and the individual contributions of diet and other programme components remain uncertain. Prospective controlled studies using standardized andrologic assessment, comprehensive etiologic investigation, objective adherence measures, and prespecified reproductive outcomes are warranted.

papers.title: Association between different types of tea consumption frequency and sleep quality with cognitive function among older adults in Qingdao rural area.
papers.abstract: Previous studies have shown that tea consumption frequency or sleep quality is independently associated with cognitive function, but the combined association remains unclear. To investigate the individual and combined associations between tea consumption frequency and sleep quality with cognitive function and analyze whether this association is modified by gender and age. The cross-sectional study involved 646 participants from 17 villages in Jimo District, Qingdao, in 2022. Data on tea consumption frequency were collected via a questionnaire. Cognitive function and sleep quality were assessed through the Montreal Cognitive Assessment and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, respectively. Linear regression models were used to analyze associations, with a combined variable for tea consumption frequency and sleep quality constructed to evaluate their combined association. Stratified analysis and interaction tests assessed the moderating effects of gender and age. Higher consumption frequency of green tea (β (95% CI): 0.97 (0.23, 1.70)) or black tea (β (95% CI): 0.78 (0.08, 1.48)) was positively associated with cognitive function. Moreover, higher consumption frequency of green tea combined with good sleep quality was significantly associated with optimal cognitive function (β (95% CI): 1.17 (0.10, 2.31)). Stratified analysis revealed no significant modifying effects of gender or age on the aforementioned associations. Increased consumption frequency of green tea, alongside maintaining good sleep quality, is associated with enhanced cognitive function. These findings highlight the value of modifiable lifestyle factors in promoting cognitive health.

papers.title: Tolerability of lemborexant for cognitive function and sleep quality in patients with dementia with Lewy bodies.
papers.abstract: We investigated the effects of an orexin receptor antagonist on sleep profiles assessed by actigraphy, and cognitive function in patients with dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB). Thirteen probable DLB patients who were taking an orexin receptor antagonist for insomnia were recruited and underwent actigraphy before and after taking lemborexant. Cognitive function and severity of sleep disturbance were compared before and after taking lemborexant. No significant differences in sleep quality and cognitive function were observed in DLB patients between before and after taking lemborexant. These results suggest the tolerability of lemborexant in patients with DLB.

papers.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of an innovative sleep technology to support individuals who experience sleep problems and worry-related stress: a crossover randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Insomnia and worry-related stress are common problems affecting both mental and physical health. Assistive sleep technologies such as the Somnox 2 may improve sleep quality and reduce stress. This study investigated whether the Somnox improves sleep quality and reduces perceived stress in adults with sleep problems and worry-related stress. A secondary objective was its impact on quality of life. In a 14-week crossover randomized controlled trial, 40 adults (90% female), reporting various types of worries, participated. Each completed two 6-week periods of either Somnox use or no intervention, separated by a 1-day washout. Outcomes were assessed using the Sleep Condition Indicator (SCI), Perceived Stress Scale (PSS), Mental Health Quality of Life (MHQoL), and daily self-reported sleep and stress ratings. Compared with the control condition, Somnox use was associated with higher sleep quality (SCI: +4.22 ± 5.46, 95% CI 2.48 to 5.97, p < 0.001) and lower perceived stress (PSS: -1.80 ± 5.61, 95% CI -3.59 to -0.01, p = 0.049). The SCI finding was supported by a baseline-adjusted first-period sensitivity analysis. Daily sleep scores increased (+0.15 ± 0.33, p = 0.012) and daily stress decreased (-0.11 ± 0.23, p = 0.056). No clear improvements were observed in quality of life. These findings suggest that Somnox is a feasible and promising sleep technology to improve sleep quality and possibly reduce worry-related stress in adults with worries. Future research should explore longer-term effects and diverse subgroups.

papers.title: Smartphone acquisition as an inflection point in early adolescence digital exposome: relevance to mental health.
papers.abstract: Acquisition of the first smartphone represents a major developmental transition. However, evidence on its effects on adolescent health and behavior remains limited. We assessed associations between first smartphone acquisition around age 12 and changes in mental health, environmental and lifestyle (exposomic) factors, and examined potential pathways underlying these associations. We analyzed longitudinal data from 3,486 participants in the U.S. Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study who did not have a smartphone by age 12 (2-year assessment wave). We tested the association between smartphone acquisition (exposure) between age 12 to 13 (the 2- and 3-year assessments) and age 13 self-reported mental health (Brief Problem Monitor [BPM]) and exposomic outcomes including digital (screen time, social media, gaming, streaming, cyberbullying) and offline (sleep duration, school performance, exercise, bullying and reading) measures. Mixed-effects regression models accounted for sociodemographic, family, and developmental covariates. To reduce confounding, models additionally adjusted for pre-exposure measures of each outcome assessed at age 12, prior to smartphone acquisition. Mediation models examined indirect effects of smartphone acquisition on mental health through total screen time, social media account ownership, and bedtime media use. Compared with youth who remained smartphone-free at age 13 (n = 1,940), smartphone acquisition (n = 1,546) was associated with worse BPM internalizing, attention, and total scores (all p's ≤ 0.003), more screen time, greater odds of having a social media account, less sleep, and more frequent bedtime use of social media, video games, and streaming (all p's < 0.001). Smartphone acquisition was not associated with differences in externalizing symptoms, academic performance, exercise, or bullying/cyberbullying (all p's > 0.05). Mediation analyses suggested indirect associations between smartphone acquisition and mental health through total screen time, social media account ownership, and bedtime media use (all indirect effects p ≤ 0.002); collectively, these factors accounted for most of the association, with social media use contributing the largest indirect effect. Smartphone acquisition is associated with several environmental and lifestyle changes in the following year, particularly around bedtime. These changes may represent mechanisms linking smartphone acquisition to mental health symptoms. Findings provide insight into potential behavioral pathways associated with smartphone acquisition and adolescent mental health and may inform future intervention studies.
papers.journal: Frontiers in child and adolescent psychiatry

papers.title: Adjunctive Acorus tatarinowii essential-oil ear-canal packing for idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss: study protocol for a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss (ISSNHL) is an acute otologic emergency, and hearing recovery remains highly variable and frequently unsatisfactory. Acorus tatarinowii Schott has long been used in traditional Chinese medicine to treat hearing impairment and related auditory disorders. Its essential oil (SCP-oil) has demonstrated anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and neuroprotective activities in preclinical studies. Advances in local otologic drug-delivery strategies suggest that administration through the external auditory canal may offer a practical, noninvasive approach to local treatment. This study therefore aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of adjunctive SCP-oil ear-canal packing in patients with ISSNHL. This is a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial to be conducted at Zhejiang Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine. The trial has been registered with the International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry (ITMCTR2026000919). A total of 258 eligible participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive conventional therapy combined with either SCP-oil ear-canal packing or glycerin placebo ear-canal packing for 14 consecutive days. The primary outcome is the study-defined total markedly effective rate of hearing recovery at week 2, defined as the proportion of participants achieving complete recovery or marked improvement, as assessed by pure-tone audiometry. Secondary outcomes include the mean improvement in hearing thresholds across the affected frequencies, the hearing-recovery categories, tinnitus severity measured using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), depressive symptoms assessed using the Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS), and sleep quality assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Efficacy outcomes will be assessed at baseline and week 2, with an additional safety assessment conducted at week 4. Adverse events will be monitored throughout the study. This trial will provide evidence on the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of adjunctive SCP-oil ear-canal packing for ISSNHL, including its effects on hearing recovery and patient-reported outcomes. The findings may also inform the design of future multicenter clinical trials.

papers.title: Effects of individualized phase-amplitude-coupled transcranial alternating current stimulation on tinnitus and cognition.
papers.abstract: Chronic tinnitus is a prevalent and disabling condition that is frequently accompanied by domain-specific cognitive difficulties. Abnormal neural oscillations and disrupted cross-frequency coupling (CFC) have been implicated in its pathophysiology. This study investigated whether individualized phase-amplitude-coupled transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS), tailored to each participant's individual alpha frequency (IAF), was associated with changes in tinnitus symptoms, cognition, and neurophysiological measures. In this prospective single-arm interventional study, 25 adults with chronic tinnitus (>6 months) were enrolled, and 21 completed the protocol. Participants received five sessions of individualized IAF-based phase-amplitude-coupled tACS at 2 mA for 20 min per session. Tinnitus outcomes included the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory (THI) and visual analog scale ratings of loudness (VAS-L) and annoyance (VAS-A). Cognitive performance was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment, Trail Making Tests A and B, Digit Span Tests forward and backward (DST-F/B), and Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT). Electroencephalography-based spectral and CFC analyses were conducted in an artifact-free subgroup of 10 participants. THI scores decreased significantly over the course of the intervention, whereas VAS-L and VAS-A showed no significant group-level changes. Cognitive performance improved across global cognition, processing speed, executive function, and working memory. Repeated-measures analyses demonstrated significant session effects for DST-F, DST-B, and SDMT. DST-B also showed a significant overall pre- to post-stimulation effect, whereas this effect was marginal for DST-F and absent for SDMT; no significant tACS × session interactions were observed. CFC analyses showed no significant pre- to post-stimulation changes after correction for multiple comparisons. Repeated individualized IAF-based phase-amplitude-coupled tACS was associated with reduced tinnitus-related functional impact and improvements in several cognitive measures, whereas subjective loudness and annoyance did not change significantly at the group level. No robust group-level CFC changes were detected. Given the single-arm design and absence of sham control, these findings are preliminary and do not establish treatment-specific or causal effects. Larger randomized sham-controlled studies are needed to determine efficacy and clarify underlying neurophysiological mechanisms.

papers.title: Age-dependent dissociation between sleep-disordered breathing severity and ventilatory impairment in children with Prader-Willi syndrome.
papers.abstract: Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) is highly prevalent in children with Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS), encompassing central, obstructive, and ventilatory abnormalities. However, its longitudinal evolution remains incompletely understood. We conducted a retrospective longitudinal study of children with genetically confirmed PWS who underwent serial respiratory polygraphy with concurrent transcutaneous carbon dioxide (TcCO₂) monitoring. Clinical characteristics, therapeutic interventions, and longitudinal respiratory parameters were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Twenty-nine children were included. SDB demonstrated an age-dependent pattern, with central respiratory abnormalities predominating in early childhood and obstructive events becoming more prominent during preschool and school age. In contrast, nocturnal ventilatory impairment was mainly observed in older children and adolescents. Clinical symptoms were independently associated with ENT intervention, whereas higher body mass index was associated with a greater likelihood of requiring non-invasive ventilation, supporting distinct obstructive and ventilatory phenotypes. Although unadjusted analyses suggested increasing TcCO₂ values with age, adjusted mixed-effects models indicated that this relationship was largely explained by obesity and treatment-related factors. SDB in children with PWS appears to represent an evolving continuum of central, obstructive, and ventilatory abnormalities. Conventional apnea indices alone may not adequately reflect ventilatory impairment, supporting longitudinal assessment of nocturnal gas exchange in addition to standard respiratory event indices.

papers.title: Temporal association between adjunctive repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation and seizure reduction in a pediatric patient with DNM1L-associated EMPF1: a case report.
papers.abstract: Encephalopathy, lethal, due to defective mitochondrial and peroxisomal fission 1 (EMPF1) is a rare, severe mitochondrial disorder characterized by acute-onset refractory seizures that rapidly progress to status epilepticus and are associated with a poor prognosis. Conventional therapies, including antiepileptic drugs and the ketogenic diet, exhibit limited efficacy. Although repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) has shown promise in other forms of drug-resistant epilepsy, its potential role in managing EMPF1 remains unexplored. A 7-year-old boy, previously healthy with normal development, presented with right-hand clonic movements and impaired consciousness, which progressed to status epilepticus. Brain MRI revealed diffuse cytotoxic edema involving the bilateral frontal, parietal, and temporal cortices, basal ganglia, and thalami. EEG recording showed generalized periodic spike-wave discharges with background slowing. Genetic testing identified a novel de novo DNM1L mutation (c.1949T > C, p.Leu650Pro), which was classified as likely pathogenic according to ACMG/AMP guidelines and provided strong support for the diagnosis of EMPF1. In addition to a regimen of antiepileptic drugs and a metabolic "cocktail," 1-Hz rTMS (90% of the resting motor threshold, 40 trains daily) was applied over the left primary motor cortex on Day 16. Following initiation of this combined therapy, seizure frequency was temporally associated with a marked reduction, decreasing from ∼20 to 5-6 episodes/day after one day, 2-3 by Day 27 (12 days after rTMS initiation), and 0-1 by Day 36 (21 days after rTMS initiation). Despite this reduction in clinical seizure burden, the patient developed progressive pneumonia leading to sepsis and acute heart failure, and died on Day 65 (hospital day 65). In this case, adjunctive rTMS applied alongside standard antiepileptic and metabolic "cocktail" therapy was temporally associated with a pronounced reduction in seizure frequency in a patient with DNM1L-associated EMPF1. This temporal association is hypothesis-generating and does not permit attribution of the observed seizure reduction to rTMS; further investigation in larger cohorts is warranted.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnea and selected comorbidities - a literature review of cohort studies.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is the most common type of sleep-related breathing disorder, characterized by repeated episodes of upper airway collapse and resulting hypoxia during sleep. Intermittent hypoxemia may exert a multisystemic impact and modulate the course of comorbidities. Pathophysiological mechanisms such as oxidative stress, inflammation, and endothelial dysfunction contribute to adverse health outcomes including cardiovascular disease, cerebrovascular complications, metabolic disorders, cancer, neurodegenerative conditions, or behavioral abnormalities. Treatment of OSA may mitigate progression of comorbidities and reduce the associated social and economic burden. This literature review aims to explore the relationships between OSA and selected comorbid diseases, including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), stroke, diabetes, cancer, and hypertension, based on cohort studies in the literature.

papers.title: Case Report: Value of MR relaxometry and spectroscopy in multimodal imaging characterization of limbic encephalitis in systemic sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Central nervous system involvement is uncommon in systemic sclerosis, and inflammatory temporomesial syndromes in this context are rarely reported. We present a 58-year-old man with systemic sclerosis who developed subacute cognitive impairment and dialeptic seizures arising from the right temporal lobe. Video electroencephalography confirmed a right temporal seizure onset zone. Brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated enlargement and subtle T2 hyperintensity of the right hippocampus and amygdala, while fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography/computed tomography images showed focal hypermetabolism of the enlarged right amygdala. Proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy demonstrated bilateral reduction of total N-acetylaspartate compared with an age-matched healthy reference subject, with a more pronounced difference on the right, a pattern compatible with bilateral, right-accentuated neuronal dysfunction or injury. MR relaxometry demonstrated significant bilateral T2 prolongation in the amygdalae and hippocampal heads, whereas T1 abnormalities were more region-dependent, involving the right amygdala and both hippocampal heads. Serum testing detected anti-pyruvate dehydrogenase antibodies, whereas routine clinical neural antibody testing was negative. The patient became seizure-free under antiseizure medication and immunosuppressive therapy with cyclophosphamide. Notably, although the unilateral conventional imaging findings did not meet the bilateral mesial temporal criterion required by current consensus criteria for definite autoimmune limbic encephalitis, MR relaxometry revealed bilateral temporomesial abnormalities. This finding is consistent with available neuropathological and experimental evidence and suggests that routine imaging may underestimate disease extent. This case highlights a rare presentation of antibody-atypical limbic encephalitis in the setting of systemic sclerosis and illustrates how multimodal imaging can support diagnosis and tissue characterization when routine antibody testing is unrevealing.

papers.title: Decoding user satisfaction during reading of pre-defined question-answer pairs: BCI approach using delta and gamma EEG.
papers.abstract: The rapid proliferation of large language models (LLMs) has intensified the need for robust evaluation frameworks to align artificial intelligence (AI) behavior with human expectations. While current reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) strategies heavily rely on explicit, post-hoc self-reports, these metrics are fundamentally limited by subjective biases and user non-compliance. To address this, the current study presents a novel brain-computer interface (BCI) framework that systematically characterizes the continuous, implicit neural correlates of user satisfaction and dissatisfaction during a reading-based evaluative task involving pre-validated LLM-generated question-answer pairs. Sixty-four-channel electroencephalography (EEG) data were recorded from 30 participants while they read and evaluated various LLM-generated responses. To capture genuine subjective experiences, individual trials were relabeled based on post-trial 5-point Likert scale ratings into five distinct evaluative states, and spatiotemporal spectral analyses were performed. A ShallowFBCSPNet architecture was further used to evaluate single-trial classification between the very satisfied and very dissatisfied conditions under a subject-mixed cross-validation scheme. Spatiotemporal spectral analyses revealed distinct neural oscillatory dynamics that temporally dissociate satisfaction and dissatisfaction. When reading highly satisfactory responses, a pronounced, sustained enhancement of low-frequency delta power was observed within the bilateral frontotemporal areas during the middle (4-8 s) and late (8-12 s) reading intervals, indexing high-order cognitive consolidation and reward processing. Conversely, processing highly dissatisfactory responses led to a localized suppression of high-frequency gamma power in the right frontotemporal region during the early interval (0-4 s), reflecting an immediate affective appraisal and expectation violation. Utilizing the ShallowFBCSPNet architecture, the system successfully discriminated between the "very satisfied" and "very dissatisfied" states, achieving an average accuracy of 81% under a subject-mixed cross-validation scheme. These findings demonstrate that user evaluative states are encoded via distinct frequency-specific cortical networks over differing temporal windows. By bridging cognitive neuroscience and artificial intelligence, this study establishes the conceptual and empirical foundation for passive BCI-driven implicit feedback channels, laying groundwork toward future real-time paradigms for next-generation LLM alignment; the classification result should be interpreted as a feasibility demonstration rather than an estimate of real-world decoding accuracy.

papers.title: Clinical characteristics and exploratory factors associated with in-hospital mortality in pediatric severe viral encephalitis.
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to describe the clinical characteristics of severe viral encephalitis (SVE) in children and to identify exploratory factors associated with in-hospital mortality, thereby providing preliminary evidence to facilitate early risk stratification and reduce SVE-related disability and mortality. A retrospective study was conducted in 75 children diagnosed with viral encephalitis at the Department of Pediatrics, Anqing Municipal Hospital, from January 2023 to December 2025, including 50 mild cases and 25 SVE cases. Demographic data, clinical manifestations, and laboratory parameters (peripheral white blood cell count (WBC), serum sodium, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) leukocyte and protein levels, serum neuron-specific enolase (NSE), electroencephalography (EEG), neuroimaging findings, and Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) scores) were collected and compared between groups. Pathogen detection was conducted through multiplex PCR and/or serum viral IgM antibody testing. In the mild encephalitis group, 14 out of 50 cases (28%) were found to be infected with specific viruses, with enteroviruses (EVs) being the predominant type, accounting for 7 cases, followed by herpes zoster virus (VZV) and human herpesvirus type 6 (HHV-6), each with 2 cases. In the SVE group, 9 out of 25 cases (36%) were found to have pathogens, with influenza A virus (4 cases) and herpes simplex virus (2 cases) being the main ones. Univariate analyses and Firth-penalized logistic regression were used to explore factors associated with in-hospital mortality (primary outcome) within the SVE subgroup. Among the 25 children with SVE (15 males, mean age 7.74 ± 2.2 years), fever (76%), signs of elevated intracranial pressure (68%), and seizures (56%) were common; four patients died (16%). Compared with children with mild encephalitis, the SVE group exhibited significantly longer hospital stays, higher seizure rates, lower GCS scores, higher proportions of abnormal EEG and neuroimaging abnormalities, and elevated serum NSE (all P < 0.05). However, there were no significant differences in CSF leukocytes, CSF protein, blood leukocytes, or serum sodium. In univariate Firth-corrected logistic regression, neuroimaging abnormalities (P = 0.007), seizures (P = 0.011), EEG abnormalities (P = 0.018), lower GCS score (per 1-point decrease, P < 0.001), and higher serum NSE (per 10 ng/mL increment, P = 0.018) were significantly associated with in-hospital mortality. Pediatric SVE presents with nonspecific early symptoms and substantial mortality. Seizures, EEG and neuroimaging abnormalities, low GCS score, and elevated serum NSE are exploratory factors associated with in-hospital mortality. However, given the small sample size and single-center design, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger multi-center prospective cohorts. Early recognition of these factors may aid in clinical risk assessment.

papers.title: Surgical Success in Obstructive Sleep Apnea Patients Using Preoperative Drug-Induced Sleep Endoscopy and Awake Endoscopy Considering Disease Severity.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a prevalent disorder characterized by recurrent episodes of airway obstruction during sleep, leading to fragmented sleep and oxygen desaturation. Identifying the precise site and pattern of obstruction is essential for surgical success. Awake endoscopy with Müller's maneuver (AEMM) has long been used, but drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) offers dynamic assessment under sleep-like conditions. To retrospectively compare surgical outcomes of OSA patients evaluated with DISE versus AEMM, stratified by disease severity, and to determine whether the comparative value of DISE over AEMM differs according to OSA severity as measured by AEMM (AHI). Records of 102 OSA patients undergoing sleep surgery between January 2022 and December 2024 at Hamad Medical Corporation were reviewed. Patients were grouped into AEMM-only (n = 54) and DISE (n = 48). Surgical success was defined as postoperative AHI < 15 events/hour and at least 50% reduction from baseline. Statistical analysis included independent and paired t-tests, chi-square tests, and the Johnson-Neyman procedure to identify AHI-based thresholds of DISE benefit. DISE group had higher surgical success compared to AEMM (62.5% vs. 40.7%, p = 0.114). Preoperative and postoperative AHI changes were significant in both groups (p < 0.001). Stratification revealed that moderate-to-severe OSA patients (AHI > 16.7) had significantly better outcomes when surgery was based on DISE (p < 0.001). In patients with mild OSA (AHI < 16.7), DISE conferred no additional benefit over AEMM. DISE-based surgical planning improves outcomes in moderate-to-severe OSA, while AEMM remains adequate for mild OSA cases. Disease severity should guide the choice of preoperative airway assessment method.
papers.journal: World journal of otorhinolaryngology - head and neck surgery

papers.title: Investigation of human defence responses in a virtual reality environment: an EEG study.
papers.abstract: A predatory imminence continuum displays the perceived imminence of threat to visualise the risk to the prey. Most human studies have utilised static paradigms that may lack ecological validity and limit the exploration of defensive behaviours. Therefore, the present study investigates Fight/ Flight defence responses and underlying neural correlates using EEG under varying conditions of threat proximity and escape availability using a virtual reality (VR) environment. The experiment consisted of a desktop VR environment, including training and experimental phases (5 conditions). Conditions 1 to 4, except 5, included a threat avatar. The conditions differed based on threat proximity (distal/ proximal) and participant's escapability (escape/no-escape). Twenty trials were presented, with each condition presented 4 times. Participants responded with a Fight/Flight response to the threat, followed by a 10-s rest scene and a 5-s fixation. A significant difference in reaction time was observed, indicating distinction based on threat proximity and escapability. A heightened Fight response was observed across all conditions. This pattern may reflect the absence of consequences associated with defensive actions compared to real-life scenarios. For the electrophysiological analysis, ERP analysis indicated a significant difference in the Late frontal activity at the F1 electrode across all conditions. This may suggest tentative cognitive processing during the period surrounding defensive response (Fight or Flight) selection and execution. Together, the findings indicate that although the lack of consequences may have promoted the Fight response more in the VR scenarios, the neural responses may have shown differences in cognitive processing.

papers.title: Changes in parent-rated attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder symptom scores and sleep parameters during individualized multidisciplinary clinical management in children with comorbid obstructive sleep apnea: a prospective cohort study in Vietnam.
papers.abstract: To describe changes in parent-rated attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptom scores, respiratory-polygraphy-derived parameters, and sleep characteristics over 6 months in children with ADHD and comorbid obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) who received individualized multidisciplinary clinical management. This single-arm prospective cohort study was conducted at Vietnam National Children's Hospital from November 2022 to October 2024. Among 629 children with ADHD screened using the Pediatric Sleep Questionnaire (PSQ), 293 had at least 8 positive responses and underwent home respiratory polygraphy; 147 had clinical features consistent with pediatric OSA and met the prespecified respiratory-polygraphy criterion of a respiratory event index (REI) ≥ 1 event/hour, and 141 completed follow-up. Parent-rated Vanderbilt ADHD Diagnostic Rating Scale (VADRS) scores were assessed at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months. Respiratory-polygraphy and sleep-diary measures were assessed at baseline and 6 months. The mean age was 7.8 years, and 85.8% were boys. After 6 months, mean REI decreased from 11.8 to 4.4 events/hour, and the lowest nocturnal peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂) increased from 78.9% to 83.4% (both p < 0.001). Prespecified respiratory-polygraphy severity categories shifted toward less severe categories (McNemar-Bowker χ 2[6] = 70.80, p < 0.001); 73 children (51.8%) improved by at least one category, and 47 children (33.3%; 95% CI, 26.1-41.5%) no longer met the prespecified respiratory-polygraphy criterion for OSA at 6 months. Sleep-onset latency and daytime sleep duration decreased. Nighttime sleep duration increased from 8.4 ± 1.1 to 8.7 ± 0.6 h (mean change, +0.3 h; 95% CI, +0.14 to +0.46; p < 0.001), whereas total 24-h sleep duration decreased by 0.5 h (p < 0.001). Parent-rated ADHD symptom scores decreased across all VADRS domains. Respiratory-polygraphy-derived indices, selected sleep characteristics, and parent-rated ADHD symptom scores improved during 6 months of individualized multidisciplinary clinical management. The uncontrolled design and concurrent interventions preclude causal attribution of these changes to OSA-directed treatment.

papers.title: Efficacy of acupuncture, Chinese herbal medicine, combined acupuncture-herbal therapy, and western medication for adult chronic insomnia: a network meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Chronic insomnia is a prevalent sleep disorder that significantly impairs quality of life and reduces patient confidence in treatment. Acupuncture, Chinese herbal medicine, and their combination have shown promise in the management of this condition. However, comparative research on these Chinese medicine modalities themselves and vs. Western medication remains scarce. PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database were comprehensively searched from database inception to June 1, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed the risk of bias in the eligible studies. Network meta-analysis was conducted using STATA 16 and R 4.5.3. Fifty-nine randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving 4 interventions were included. According to the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) analysis, for total efficacy (TE), acupuncture plus herbal medicine ranked the highest (92.0%), followed by acupuncture (74.7%), herbal medicine (33.1%), and Western medicine (0.2%). For Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), acupuncture ranked first (82.0%), followed by acupuncture plus herbal medicine (76.8%), herbal medicine (36.4%), and Western medicine (4.9%). For adverse events, where a higher SUCRA indicates fewer events, acupuncture ranked first (78.8%), followed by herbal medicine (76.0%), acupuncture plus herbal medicine (45.2%), and Western medicine (<0.1%). Combination therapy (acupuncture plus herbal medicine) showed the highest probability of being the most effective intervention for total efficacy based on SUCRA analysis, and significantly outperformed Western medication and herbal medicine alone. However, no significant difference was observed between combination therapy and acupuncture alone. Acupuncture alone ranked first for improving sleep quality (PSQI) and minimizing adverse events. Given the methodological limitations of the included studies, high-quality, rigorously designed RCTs are warranted to validate these findings. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD420261413406, Identifier CRD420261413406.

papers.title: Experimentally manipulating dream content by reactivating a remote emotional memory.
papers.abstract: Sleep and dreaming have long been hypothesized to serve a functional role in emotion regulation. Here, we investigated how reactivating highly emotional autobiographical memories prior to sleep affects dream content and subsequent emotional appraisal of these memories. Participants (N = 42) completed the Autobiographical Emotional Memory Task prior to bed for three consecutive nights, providing up to three verbal dream reports each night, with sleep monitored via wrist actigraphy. Consistent with emotion regulation theories of dreaming, we hypothesized that reactivating negative emotional memories before sleep would affect the content and emotion of dreams more than reactivating positive memories, and that participants who dreamed about negative memories would have greater overnight reductions in emotional reactivity toward them than those who did not. As hypothesized, the valence of reactivated memories strongly influenced participants' dream emotions. Contrary to our hypotheses, positive memories were descriptively more likely to be incorporated into dream content than negative memories, although this difference did not reach significance. Furthermore, overnight changes in emotional appraisal of memories were unrelated to dream emotion or content. These observations demonstrate that it is possible to experimentally manipulate dreaming by reactivating highly emotional autobiographical memories before sleep. However, we find no support for preferential incorporation of negative emotional experiences into dreams, and no evidence that dreaming about emotional memories is associated with overnight changes in reactivity toward them.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society

papers.title: Auditory paradigm-dependent EEG feature screening and representation for distinguishing consciousness states in male patients with disorders of consciousness.
papers.abstract: Accurate assessment of disorders of consciousness (DoC), including minimally conscious state (MCS) and unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS/VS), remains a major challenge in clinical neurorehabilitation. EEG-based biomarkers offer a non-invasive approach for characterizing residual brain activity, yet their discriminative sensitivity may depend on auditory stimulus design. EEG recordings were obtained from 15 male patients with DoC during four auditory stimulation paradigms. Nonlinear, spectral power, and graph-theoretic features were extracted, yielding 136 candidate features. All individual features were independently evaluated using patient-level leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) to characterize paradigm- and feature-domain-specific predictive performance. In a complementary exploratory optimization analysis, univariate statistical screening identified 26 features with nominal group differences (p < 0.05); these features were subsequently subjected to within-fold K-means clustering and principal component analysis (PCA), and compared with directly combined feature representations for MCS versus UWS/VS classification and CRS-R score regression. In the single-feature benchmark, the reversed-word sequence paradigm showed relatively higher averaged classification performance, while nonlinear features demonstrated comparatively stronger classification characteristics than spectral power and graph-theoretic features. In the optimization analysis, the PCA-derived representation achieved competitive classification performance, whereas the direct combination of all statistically screened features achieved the highest observed classification accuracy. Regression performance was generally limited. These findings suggest that auditory stimulus design and EEG feature representation may influence the discrimination of consciousness states in DoC. In this small-sample exploratory study, reversed-word auditory stimulation and nonlinear EEG features showed promising discriminative characteristics, while direct feature combination provided additional predictive information for categorical classification. Further validation in larger and independent cohorts is required.

papers.title: Clinical, polysomnographic, and psychological profiles across questionnaire-defined symptom groups in obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) has heterogeneous symptom presentations that are not fully captured by the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI). We aimed to identify demographic, polysomnographic, and psychological profiles across four questionnaire-defined symptom groups in OSA patients. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 789 treatment-naïve patients with OSA (AHI ≥5 events/h) who underwent overnight polysomnography and neuropsychological assessment between May 2021 and August 2025. Participants were classified into four symptom-groups: low symptom burden, poor sleep quality only, excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) only, and combined poor sleep quality and EDS, using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index and the Epworth Sleepiness Scale. Multinomial logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with these symptom-groups, with the low symptom burden group as the reference. Results showed that the poor sleep quality only symptom-group was most prevalent (49.0%), followed by the low symptom burden group (29.8%), the combined group (14.3%), and the EDS-only group (6.8%). Female sex, lower BMI, altered sleep continuity and sleep-stage distribution were associated with the poor sleep quality only group, whereas younger age, shorter sleep onset latency and a shorter maximum hypopnea duration were associated with the EDS-only group. Higher PHQ-9 and CFS scores were consistently associated with all three higher symptom-burden groups (all P < 0.001), with the largest effect estimates observed for the combined group. Higher GAD-7 scores were also associated with the poor sleep quality only and combined groups, whereas the association between GAD-7 score and the EDS-only group was less precise and only nominally significant. Several additional sleep-stage, stage- or position-specific respiratory, and limb-movement associations were nominal and should be considered hypothesis-generating. Several conventional hypoxemia measures, including TST90, mean oxygen desaturation, and mean nocturnal oxygen saturation, were not significantly associated with any symptom-group in the primary adjusted analyses. The overall pattern was generally similar in the sensitivity analyses, although several nominal associations were attenuated. Overall, questionnaire-defined OSA symptom groups differed in demographic, polysomnographic, and psychological characteristics that were not fully captured by AHI alone, supporting multidimensional clinical assessment while considering the need for independent validation.

papers.title: Case Report: Right frontal periventricular heterotopia underlying secondary network epilepsy with a Lennox-Gastaut phenotype: multimodal SEEG, CCEP, and rs-fMRI evidence.
papers.abstract: Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (LGS) is generally regarded as a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy involving distributed brain networks, although a focal structural abnormality may occasionally recruit bilateral cortical and thalamic circuits and produce an LGS phenotype. We characterized the spatiotemporal organization of such a network and its changes after focal SEEG-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RF-TC). A 50-year-old woman with drug-resistant epilepsy, multiple seizure types, diffuse slow spike-and-wave discharges, generalized paroxysmal fast activity, intellectual impairment, and right frontal periventricular heterotopia (PVH) underwent stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG). Cortico-cortical evoked potentials (CCEPs) were acquired before and after SEEG-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RF-TC). Resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI), obtained before and 3 months after RF-TC, was analyzed using three seeds: the entire right frontal PVH and the right and left centromedian thalamic nuclei (CM). SEEG identified the earliest sustained ictal activity within the sampled right frontal PVH-related medial contacts, accompanied by high-frequency activity. This was followed by ipsilateral lateral frontal recruitment, contralateral frontal synchronization, and subsequent bilateral CM involvement. Two-stage RF-TC of the onset and early-recruited networks was followed by seizure freedom through 9 months. After RF-TC, right-sided stimulation produced markedly attenuated lesion-related CCEP responses, whereas left-sided responses and responses between thalamic contacts showed little appreciable change. Descriptive rs-fMRI difference maps demonstrated decreased local frontal connectivity around the treated territory and increased long-range connectivity for the PVH seed; both CM seeds showed predominantly increased connectivity with distributed cortical and cerebellar regions. In this patient, a focal PVH-related epileptogenic network was associated with secondary bilateral cortical and thalamic recruitment underlying an LGS phenotype. CCEP and rs-fMRI captured complementary aspects of postoperative network change: attenuation of stimulation-evoked propagation and postoperative changes in intrinsic functional connectivity, respectively.

papers.title: Machine learning based multimodel prediction of poor wellbeing, generalized anxiety disorder, and insomnia among adults in Indian urban informal settlements: toward explainable digital mental health screening.
papers.abstract: Mental health morbidity among urban informal settlements-dwelling populations is shaped by a complex interplay of behavioural exposures including screen time, working hours, and sleep duration and sociodemographic vulnerability. We analyzed cross-sectional data from 1,600 adults recruited from 16 clusters within the urban informal settlement field practice area of a medical college's Urban Health Training Centre in Pune, India, to develop and compare ten supervised machine learning algorithms predicting poor wellbeing (WHO-5), moderate-to-severe generalized anxiety disorder (GAD-7), and moderate-to-severe insomnia (ISI); internal consistency of all three instruments was confirmed from item-level responses. Because participants were nested within 16 clusters, our primary analysis used leave-one-cluster-out (LOCO) cross-validation, in which each cluster was held out in turn as an independent test set; a conventional participant-level 80/20 split with 10-fold cross-validation was retained as a secondary analysis. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were assessed using AUC, sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, Brier score, decision curve analysis, and DeLong's test, each with cluster-level bootstrap 95% confidence intervals. SHAP was used to interpret the best-performing model, and feature-attribution concordance was additionally assessed across the Rashomon set of near-equivalent top models. The WHO-5, GAD-7, and ISI showed acceptable-to-excellent internal consistency in this sample (Cronbach's alpha 0.730-0.938; McDonald's omega 0.815-0.953).
