LightGBM achieved the highest primary (LOCO-CV) AUC for all three outcomes: 0.977 (95% CI 0.970-0.983) for poor wellbeing, 0.987 (95% CI 0.984-0.992) for GAD, and 0.988 (95% CI 0.982-0.993) for insomnia. Several sociodemographic predictors showed unusually strong univariate associations with the outcomes, traced to a repeating between-cluster pattern in the sampling frame; this structure means that even cluster-aware validation may remain optimistic relative to a genuinely external population, a limitation we discuss in detail. SHAP-based rankings were highly concordant (Spearman ρ = 0.84-0.95) across the three top-performing, statistically near-equivalent models. A class-weighting sensitivity analysis improved positive predictive value for poor wellbeing from 0.478 to 0.600 with minimal AUC cost. Gradient-boosted tree ensembles, particularly LightGBM, showed strong and internally consistent discrimination for these three outcomes, assessed using reliable instruments; however, given the between-cluster homogeneity identified in this sample, external validation in an independent population is essential before any claim of generalizable clinical utility.

papers.title: CLSP-REQA: a real-time quality-aware closed-loop seizure prediction framework with Mamba-BiLSTM and confidence-gated intervention.
papers.abstract: Reliable seizure prediction is a prerequisite for closed-loop neurostimulation therapy, yet existing methods rarely account for the variability in EEG signal quality encountered in real-world deployment, and the overwhelming majority adopt non-strict evaluation protocols that overestimate generalization performance. We propose CLSP-REQA (Closed-Loop Seizure Prediction with Real-time EEG Quality Assessment), a unified framework that embeds a lightweight signal quality estimator directly within the prediction pipeline. A Real-time EEG Quality Assessment (REQA) module runs in parallel with a Mamba-BiLSTM backbone, producing a scalar quality score q ∈ [0, 1] that modulates output confidence through a tiered non-linear fusion function (ECLO). We conducted dedicated experiments testing whether this learned score reflects genuine signal quality rather than a redundant proxy for the prediction task, and a sensitivity analysis of the fusion thresholds against standard calibration baselines. The framework was evaluated under strict cross-patient evaluation on the CHB-MIT Scalp EEG Database (n = 23 subjects, 198 seizures) and the SIENA Scalp EEG Database (n = 14 subjects, 47 seizures). On CHB-MIT, CLSP-REQA achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.7426 ± 0.0199, exceeding the unadapted cross-patient baseline of 0.69 reported by Jemal et al., using only 16 EEG channels compared to 23 in prior work, and without requiring any target-patient data or domain adaptation. On SIENA, CLSP-REQA achieved an AUC of 0.7012 ± 0.0249, exceeding the best domain-adapted cross-patient result of 0.61 on the same dataset under a strictly harder information constraint, since domain adaptation methods are given access to unlabelled target-patient data that CLSP-REQA does not use. The framework outputs a structured four-tuple 〈p, q, c, ΦSHAP〉 designed for compatibility with closed-loop neurostimulator interfaces. As both evaluation datasets are retrospective recordings from controlled hospital settings, we report this study as a feasibility demonstration rather than evidence of prospective, real-world clinical readiness, and the comparison with domain adaptation should not be read as unconditional superiority.

papers.title: Uncovering the mortality burden of lung cancer with documented sleep apnea in the United States: a 22-year population-based study.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and sleep apnea may identify a clinically vulnerable subgroup of patients with lung cancer. However, population-level mortality patterns involving lung cancer with documented sleep apnea remain unclear. This study examined long-term trends, disparities, geographic variation, socioeconomic patterns, and future projections of related mortality in the United States. We conducted a retrospective population-based analysis using CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death data from 1999 to 2020. Deaths were included when lung cancer was recorded as the underlying cause of death and sleep apnea as a contributing cause. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were calculated per 100,000 population. Temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression, historical AAMRs were projected with ARIMA models, out-of-sample performance was evaluated against final 2021-2024 CDC WONDER data, and state-level Sociodemographic Index and frontier analyses were performed. A total of 4,339 deaths involving lung cancer with documented sleep apnea were identified. The overall AAMR was 0.05 per 100,000 population. Mortality was concentrated predominantly among adults aged 65 years and older and was higher among men, White and non-Hispanic individuals, residents of nonmetropolitan areas, and those living in the Midwest and West. The AAMR increased from 0.011 in 1999 to 0.112 in 2020, with a significant annual percent change of 9.398%. The ARIMA model projected an increase to 0.160 per 100,000 by 2030, but it consistently overestimated observed AAMRs during 2021-2024 (MAPE 9.71%); therefore, these forecasts were interpreted as conditional and exploratory projections. State-level analyses showed marked geographic heterogeneity not fully explained by socioeconomic development. Mortality involving lung cancer and documented sleep apnea increased substantially over 22 years and showed clear demographic and geographic disparities, with a disproportionate burden among older adults, particularly those aged 65 years and above. The historical trend and exploratory forecasting results support continued attention to sleep health assessment and integrated respiratory-oncology care.

papers.title: Resting-state cortical alpha frequency in Parkinson's disease and multiple system atrophy: associations with diagnosis, age, and symptom burden.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) and multiple system atrophy (MSA) are clinically overlapping neurodegenerative disorders that present with a complex, heterogeneous burden of motor and non-motor symptoms. Resting-state EEG reveals that cortical alpha slowing is a hallmark of pathological aging, yet its specific presence and clinical significance in these distinct synucleinopathies remain incompletely understood. Therefore, precisely quantifying the individual alpha frequency serves as a critical, non-invasive approach to characterize cortical network dysfunction across synucleinopathies and evaluate how aging moderates its association with clinical symptom burden. We analyzed source-reconstructed resting-state EEG data from 104 participants, comprising patients with PD, patients with the parkinsonian (MSA-P) and cerebellar subtypes (MSA-C) of MSA, and healthy controls. To accurately capture oscillatory dynamics, a data-driven masking empirical mode decomposition approach was applied to extract the individual alpha frequency across canonical cortical networks. General linear models tested diagnostic group differences, age-related effects, and age-dependent associations between individual alpha frequency and clinical symptom scores. Relative to healthy controls, both PD and MSA-C exhibited significant lower cortical IAF, whereas MSA-P showed no significant global IAF difference. At the network level, significant reduction of IAF was detected in the visual and dorsal attention networks in both PD and MSA-C. Advancing age independently contributed to alpha slowing across all participants without accelerating the disease-related trajectories. Notably, chronological age significantly moderated the relationship between alpha slowing and non-motor symptoms. In older patients, reduced individual alpha frequency was strongly associated with a higher burden of overall non-motor, autonomic, and psychiatric/cognitive symptoms, a relationship not observed in younger patients or with motor symptom severity. Cortical alpha slowing was detected in PD and MSA-C, but not in MSA-P. Age independently contributes to alpha slowing and strengthens its association with non-motor symptom burden, supporting age-aware interpretation of resting-state electroencephalography biomarkers in synucleinopathies.

papers.title: TXN/TXNIP signatures point to plasma cells as a potential immune hub in periodontitis based on integrated transcriptomic analysis and preliminary experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis (PD) is a prevalent chronic inflammatory disease characterized by periodontal tissue destruction and alveolar bone loss. The contribution of cellular senescence- and circadian rhythm-related genes to PD progression remains incompletely defined, limiting biomarker discovery and precision therapeutic development. Publicly available PD bulk transcriptomic data, single-cell RNA-seq data, and gene sets associated with cellular senescence and circadian rhythms were integrated. Differential expression analysis (|log2FC| > 0.5, P < 0.05) and machine-learning strategies were used to identify key genes and establish a diagnostic model. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, cell-cell communication, pseudotime trajectory, and drug prediction analyses were subsequently performed to characterize the biological roles and cellular specificity of these genes. Animal experiments were performed to validate the expression and cellular localization of the key genes in periodontal tissues via histologic and immunofluorescence analyses (ethics approval: No. PZW2024031). TXN and TXNIP were identified as key genes. The diagnostic model based on these genes showed strong discrimination in both the training and validation sets (area under the curve > 0.7). Pathway analysis revealed that both genes were associated with antigen processing and presentation as well as with apoptosis. TXN was inversely related to activated B cells, whereas TXNIP was positively associated with immature B cells. Single-cell analysis revealed plasma cells as the principal cell subset. In PD, plasma cells changed from an immunologically isolated population to an interactive regulatory hub, communicating broadly with other cell types through the MIF signaling axis and displaying prominent functional heterogeneity and pseudotime-dependent differences. TXN and TXNIP may serve as candidate molecular tools for PD classification. The association of plasma cells with immune regulation highlights a potential mechanistic link between oxidative stress and immune remodeling in PD, warranting further investigation.

papers.title: Increased visual reliance for postural control in multiple sclerosis: preliminary evidence from task-related cortical desynchronization.
papers.abstract: Balance impairment is one of the most disabling symptoms in multiple sclerosis (MS), yet the underlying cortical mechanisms remain poorly understood. This exploratory study investigated how postural demands modulate brain activity in MS. Seven individuals with MS (mean age: 51.1 ± 9.7 years; 5 women; median Expanded Disability Status Scale: 5.5, IQR: 4.5-6.0) and seven age- and sex-matched healthy controls (mean age: 51.0 ± 9.6 years) performed three static balance tasks on a force plate: quiet stance with eyes open, quiet stance with eyes closed, and narrow stance with eyes open. Electroencephalography (EEG) and center of pressure (COP) were simultaneously recorded. Group differences were assessed using Linear Mixed Models. Significant effects are reported with false discovery rate (FDR)-corrected q-values, and otherwise with uncorrected p-values. MS patients demonstrated greater postural sway than healthy controls, with FDR-corrected group × condition interactions across COP parameters (semi-partial R 2 = 0.225-0.441; all q < 0.05), most pronounced during eyes closed (semi-partial R 2 = 0.124-0.282; all p < 0.05). Resting-state EEG revealed no consistent group differences except for an uncorrected elevation of occipital theta power in MS patients (p = 0.017; r = -0.76). During stance, uncorrected group × condition interactions indicated that MS patients exhibited a greater task-induced decrease of theta, alpha, and beta power relative to their matched resting baseline compared to healthy controls (semi-partial R 2 = 0.193-0.318; all p < 0.05). These effects were specific to the eyes-closed condition. These preliminary findings are consistent with an increased reliance on visual information for postural control in MS, accompanied by a task-related cortical desynchronization specifically upon visual deprivation. The observed effect sizes, while likely subject to inflation given the small sample size, suggest that oscillatory EEG parameters warrant investigation in larger confirmatory studies.

papers.title: Operationalizing Iterative RE-AIM in two pragmatic nursing home trials to support an adaptation learning cycle.
papers.abstract: Complex, heterogeneous settings such as nursing homes require ongoing adaptation of interventions and implementation strategies. Iterative RE-AIM offers a structured approach to guide adaptations, but how the approach is operationalized may need to vary across implementation contexts. We describe how two pragmatic nursing home trials operationalized Iterative RE-AIM with FRAME-IS to enable a systematic adaptation learning cycle. We conducted a narrative analysis of two ongoing multi-site trials: TEAM EFFORT (focused on falls reduction in State Veterans Homes) and 40 WINKS (focused on sleep improvement in nursing home residents with dementia). Both used RE-AIM for evaluation and FRAME-IS to document adaptations. Each operationalized the Iterative RE-AIM steps based on study scope, resources, team structure, and implementation timing, with a primary focus on refining a coach-supported implementation strategy. TEAM EFFORT embedded adaptation-related data collection, deliberation, and decision-making within weekly team meetings, supported by an ongoing input tool; 40 WINKS used individual-level surveys followed by structured, once-per-wave team gatherings to decide on adaptations. These two operationalizations illustrate how the timing, methods, and cadence of an adaptation learning cycle based on Iterative RE-AIM can vary in response to implementation context. Iterative RE-AIM can be operationalized differently across implementation contexts while remaining faithful to its underlying intent. Paired with FRAME-IS, Iterative RE-AIM can enable an adaptation learning cycle that integrates systematic documentation of adaptations with structured team deliberation. Rather than prescribing a single Iterative RE-AIM implementation protocol, these findings suggest that operationalization can respond to the context in which implementation occurs.

papers.title: Association of Taiyin personality traits with sleep quality among college students: parallel indirect effects through resilience and rumination.
papers.abstract: To investigate the relationships and pathways among Taiyin personality trait, resilience, rumination, and sleep status in a college student population. Using a cluster sampling method, 500 undergraduate students from a general higher education institution were selected as participants. They were surveyed using the Five-Pattern Personality Inventory (Taiyin Personality Subscale), the Rumination Response Scale, the Chinese Revised Version of the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale, and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (Chinese Revised Version). (1) The anal revealed a significant positive correlation between Taiyin personality and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index score (r = 0.405, p < 0.01), and this personality trait positively predicted sleep quality (β = 0.130, p < 0.01). Individual scores on the Taiyin personality trait showed a positive correlation with Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores, indicating that higher scores on this personality trait were associated with poorer sleep quality. (2) After controlling for all demographic variables, the Bootstrap test results confirmed that resilience played a partial mediating role between the Taiyin personality trait and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index score. The mediation effect size was 0.0345 (95% CI: 0.015 to 0.054), accounting for 26.46% of the total effect. Rumination also served as a partial mediator between the Taiyin personality trait and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index score, with a mediation effect size of 0.0567 (95% CI: 0.036 to 0.081), contributing 43.48% of the total effect. The Taiyin personality trait is directly correlated with the sleep status of college students and also indirectly influence sleep quality through the two pathways of resilience and rumination.

papers.title: Short sleep duration and incident self-reported severe periodontitis among Japanese adults: a nationwide prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory condition influenced by behavioral, systemic and socioeconomic factors, and its prevalence increases with age. Although cross-sectional studies suggest an association between short sleep duration and periodontitis, longitudinal evidence remains limited. This study aimed to examine the association between sleep duration and self-reported incident severe periodontitis using data from a nationwide prospective cohort. We conducted a prospective cohort study using longitudinal data from the 2023-2025 waves of the Japan COVID-19 and Society Internet Survey. Participants without self-reported severe periodontitis at baseline were followed for self-reported incident severe periodontitis. Short sleep duration was defined as <6 h per night. Cox proportional hazards models were used as the primary analysis, and generalized estimating equations were used as a secondary analysis. Among 33,000 respondents to the 2023 survey, 8,144 individuals without self-reported severe periodontitis at baseline and with follow-up data were included in the study population. Short sleep duration was reported by 22.7% of participants and was associated with a higher risk of self-reported incident severe periodontitis (hazard ratio = 1.28, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.13-1.46). This association was consistent in the secondary analysis using repeated measures (odds ratio = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.09-1.46). Older age, lower income, diabetes, dyslipidaemia, depression and smoking were also associated with an increased risk. Short sleep duration may be a modifiable risk factor for self-reported incident severe periodontitis in the general population. The present findings highlight the potential importance of sleep for the prevention of periodontitis.

papers.title: Electroencephalography-based Alzheimer's disease detection using multi-scale information retention transform: a subject-level comparison of machine learning classifiers.
papers.abstract: This exploratory study evaluates Multi-Scale Information Retention Transform (MSIRT), a feature-fusion framework for electroencephalography (EEG)-based Alzheimer's disease (AD) classification. Ratios between differential entropies were removed, and all EEG amplitudes were converted to volts before feature extraction because the transform is not invariant to arbitrary physical units. Revised MSIRT combines fuzzy entropy (FE), permutation entropy (PE), and differential entropy (DE) using training-fold normalization and cross-feature products. The framework was evaluated on OpenNeuro ds004504 (29 healthy controls and 36 participants with AD) using participant-level cross-validation. With Random Forest (RF) held fixed, direct concatenation achieved 84.62% accuracy and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.8956, whereas revised MSIRT achieved 86.15% accuracy and an AUC of 0.9004. An interaction-only control achieved 80.00% accuracy and an AUC of 0.8908. Because the no-product transform is feature-wise strictly monotonic, it was treated as an RF invariance control rather than a source of new predictive information. The paired AUC difference between revised MSIRT and concatenation was 0.0048 (bootstrap 95% confidence interval, -0.0067 to 0.0192; paired permutation p = 0.3780). In 20 sex-balanced resamples, revised MSIRT had a mean AUC of 0.8846. These results do not establish statistical superiority or clinical utility.

papers.title: Associations between sleep quality and well-being among nurses: the serial mediating roles of psychological resilience and adversity coping.
papers.abstract: Promoting nurses' well-being is important for mental health and workforce stability. Poor sleep quality is common among nurses and has been associated with lower general well-being. Psychological resilience and adversity quotient may serve as protective personal resources, but their roles in this association remain unclear. This study examined the association between sleep quality and general well-being among Chinese nurses from the perspective of conservation of resources theory, focusing on the independent and serial mediation of psychological resilience and adversity quotient. This multicenter cross-sectional study enrolled 1,149 nurses from 22 tertiary medical institutions in Zhejiang Province, China, between September and November 2025. Data were collected using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, the Adversity Quotient Scale, the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale, and the General Well-being Schedule. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, and common method bias tests were conducted for the study variables. Confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling were used to evaluate the measurement and hypothesized structural models, respectively. Indirect effects were tested using bias-corrected bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples. Sleep quality, psychological resilience, adversity quotient, and general well-being were all significantly correlated (P < 0.001). Psychological resilience and adversity quotient significantly mediated the association between sleep quality and general well-being. The total indirect effect accounted for 41.6% of the total effect. All three indirect effects were significant: (1) sleep quality → psychological resilience → general well-being (β = -0.137, P < 0.001, 22.2% of the total effect), (2) sleep quality → adversity quotient → general well-being (β = -0.070, P < 0.001, 11.2% of the total effect), and (3) sleep quality → psychological resilience → adversity quotient → general well-being (β = -0.051, P < 0.001, 8.2% of the total effect). Sleep quality was associated with Chinese nurses' well-being both directly and indirectly through psychological resilience, adversity quotient, and their serial mediation effect. Nursing managers may consider sleep quality improvement and targeted strategies to strengthen psychological resilience and adversity quotient as potential approaches to supporting nurses' general well-being.

papers.title: Ergothioneine Mediated Neuroprotective Effects in the Nervous System.
papers.abstract: Ergothioneine (EGT), a micromolecular derivative of histidine containing sulfur, is found in various organisms, including humans. It demonstrates antioxidant properties, reduces inflammation, and potentially possesses antiaging effects for neurodegenerative conditions, positioning EGT as a potential candidate for health enhancement and healthy aging. EGT appears to offer strong protective properties at the cellular level and shows decreased concentration levels in blood plasma in different neurological conditions such as cognitive impairment, Parkinson's disease, macular degeneration, and other neurodegenerative diseases. Further, emerging evidence from both preclinical and currently limited clinical studies indicates EGT's therapeutic potential for neurological disorders. For instance, EGT treatment slowed the progression of age-related hearing loss and alleviated the cisplatin-induced hearing loss in mouse models, especially in male mice. Similarly, EGT intervention in older adults (aged 60 years or older) has shown some effectiveness in improving cognitive ability, memory, and sleep quality. In this review, we present a thorough examination of its function in neuroprotection, particularly within the nervous system and explore its potential intracellular targeting pathways and their underlying mechanisms.
